cars.description: The Abarth 124 Spider is a two-door, rear-wheel-drive convertible featuring a manual fabric soft-top roof and a low-slung, balanced stance with a classic long-bonnet proportion. It is distinguished by an aggressive front fascia with a wide lower grille intake, sharp horizontal projector headlights, and a flat sculpted bonnet carrying twin power bulges. The rear showcases wraparound angular tail lights, an integrated lip spoiler, and a prominent quad-tip chrome exhaust system. It rides on 17-inch Gun Metal alloy wheels and features matching dark metallic grey exterior mirror caps and trim accents.

The Abarth 500e is a compact 3-door hatchback featuring stubby, aggressive proportions with a wide stance and short overhangs. It sports distinctive LED 'Infinity' headlights flanking a smooth, body-coloured front panel bearing bold lettering, alongside a deep front bumper layout. The rear is accented by signature LED tail lights and a sporty roof spoiler, while the side profile is defined by large 18-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels and specific Abarth branding.

The Abarth 595 Series 4 hatchback features a compact, aggressive three-door stance with a stubby silhouette and a distinctively sculpted front bumper integrating a large honeycomb cooling grille. It is fitted with poly-elliptical headlights, body-colored or contrasting door mirrors, and prominent side skirts. The rear end incorporates oval or quad exhaust outlets depending on the variant, a roof spoiler, and updated lighting clusters with body-colored center inserts, sitting on 17-inch multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Abarth 695 Series 4 hatchback is a compact, three-door performance vehicle featuring a stubby, rounded silhouette with short overhangs. Its front end is defined by a deep bumper, a prominent lower grille mesh, and circular multi-element headlights flanked by separate indicator pods on the upper wings. At the rear, it features rectangular tail lights with body-colored centers, a roof spoiler, and quad exhaust tips arranged vertically. It rides on 17-inch alloy wheels and sports contrasting 'Tar Cold Grey' exterior trim highlights on the door handles, mirror caps, and bumper moldings.

The Alfa Romeo 4C coupe features a compact, ultra-low two-door sports car body with voluptuous, muscular proportions and a carbon-fibre monocoque structure. The front fascia is dominated by a triangular 'trilobo' grille and swept-back headlamps, complemented by large cooling side air intakes on the swelling rear fenders. At the rear, it has circular LED tail lights inset into rounded corners above dual exhaust outlets. It rides on staggered-diameter alloy wheels (17-inch front and 18-inch rear) that accentuate its aggressive, low-slung stance.

The Alfa Romeo 4C Spider is a compact, mid-engine two-door convertible featuring a removable fabric targa roof panel and exposed carbon-fibre A-pillars. Its ultra-low stance is defined by heavily sculpted side air intakes, rounded rear haunches, and circular LED tail lights. The front end displays the brand's signature 'Trilobo' shield grille flanked by sweeping headlamp clusters, while the rear decklid incorporates triple heat-extractor vents above dual exhaust tips. It rides on staggered lightweight alloy wheels (17-inch front and 18-inch rear).

The Alfa Romeo Giulia (Type 952) is a four-door luxury sports sedan featuring an athletic profile, a cab-rearward stance, and smooth, curvaceous body lines. At the front, it is defined by the iconic offset triangular "Scudetto" V-shield grille and sharp, horizontal headlamps updated with adaptive matrix LED technology. The rear features wraparound, horizontal tail lights with distinctive internal graphics, sitting above integrated exhaust outlets. Depending on the variant, it rides on multi-spoke alloy wheels—such as classic 19-inch 5-hole designs—and showcases a clean roofline without dramatic external overhangs.

The Alfa Romeo Giulietta hatchback features an athletic five-door body with hidden rear door handles near the windows to mimic a coupe silhouette. Its front end is defined by a triangular inverted-shield grille floating within the bumper and swept-back teardrop headlights with LED daytime running lights. The side profile showcases clean, curving shoulder lines and a low-slung stance riding on alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches. At the rear, it is equipped with circular LED tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and a sporty bumper housing integrated exhaust tips.

The Alfa Romeo Junior is a compact five-door SUV featuring heavily sculpted bodywork with muscular haunches and hidden rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars. It showcases a bold 'Leggenda' or 'Scudetto' shield grille up front flanked by sharp, adaptive LED matrix headlights with a distinct three-element signature. The rear adopts a sloping 'coda tronca' (truncated tail) design fitted with wraparound LED tail lights and a contrasting two-tone black roof. It rides on prominent diamond-cut alloy wheels (such as 18-inch 'Petali' or 'Fori' patterns) and features subtle heritage details like the Biscione serpent emblem etched into the C-pillar.

The Alfa Romeo MiTo is a compact 3-door hatchback featuring rounded proportions, frameless door glass, and a distinctive sweeping beltline. It is dominated by a signature triangular shield grille flanked by prominent, circular bug-eye headlights with metallic bezels. The rear showcases rounded LED tail lights nested within curvaceous haunches, complemented by alloy wheel options and a subtle roof spoiler.

The Alfa Romeo Stelvio (Type 949) is a five-door medium luxury SUV featuring athletic, flowing proportions and a coupe-like roofline. Up front, it showcases the iconic triangular 'Trilobo' grille flanked by sweeping headlights, which were updated for the 2023 model year to distinctive '3+3' matrix LED units. The rear end features wrap-around LED tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and twin exhaust outlets. The exterior profile is characterized by a high beltline, body-coloured or gloss-black wheel arches depending on the variant, and large alloy wheel options.

The Alfa Romeo Tonale is a compact premium SUV featuring a distinctive triangular 'Trilobo' shield grille and sleek '3+3' full LED matrix headlights. Its profile includes fluid shoulder lines, hidden rear door handles flush with the C-pillars, and available two-tone black roof treatments above large 19-inch to 20-inch alloy wheels. The rear is defined by a wraparound LED light strip styled with a continuous signature loop echoing the front headlight motif.

The Aston Martin DB11 coupe features a classic low-slung grand tourer body style with two swan doors. Its exterior is defined by a prominent front-hinged clamshell bonnet, a distinctively sculpted front grille, and slim LED headlights. A key visual signature includes the continuous roof strakes flowing from the A-pillar to the C-pillar, alongside C-pillar hidden air intakes for the 'Aeroblade' system. The rear showcases thin, wraparound LED light-blade tail lights above an integrated diffuser.

The Aston Martin DB11 Volante is a two-door convertible featuring fluid grand tourer proportions with a clamshell aluminium hood and distinctive 'Curlicue' side vents. It is styled with a wide front grille, slim LED headlights, and a tailored multi-layer fabric soft top. The rear end incorporates ultra-slim C-shaped 'light blade' LED tail lights and dual oval exhaust outlets. It rides on forged alloy wheels, complemented by clean waistline body creases and unique wood or carbon-fibre seat-back veneers.

The Aston Martin DB12 coupe features a traditional two-door grand tourer silhouette with a low-slung stance, muscular rear haunches, and frameless swan-wing doors. The front end is dominated by a significantly larger, more upright metal vaned grille flanked by distinctive LED headlights with a multi-element daytime running light signature. At the rear, it employs slim 'light blade' tail lamps and an active deployable spoiler system integrated with an Aeroblade. The car rides on 21-inch alloy wheels and showcases athletic side strakes along the front guards.

The Aston Martin DB12 Volante is a 2-door convertible featuring a multi-layered fabric K-fold roof and muscular, wide-body proportions with a wider track than its predecessor. It is characterized by a prominent, enlarged vaned front grille, swept-back LED headlights with a distinct daytime running light signature, and sleek LED light-blade tail lights. The exterior is accented by swan-wing doors, side strakes on the front fenders, and large 21-inch alloy wheels.

The Aston Martin DBS Superleggera coupe features a muscular 2-door grand tourer body style with swan doors and an aggressive low-slung stance. It is characterized by a massive, honeycomb mesh front grille, sleek horizontal LED headlamps, and a sculpted carbon-fibre clamshell bonnet with distinct ventilation louvres. The rear profile showcases slim, continuous LED tail lights connected across the boot lid, sitting above a pronounced aerodynamic double diffuser and quad exhaust outlets. It rides on large 21-inch alloy wheels and features a sweeping fastback roofline that integrates active aerodynamic elements like the Aeroblade system.

The Aston Martin DBS Superleggera Volante features a low-slung, two-door convertible body with classic grand tourer proportions, characterized by an elongated clamshell bonnet and muscular rear haunches. Up front, it showcases a massive, hexagonal black grille flanked by sleek, swept-back LED headlights and a pronounced carbon-fibre front splitter. The rear is defined by ultra-slim, continuous LED tail lights that wrap across the tail, sitting above an aggressive quad-exhaust setup and a functional double diffuser. It rides on 21-inch alloy wheels and utilizes a multi-layer fabric soft top that folds flush into the rear deck.

The Aston Martin DBX features a muscular five-door luxury SUV body style with a sculpted clamshell bonnet and frameless 'swan-wing' doors. Up front, it showcases a signature large metal grille flanked by sleek, swept-back LED headlights and a low-slung stance. The rear profile is characterized by a distinctive, ducktail-style spoiler inspired by the Vantage, paired with a full-width LED light bar. It rides on large alloy wheels, up to 23 inches in size, beneath heavily flared wheel arches, and features a standard panoramic glass sunroof.

The Aston Martin Rapide S features a low-slung, four-door fastback sedan body style with distinctive swan-wing doors and no visible exterior B-pillars. It is characterised by an assertive, full-face polished aluminium grille, elongated sweeping hood, and elongated rear haunches finished with a pronounced duck-tail boot lid spoiler. The stance is anchored by 20-inch multi-spoke alloy wheels and complemented by slim, wraparound LED tail lights spanning the rear.

The Aston Martin V12 Vantage S coupe features a compact, low-slung two-door body with athletic proportions, highlighted by a muscular rear stance and side strakes. Up front, it showcases a distinctive carbon-fibre grille with vertical spars flanked by swept-back headlights with dark bezels and a vented bonnet. The rear incorporates an upswept boot-lid spoiler and clear-lens tail lights bridged by a dark trim panel, sitting above quad exhaust pipes and a carbon-fibre diffuser. It rides on 19-inch lightweight forged alloy wheels and can be distinguished by available contrast roof panels and exterior carbon-fibre packages.

The Gen 1 Aston Martin V8 Vantage coupe features a compact two-door fastback body style with a long clamshell bonnet, a low-slung stance, and prominent rear haunches. It is characterized by an iconic bright mesh eggcrate grille flanked by swept-back teardrop headlights, and distinctive side strakes integrated into the front guards. The rear showcases horizontal, V-shaped LED tail lights and dual round exhaust tips exiting through the lower bumper. It rides on alloy wheels with minimal front and rear overhangs, and features a practical rear tailgate providing access to a luggage shelf.

The first-generation Aston Martin V8 Vantage Roadster is a two-door convertible featuring a low-slung, athletic stance with classic long-hood, short-deck proportions and a power-operated fabric soft top. It is characterized by an iconic low-mounted mesh grille, swept-back projector headlights, and distinctive side strakes positioned behind the front wheels. The rear features pronounced, muscular haunches housing horizontal LED tail lights, complemented by dual exhaust tips integrated into the lower bumper.

The second-generation Aston Martin Vanquish coupe features a sleek, aerodynamic carbon-fibre body with classic grand tourer proportions, characterized by a long sculpted hood and a low roofline. It showcases a traditional wide grille flanked by elongated, swept-back headlights with integrated LED accents, alongside deep side strakes running from the front guards back toward the doors. The rear profile is defined by an integrated 'aero-duct' spoiler on the boot lid and distinctive boomerang-shaped LED tail lights inspired by the One-77. It sits on 20-inch alloy wheels, complemented by exposed carbon-fibre side skirts and a rear diffuser.

The third-generation Aston Martin Vanquish coupe features a striking two-door fastback body crafted entirely from carbon fibre, sporting an elongated bonnet and an extended wheelbase that visually emphasize its front-engine, rear-drive proportions. The aggressive front end is dominated by a massive, concave mesh grille flanked by matrix LED headlights and thermal cooling louvres on the muscular front guards. At the rear, it features a distinctive Kamm tail housing a customizable central shield element, razor-sharp LED light blade tail lights, a wide diffuser, and quad exhaust outlets. The stance is completed by 21-inch forged alloy wheels and an optional panoramic glass roof.

The Aston Martin Vanquish Volante features a sleek two-door convertible body with a powered fabric soft-top roof and classical long-bonnet, short-rear-deck proportions built on a carbon-fibre structure. Its low front fascia is dominated by a signature metal grille flanked by elongated, swept-back bi-xenon headlights with integrated LED daytime running lights. The rear profile showcases distinctive C-shaped LED tail lights connected by a slim light strip, framed by muscular haunches and dual exhaust outlets integrated into a carbon-fibre diffuser.

The second-generation Aston Martin Vantage coupe features a two-door fastback body style with an aggressive, low-slung stance, a clamshell bonnet, and distinctive side strakes. At the front, it showcases a prominent low-mounted mesh grille flanked by sleek, swept-back LED headlights. The rear is dominated by a signature slim, full-width continuous LED light strip above a pronounced diffuser and dual exhaust tips. It rides on large alloy wheels and features a sweeping roofline flowing into an integrated ducktail spoiler.

The third-generation Aston Martin Vantage coupe features an aggressive two-door stance with a low-slung, muscular silhouette and an extended, muscular rear haunch profile. It showcases a massive, low-mounted rectangular matrix grille flanked by wide, swept-back LED matrix headlamps. The rear end is defined by a slender, full-width LED light strip running across the trunk lid above a prominent diffuser and quad exhaust outlets. It rides on large 21-inch alloy wheels and utilizes signature swan-wing opening frameless doors.

The Aston Martin Vantage Roadster features a two-door convertible body style with an automated fabric Z-fold soft top. Its aggressive front end is defined by a low-mounted, wide-vane mesh grille flanked by sleek, angular matrix LED headlights. The low-slung stance showcases sculpted side strakes, flush-fitting door handles, and muscular rear haunches that flow into a full-width linear LED tail light strip above a pronounced rear diffuser.

The first-generation Audi A1 (8X) hatchback features a compact, aggressive stance characterized by a prominent single-frame grille and angular headlights with distinctive LED daytime running lights. It is available in both 3-door and 5-door (Sportback) body styles, distinguished by an arching roofline that can feature contrasting-color roof arches. The rear profile is defined by wraparound tailgate light clusters and a subtle roof spoiler. Alloy wheel options range across various multi-spoke and sporty designs, complemented by short overhangs and taut surface proportions.

The second-generation Audi A1 Sportback features a compact five-door hatchback body style with sharp, angular proportions and a wide stance. The front is defined by a low, broad Singleframe grille flanked by angular LED headlights with distinctive segmented daytime running graphics. In profile, it showcases a steeply raked C-pillar inspired by classic rally models and is often styled with a contrasting roof arch. The rear incorporates geometric LED tail lights and alloy wheel options ranging up to 18 inches.

The Audi A3 sedan (8V) features a compact four-door three-box silhouette characterized by a long bonnet, high waistline, and short rear deck. It is defined by a prominent single-frame hexagonal grille flanked by angular headlights—which feature distinct lower kinks following the 2016 facelift—and clean, sharp tornado lines running along the flanks. The rear exhibits horizontal LED tail lights and a subtle integrated bootlid lip. It typically rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches, with many models equipped with a sporty S line body kit.

The Audi A3 sedan (8Y generation) features a four-hour-door three-box profile with a continuous shoulder line, concave lower body panels, and a hexagonal frameless Singleframe grille flanked by angular LED headlights. The rear is defined by low-profile, wedge-shaped taillights, a subtle integrated bootlid spoiler, and a flat diffuser element with vertical reflectors. It rides on 18-inch alloy wheels and standard S line exterior body styling featuring aggressive front and rear bumper treatments.

The Audi A4 B9 sedan features a classic three-box profile with taut, chiseled body lines and a clamshell bonnet. It is defined by a wide, low-slung hexagonal Singleframe grille flanked by angular headlights. The rear showcases sharp LED tail lights connected visually by clean horizontal surfacing. Depending on the specification, it sits on alloy wheels ranging up to 19 inches and features a sloping roofline that flows smoothly into an integrated bootlid spoiler.

The Audi A5 Coupe (F5 generation) features a sleek two-door fastback profile with a low-slung stance and a sharply raked, sweeping roofline. The front is dominated by a wide, flat Singleframe grille flanked by angular LED or Matrix LED headlights. Its athletic sides are defined by a distinct shoulder character line running above the wheel arches, complemented by large alloy wheels and crisp horizontal LED tail lights at the rear.

The Audi A5 B10 sedan features a fastback-style silhouette with a low-slung, coupe-like greenhouse that flows smoothly into a liftback tailgate. The front is defined by a wide, flattened Singleframe honeycomb grille flanked by slim, sharp LED headlamps and sculpted air curtains. At the rear, a continuous three-dimensional light strip spans the width above a sporty bumper and integrated diffuser. The side profile showcases a long hood, flush door handles, and muscular wheel arch blisters reminiscent of classic quattro styling.

The Audi A6 C7 sedan features a sleek, low-slung four-door body style with a long bonnet and a sweeping, coupe-like roofline. It is characterized by a prominent single-frame hexagonal front grille flanked by angular headlights with distinct LED daytime running light signatures. The rear showcases tapered LED tail lights, a clean boot lid with an integrated spoiler lip, and alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 20 inches. Australian-delivered variants commonly feature aggressive styling elements courtesy of a standard S line exterior package, giving it lower bumpers and a planted stance.

The C8 Audi A6 sedan features a sharp, low-slung four-door profile defined by crisp character lines and a wide, prominent single-frame grille flanked by angular LED or Matrix LED headlights. Its rear end is characterized by sleek, horizontally oriented LED tail lights connected by a slim chrome strip, complemented by a clean trunk lid and sculpted bumper integration. The exterior stance is emphasized by a long wheelbase with balanced proportions, often riding on large multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The first-generation Audi A7 Sportback features a five-door liftback body style characterized by a sweeping, coupe-like roofline, a steeply raked rear window, and four frameless doors. At the front, it showcases a wide, hexagonal Singleframe grille flanked by tapered headlights with distinctive LED daytime running light signatures. The low-slung profile flows into a rounded tail with an active rear spoiler and wrap-around horizontal LED tail lights. It rides on large alloy wheels, accentuating its low, wide proportions and grand touring stance.

The second-generation Audi A7 (4K8) is a sleek five-door liftback featuring a low-slung, coupe-like fastback profile with four frameless doors and a sharply raked rear window. At the front, it showcases a wide, low-mounted Singleframe grille flanked by angular, horizontally segmented HD Matrix LED headlights. The rear is tapered like a yacht and is distinguished by an edge-to-edge LED light strip with vertical signature segments, complemented by an active rear spoiler that deploys at highway speeds. Sculpted shoulder lines and pronounced wheel arches accentuate its athletic proportions.

The Audi A8 D4 is a large, four-door luxury sedan characterized by a lightweight aluminum space frame, clean proportions, and a low, sweeping roofline. It features a prominent single-frame front grille flanked by tapered, angular headlights equipped with distinctive LED daytime running light signatures. The rear showcases wide, flat LED tail lights linked by a subtle chrome trunk accent, while the profile is defined by a clean, sharp upper shoulder line running from front to rear.

The Audi A8 (D5 generation) is a full-size luxury sedan featuring a sleek, three-box silhouette with a low, flowing roofline and muscular proportions. The front end is dominated by a wide, three-dimensional hexagonal Singleframe grille flanked by sharp HD Matrix LED headlights. The rear profile incorporates a continuous light strip utilizing advanced digital OLED technology. Clean lateral character lines emphasize its length, complemented by large alloy wheels and discreet chrome exterior accents.

The Audi e-tron (GE) SUV features a traditional five-door wagon body style with clean, muscular proportions closely resembling Audi's fuel-powered Q models. At the front, it showcases an octagonal Singleframe grille flanked by sharp LED headlights featuring four horizontal daytime running light signatures. The rear is dominated by wraparound LED tail lights connected by a continuous light bar spanning the tailgate. Exterior details include subtle orange or platinum charging accents, flush alloy wheels, and an integrated rear spoiler above the raked tailgate.

The Audi e-tron GT features a low-slung, four-door gran turismo sedan silhouette with wide, muscular haunches and a pronounced aerodynamic stance. The front end is defined by a wide, inverted Singleframe grille flanked by sleek, angular Matrix LED headlights. At the rear, a continuous light strip connects sharp LED tail lights above a prominent diffuser. It rides on large 20- to 21-inch alloy wheels and can be specified with a lightweight carbon-fibre roof panel.

The Audi Q2 is a compact five-door urban SUV featuring a sharp, polygonal design language with angular body creases and contrasting blade-style C-pillars. It is highlighted by a wide Singleframe grille, geometric LED headlights, and angular tail lights with available dynamic indicators. The stance is broad and low-slung for an SUV, rolling on alloy wheels up to 18 inches in diameter beneath pronounced wheel arches.

The first-generation Audi Q3 (8U) features a compact, five-door crossover SUV body with a coupe-like sloping roofline. It is characterised by a prominent single-frame grille, wraparound tailgate design, and wrap-around headlights that were updated with a sharper LED signature during its 2015 mid-life refresh. The stance is rounded and urban-focused, featuring subtle roof rails, body-coloured bumpers, and alloy wheel options ranging typically from 17 to 20 inches depending on the variant.

The Audi Q3 F3 generation is a compact 5-door SUV featuring athletic proportions, muscular wheel arches, and a bold octagonal Singleframe front grille. It is styled with sharp body creases, angular LED headlights, and wedge-shaped tail lights that flank the tailgate. The roofline is complemented by aluminium roof rails, while the stance is finished off with alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches depending on the variant.

The Audi Q5 (8R generation) is a five-door mid-size luxury SUV featuring a curvaceous, coupe-like roofline with aluminum roof rails and a distinct sloping tailgate. Up front, it showcases a prominent Singleframe grille flanked by wraparound headlights with integrated LED daytime running lights, which received a sharper, multi-faceted layout following its mid-cycle update. The profile is defined by flowing shoulder lines and muscular wheel arches that house alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 21 inches. At the rear, it is equipped with wraparound LED tail lights, a subtle integrated roof spoiler, and twin exhaust outlets.

The second-generation Audi Q5 (FY) features a five-door mid-size SUV body style characterized by athletic, sculpted flanks and balanced, aerodynamic proportions. Up front, it displays a prominent hexagonal Singleframe grille flanked by sharp LED or Matrix LED headlights featuring distinct daytime running light signatures. The rear highlights wraparound LED tail lights—with available digital OLED clusters—and clean bumper integrations. Roof rails, a raked rear hatch line, and various alloy wheel options ranging from 18 to 21 inches complete its contemporary stance.

The third-generation Audi Q5 SUV features an athletic, sculpted silhouette built on a new platform. Up front, it showcases a wider Singleframe grille flanked by slimline Matrix LED headlights. The rear is distinguished by a clean, continuous full-width light strip and deeply inset 3D-look tail lights (with optional next-generation OLED graphics). It rides on various alloy wheel designs ranging up to 21 inches, and features a sweeping roofline with an available panoramic glass sunroof.

The Audi Q7 (4M) is a large seven-seat luxury SUV featuring a muscular stance, sharp body creases, and a prominent hexagonal Singleframe grille flanked by angular LED or Matrix headlights. Its profile is defined by a strong upper shoulder line, an expansive glasshouse, and distinctive alloy wheel designs ranging from 20 to 22 inches. The rear sports wraparound LED tail lights connected by a chrome or trim strip, with sportier variants featuring S line body kits, larger air intakes, and a dual-exhaust layout.

The Audi Q8 features an athletic coupe-SUV body style with a wide, muscular stance, frameless doors, and a heavily raked, sloping roofline. The front end is dominated by a large octagonal Singleframe grille flanked by sharp Matrix LED headlights. The rear showcases a distinctive full-width LED light bar connecting angular tail lights above an aggressive lower diffuser. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging up to 22 inches, complemented by subtle roof rails and clean body-side character lines.

The Audi R8 Type 4S coupe features a low-slung, wide two-door stance with sharp, angular proportions and a mid-engine layout. It is characterized by an aggressive, wide Singleframe grille flanked by angular LED or laser headlights, split side blades on the doors, and a full-width rear mesh grille paired with oval or rectangular exhaust outlets. The exterior is completed by large alloy wheels and crisp character lines emphasizing the flared wheel arches.

The third-generation Audi TT Coupé features a low-slung, compact two-door fastback body style characterized by a distinctively arched roofline and prominent, muscular wheel arches. At the front, it showcases a wide hexagonal Singleframe grille accompanied by sharp, angular LED or Matrix LED headlamps featuring vertical daytime running light signatures. The rear is defined by clean horizontal lines, an active deployable spoiler that rises at highway speeds, and horizontal LED tail lights. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 20 inches, with short overhangs accentuating its aggressive, planted stance.

The first-generation Bentley Bentayga is a large luxury SUV characterized by a commanding, muscular stance and sculpted bodywork. The front end is dominated by a massive, upright matrix grille flanked by four distinctive circular LED headlamp units. At the rear, it features elliptical LED tail lights incorporating a signature B-graphic, alongside prominent rear haunches. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging up to 22 inches, complemented by an expansive glasshouse and an integrated roof spoiler.

The second-generation Bentley Continental GT coupe features a muscular two-door fastback body style with classic grand tourer proportions, characterized by a long bonnet, short front overhang, and pronounced rear haunches. The front fascia is dominated by a large, upright matrix grille flanked by four distinctive circular headlamps, where the outer lenses are larger than the inner ones. At the rear, the boot lid exhibits a subtle integrated aerodynamic spoiler lip above wide, ellipse-shaped LED tail lights. The side profile is defined by a sweeping power line running from the front guard toward the rear wheels, sitting atop large multi-spoke alloy wheels typically ranging from 20 to 21 inches.

The third-generation Bentley Continental GT coupe features a low, muscular fastback body style with two doors and elongated proportions. It is characterized by a wide matrix grille flanked by four jewel-like circular LED matrix headlights, with the outer pair noticeably smaller. The rear displays clean, wide haunches complemented by sleek elliptical tail lights that mirror the shape of the dual exhaust tips. It rides on large alloy wheels up to 22 inches and features a sweeping roofline flowing into a short, sculpted rear deck.

The fourth-generation Bentley Continental GT coupe features a muscular, low-slung two-door fastback body style with sweeping character lines and a wide, planted stance. Its revised front end introduces striking single-piece headlamps with an intense horizontal accent line flanking a prominent matrix grille. The rear showcases sleek, horizontally oriented elliptical tail lights and sculpted bumper geometry. It rides on large alloy wheel options ranging from 21 to 22 inches, complemented by refined roof framing that flows seamlessly into the muscular rear haunches.

The second-generation Bentley Continental GTC is a luxury two-door convertible featuring a triple-layer fabric soft-top roof and muscular, superformed aluminum body panels. Its front fascia is defined by a matrix mesh grille flanked by four distinct round LED headlamps, with the outer lamps being larger. At the rear, it sports a clean flat deck layout and twin oval exhaust finishers integrated into the bumper, complemented by large alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 21 inches.

The third-generation Bentley Continental GTC is a two-door luxury convertible featuring a sculpted, muscular body with an extended hood and a tailored fabric soft-top that deploys or stows in 19 seconds. Its front fascia is defined by a wide matrix grille flanked by four distinct round headlamps, where the outer lamps are larger than the inner ones. The rear showcases wide, athletic haunches and elliptical LED tail lights that mirror the shape of the dual exhaust outlets. It rides on large alloy wheels up to 22 inches, complemented by sharp power lines running along its low-slung profile.

The fourth-generation Bentley Continental GTC features a sweeping convertible body with an insulated four-layer fabric roof and muscular, well-defined rear haunches. It introduces a revolutionary front fascia marked by single, jewel-like LED matrix headlamps with a distinctive horizontal eyebrow accent. The wider, lower matrix grille is accompanied by a sculpted bumper and clean modern surfacing along the endless bonnet. At the rear, it sports wide, horizontal wrap-around taillights and sits on large alloy wheel options ranging up to 22 inches.

The second-generation Bentley Flying Spur is a large four-door luxury sedan featuring a muscular, low-slung body with a long bonnet and a powerful shoulder line. The front end is dominated by a bold chrome matrix grille flanked by distinctive quad-round LED headlamps, where the outer pair is noticeably larger than the inner pair. At the rear, it sports wide, sleek horizontal tail lights that replace the vertical clusters of the previous generation. The profile is accented by fender wing vents behind the front wheels, sharp character lines, and large multi-spoke alloy wheels, riding on a low and planted stance.

The third-generation Bentley Flying Spur is a four-door luxury sedan characterized by a long, muscular hood, a sweeping roofline, and a commanding wheelbase. Its front end features a prominent, upright vertical-vane matrix grille flanked by crystal-cut LED matrix headlights with striking illuminated inner rings. The rear is defined by wrap-around LED tail lamps incorporating a distinctive illuminated 'B' motif within the lens. It rides on large alloy wheels—typically 20 to 22 inches—and features a retractable 'Flying B' mascot atop the grille on select specifications.

The fourth-generation Bentley Flying Spur is a large luxury sedan featuring a muscular, flowing silhouette with clean, uninterrupted body surfaces and a smooth front wing. At the front, it departs from tradition by adopting single headlamps integrated with a redesigned bumper and radiator grille. The rear showcases a resculpted boot lid, modern tail lights, and a body-coloured number plate surround. It rides on large alloy wheels up to 22 inches in diameter, with sportier variants featuring dark-tinted lighting elements and gloss black exterior brightware.

The Bentley Mulsanne is a large, imposing four-door luxury sedan featuring a long hood, short front overhang, and a strong signature power line running along its profile. The front end is dominated by a grand matrix grille flanked by distinctive, circular all-LED headlights. At the rear, it features elegant tail lights incorporating a 'B'-shaped graphic motif. It rides on large 20-inch or optional 21-inch alloy wheels and includes signature 'Flying B' fender vents.

The F20 BMW 1 Series 5-door hatchback features a classic rear-wheel-drive silhouette defined by a long bonnet, a set-back cabin, and short overhangs. Up front, it features BMW's signature kidney grille flanked by angular headlights—which transitioned from a controversial, swept-back pre-facelift design to a sleeker, more horizontal profile during the 2015 LCI update. At the rear, it sports two-piece, wide-stretching 'L'-shaped tail-lights and a broad bumper stance. Exterior styling varies across trims like the Sport Line, Urban Line, and M Sport, showcasing distinct alloy wheel designs, aggressive front air intakes, and body kits.

The F40 BMW 1 Series is a 5-door hatchback featuring a wedge-shaped profile, a pronounced shark-nose front aspect, and a wide stance. It features a prominent interconnected kidney grille, angular LED headlights, and low-profile horizontal wraparound tail lights. The exterior is styled with short overhangs, a distinct Hofmeister kink on the C-pillar, and alloy wheel options ranging up to sporty multi-spoke configurations.

The BMW 1 Series 5-door hatchback features a low-slung, forward-leaning stance with a long bonnet and a cabin set toward the rear. It is styled with a wide, aggressive kidney grille containing diagonal and vertical bars, flanked by sharp LED headlights featuring angular daytime running light elements. The side profile highlights a dynamic roofline, flush door handles, and a distinctive '1' graphic integrated into the Hofmeister kink on the C-pillar trim. At the rear, it sports slim, multi-element LED tail lights and a sculpted bumper incorporating a diffuser-style element. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 19 inches in diameter and is available with a contrasting black roof option.

The BMW 2 Series coupé (F22) features a classic two-door, three-box silhouette defined by a long sculpted bonnet, a cabin set well back over the rear axle, and short overhangs. Its front end showcases angled twin-kidney grilles flanked by swept-back headlights with integrated LED corona rings or daytime running strips, while the rear features wide, L-shaped LED tail lights and a low boot lid. The profile is marked by frameless door glass and muscular wheel arches, housing various alloy wheel designs spanning 17 to 19 inches depending on the specification.

The BMW 2 Series F23 convertible features a sleek two-door body style with a low, sweeping profile and an insulated, power-operated fabric soft-top. It showcases a forward-slanting kidney grille, wide-set angular headlights with LED accents, and muscular, flared rear wheel arches. The rear is distinguished by wraparound L-shaped LED tail lights, a flat trunk lid, and sits on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches.

The BMW 2 Series Active Tourer (F45) is a compact 5-door MPV featuring a short-nosed, high-roof stance with relatively short front and rear overhangs. It features a prominent forward-slanting kidney grille flanked by swept-back twin-circular headlights, and a distinctive Hofmeister kink on the rear side window frame. The rear showcases wide horizontal L-shaped tail lights and a practical tailgate roof spoiler. Profile details include sculpted body side lines, alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches, and an optional panoramic glass roof.

The BMW 2 Series Coupé features a low-slung, athletic two-door profile with muscular wheel arches and a short rear deck. The front fascia incorporates angular LED headlights flanking a wide, horizontally-oriented kidney grille, while the rear features compact, three-dimensional LED tail lights. It rides on large alloy wheels up to 19 inches, and its silhouette is defined by a sweeping roofline and a pronounced power dome on the bonnet.

The BMW 2 Series Gran Coupé (F44) features a low-slung, four-door fastback body style with a sharply sloping roofline flowing into a short boot lid. The front end is dominated by an angled kidney grille and swept-back LED headlights, complemented by large bumper air intakes. Along the sides, it showcases frameless door windows and a distinct Hofmeister kink on the C-pillar incorporating a subtle '2' badge. The rear end exhibits slim, wraparound LED tail lights that extend towards the center, athletic bumper shaping, and alloy wheel options ranging up to large diameter M-sport designs.

The BMW 2 Series Gran Coupé (F74) features a low-slung, four-door fastback body style with frameless doors and a sweeping roofline. The front fascia incorporates a prominent, forward-leaning kidney grille—with vertical slats on standard trims or horizontal slats on the performance M235—flanked by sharply angled LED headlamps. At the rear, it sports slim LED tail lights, a clean decklid design, and a lower bumper configuration that hides exhaust tips on base models or exhibits quad tailpipes on the flagship M235. Exterior options include a contrasting gloss-black roof and alloy wheels ranging up to 19 inches.

The F30 generation BMW 3 Series comprises a low-slung four-door sedan, a practical five-door Touring (wagon), and the longer, high-roofed Gran Turismo hatchback featuring a coupe-like profile and frameless door windows. All variants feature a distinctive front fascia where the wide kidney grilles physically merge with the swept-back headlight clusters (which utilize twin corona rings and LED accents). The rear is defined by signature sweeping 'L'-shaped LED tail lights and dual or single-side exhaust outlets depending on the model.

The G20 BMW 3 Series is offered as a low-slung four-door sedan and a practical five-door wagon (Touring) featuring athletic proportions and crisp character lines. Up front, it features a prominent kidney grille flanked by angular LED headlights that slope slightly upward. The rear showcases slim, three-dimensional L-shaped tail lights and a sculpted bumper integrating dual exhaust outlets. Side profiles emphasize a modern take on the Hofmeister kink integrated directly into the C-pillar alongside diverse 18- or 19-inch alloy wheel designs.

The BMW F32 2-door coupé features a low-slung, stretched silhouette with a long bonnet, short overhangs, and a flowing roofline that merges into a muscular rear stance. At the front, it showcases a wide kidney grille flanked by twin angular headlights (using bi-xenon or LED technology) and distinctive 'Air Breather' vents positioned just behind the front wheel arches. The rear end is defined by wide horizontal LED tail lights and muscular wheel arches, complemented by various alloy wheel designs and an athletic stance sitting lower than its sedan counterpart.

The BMW 4 Series Convertible (F33) features a two-door body style with a three-piece retractable metal hardtop that delivers a sleek coupe-like roofline when closed. Its front fascia showcases a wide kidney grille flanked by sharp, swept-back LED headlights and a low-slung bumper with large air intakes. The side profile highlights a long bonnet, short overhangs, and 'Air Breather' vents positioned just behind the front wheel arches. At the rear, it is equipped with wide, wrap-around L-shaped LED tail lights and a sculpted bumper housing integrated exhaust tips.

The BMW 4 Series Coupé (G22) features a sleek, low-slung two-door fastback profile with a stretched bonnet, frameless door glass, and a flowing roofline ending in pronounced rear haunches. Its defining facial feature is an imposing, vertically-oriented double-kidney grille flanked by slim, angular LED or laser headlights with sharp daytime running light elements. The rear end is characterized by slender, darkened L-shaped LED tail lights, a sculpted boot lid spoiler lip, and a gloss-black lower diffuser incorporating integrated exhaust outlets. Alloy wheel designs range up to 19 inches in diameter, accentuating its wider rear track and planted stance relative to its sedan sibling.

The G23 BMW 4 Series Convertible features a low-slung, athletic two-door stance accented by a prominent, vertically oriented double-kidney front grille and narrow LED headlamps. Moving away from the preceding metal hardtop, it utilizes a sleek multi-layer fabric soft-top that folds neatly into the rear deck. The rear profile is defined by slim, darkened LED tail lights and a clean shoulder line flowing into a wide boot lid. Australian-delivered models typically ride on large alloy wheels (such as 19-inch variants) and feature aggressive M Sport body styling.

The BMW 4 Series Gran Coupé (F36) features a low-slung, four-door fastback body style with a flowing roofline that extends further back than the standard two-door coupe. It is characterized by frameless side doors, a wide stance, and a prominent single-piece rear liftback tailgate. The front end showcases a distinct kidney grille flanked by sharp twin-halo headlights (bi-xenon or LED), while the rear displays wrap-around LED tail lights and alloy wheel designs ranging from 18 to 19 inches.

The BMW 4 Series Gran Coupé (G26) features a sleek 4-door fastback body style with a low-slung, stretched silhouette, frameless door windows, and flush-fitting door handles. Up front, it is dominated by a prominent vertically oriented kidney grille flanked by angular LED or optional laser headlights. The rear showcases a sloping roofline culminating in a subtle tailgate spoiler, accompanied by slim wrap-around LED tail lights and muscular rear wheel arches. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 19 inches, featuring short overhangs and a pronounced stance.

The F10 generation BMW 5 Series features a traditional three-box sedan, a practical Touring wagon, and a high-roofed Gran Turismo fastback with a two-piece tailgate. It is characterised by a sweeping shoulder line, a short front overhang, and a prominent kidney grille flanked by twin circular or squared-off LED corona headlight rings. The rear sports wide, L-shaped LED tail lights and dual exhaust outlets, while various alloy wheel designs and an optional M Sport aerodynamic body kit accentuate its athletic stance.

The G30 BMW 5 Series sedan features a classic three-box silhouette with four doors, a low-slung stance, and a sharp character line rising toward the rear Hofmeister kink. The front end is dominated by a wide kidney grille that connects directly to slender, angular LED headlights. At the rear, it sports wraparound LED tail lights with a distinctive horizontal L-signature and dual exhaust outlets. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches, complemented by a smooth, sloping roofline.

The BMW 5 Series sedan (G60 generation) features a traditional three-box executive silhouette with flush door handles and an elongated, athletic stance. Up front, it showcases an angular, slightly forward-protruding kidney grille—optionally featuring illuminated 'Iconic Glow' surrounds—flanked by sharp, twin-element LED headlights. The rear profile is dominated by slim, horizontally stretched LED tail lights that wrap into the car's shoulders. Depending on the specification, variants feature large alloy wheels ranging up to 20 inches in diameter and clean rooflines flowing seamlessly into a short bootlid spoiler.

The third-generation BMW 6 Series features a long, sweeping bonnet, a low-slung stance, and a cabin set well back over the rear wheels. It includes a wide kidney grille flanked by adaptive LED headlights, muscular rear haunches, and wrap-around LED tail lights. The lineup spans the two-door convertible (with a fabric soft-top), two-door coupé, and the extended four-door Gran Coupé, all riding on various multi-spoke alloy wheel designs.

The BMW 6 Series Gran Turismo (G32) features a 5-door fastback body style with an elongated silhouette, a long wheelbase, and a sloping, coupe-like roofline terminating in a large power-operated tailgate. Up front, it showcases a wide kidney grille flanked by adaptive LED headlights, while the sides are characterized by frameless door windows. The rear features wraparound LED tail lights and an active rear spoiler that deploys automatically at highway speeds.

The BMW 7 Series (G11) is a 4-door luxury sedan featuring a low-slung, elongated profile and balanced proportions built around a carbon-core structure. Early models feature sleek, elongated LED headlamps flanking a standard-sized kidney grille, while post-2019 facelift versions introduce a heavily prominent, 40-percent larger vertical grille coupled with much narrower headlights. The rear exhibits slim, wrapping LED tail lights connected across the boot lid by a thin horizontal light strip, complemented by chrome Air Breather side vents on the front guards and multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The G70 BMW 7 Series is a large four-door luxury sedan featuring a monolithic, upright profile with flush door handles and a flat beltline. The front end is dominated by a massive, vertically oriented illuminated kidney grille flanked by divisive split-level headlights with slim upper daytime running lamps. The rear showcases clean, minimalist surfacing accented by very thin, horizontal LED tail lights. Available appearance trims include sophisticated luxury packages and athletic M Sport variants featuring larger front air intakes and distinct alloy wheel designs.

The BMW 8 Series features a low-slung, muscular stance with a long sculpted bonnet and a double-bubble roof profile on the coupé. At the front, it showcases a wide, angular kidney grille flanked by slender, sharply angled LED or laser headlights. The rear end is defined by slim, wraparound LED tail lights, muscular haunches, and dual exhaust outlets. The convertible variant features a multi-layer fabric soft-top, while the four-door Gran Coupé adds length with an extended wheelbase and gracefully sloping roofline.

The BMW i3 features a tall, narrow-bodied five-door hatchback configuration utilizing a lightweight carbon-fiber reinforced plastic passenger cell. It incorporates conventional front doors and rear-hinged suicide doors with a distinctive glass-heavy, black-accented roofline. The front end showcases a blanked-out, U-shaped kidney grille flanked by swept-back LED headlights, while the rear features a large glass tailgate embedded with U-shaped tail lights. It rides on tall, narrow-profile 19-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels designed to reduce rolling resistance.

The BMW i4 fastback features a low-slung, four-door coupe silhouette with frameless windows and a smooth liftback roofline. It is characterized by an assertive front fascia showcasing a prominent vertical kidney grille and sharp LED headlights with vertical daytime running lights. The rear exhibits slim, wraparound tail lights and a sculpted bumper incorporating diffuser elements. Standard setups ride on distinctive alloy wheels, complemented by clean body surfacing and flush-fitting door handles.

The BMW i5 sedan features an athletic four-door fastback silhouette with flush door handles and a pronounced Hofmeister kink on the C-pillar. The front showcases an upright, enclosed kidney grille with available contour lighting, flanked by sharp twin LED headlamps. At the rear, slim horizontal LED tail lights wrap into the quarter panels, complemented by a clean bumper design and available M Sport aerodynamic treatments. Large alloy wheels and a flat underbody optimize its modern aerodynamic profile.

The BMW i7 (G70) is a monolithic, full-size luxury sedan featuring an upright front fascia dominated by a massive, illuminated kidney grille. It utilizes a split headlight arrangement with upper crystalline daytime running lamps and flush, electronic door handles along its clean-surfaced, long-proportioned side profile. The rear is styled with slender, horizontal LED tail lights, while the roofline incorporates a panoramic glass sunroof and a distinct Hofmeister kink on the C-pillars.

The BMW iX large SUV features a monolithic, aerodynamic body with flush door handles and frameless windows. The front showcases a tall, vertical enclosed 'kidney' grille flanked by ultra-slim adaptive LED headlights. At the rear, it has thin, horizontal LED tail lights, a sloping roofline with an integrated spoiler, and large alloy wheels ranging up to 22 inches. Distinctive details include a unique hexagonal steering wheel and a large curved digital display inside the minimalist cabin.

The BMW iX1 (U11) is a compact five-door SUV featuring an upright front fascia, a nearly closed double-kidney grille, and slim adaptive LED headlights. Its side profile showcases a boxy silhouette with squared-off wheel arches, flush door handles, an extended roof spoiler, and a variety of alloy wheel designs up to 19 inches. The rear is defined by a square tailgate opening and striking three-dimensional L-shaped LED tail lights. Inside, the cabin is dominated by a sweeping, curved dual-screen display panel.

The BMW iX2 (U10) is a five-door compact coupe SUV featuring a sloping fastback roofline and an athletic, wedge-like stance. Its front end showcases angular adaptive LED headlights flanking an available illuminated 'Iconic Glow' hexagonal kidney grille. The rear profile is dominated by sharply creased, wraparound LED tail lights, a distinct tailgate spoiler lip, and a muscular bumper design. It rides on flush alloy wheels (typically 19-inch variants) with squared-off wheel arches characteristic of BMW's modern electric SUV lineup.

The G01 BMW iX3 is a mid-size five-door SUV sharing its traditional upright proportions and body shell with the combustion-powered X3. It features a blanked-off, closed double-kidney front grille adorned with signature blue EV accents, flanked by slim adaptive LED headlights. The rear is defined by wrap-around LED tail lights, a clean bumper lacking exhaust cutouts, and aerodynamic alloy wheels. Distinctive blue highlights on the badging and exterior trim set it apart from its fuel-driven counterpart.

The BMW X1 F48 is a five-door compact SUV characterized by a taller, more upright stance than its predecessor. It features a prominent kidney grille flanked by angular LED headlights, wrapping fenders, and horizontal LED tail lights. Depending on the variant trim, it rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches and includes body cladding, roof rails, and a heavily raked rear tailgate window.

The BMW X1 (U11) is a compact SUV featuring a modern, upright stance with clean side surfaces and nearly square wheel arches. It showcases an assertive front end dominated by a near-rectangular double kidney grille flanked by slim, angular LED headlights. The rear is defined by a subtle roof spoiler and distinctive, three-dimensional L-shaped LED tail lights, complementing flush-fitting door handles and alloy wheel options ranging up to larger diameter variants depending on the model line.

The first-generation BMW X2 features a compact 5-door crossover silhouette with a low-slung, coupe-like roofline and a hunkered-down stance. Its front end is defined by inverted kidney grilles—wider at the bottom than the top—flanked by sharp, angular LED headlights and a heavily sculpted bumper. A unique stylistic hallmark of this generation is the placement of BMW roundels on the C-pillars. The rear features wrap-around LED tail lights, a tailgate-mounted spoiler, and prominent dual exhaust outlets. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 20 inches in diameter, complemented by contrasting body cladding or body-colored M Sport styling packages depending on the variant.

The second-generation BMW X2 features a striking, fastback-style coupe SUV silhouette characterized by a sharply raked rear roofline and a prominent tailgate. It showcases an angular hexagonal kidney grille—optionally illuminated—flanked by sharp LED headlights with distinct dual-element daytime running lights. The rear end incorporates wraparound, claw-shaped LED tail lights and a muscular bumper design. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to large diameter sizes, complemented by clean body-side surfacing and flush door handles.

The F25 BMW X3 is a four-door mid-size luxury SUV featuring classic athletic proportions with a long wheelbase and short overhangs. Its front end is defined by a prominent kidney grille flanked by twin-circular headlamps (which merge into the grille on post-2014 LCI models). The rear features wraparound two-piece tail lights and a steeply raked tailgate, complemented by alloy wheel options ranging from 17 to 20 inches depending on the trim level.

The third-generation BMW X3 (G01) features a muscular, athletic five-door mid-size SUV stance with short front and rear overhangs. Up front, it showcases a prominent hexagonal kidney grille flanked by sharp, adaptive LED headlights. The rear highlights three-dimensional full-LED tail lights, a subtle downward-sloping roof spoiler, and alloy wheel options ranging from 18 to 21 inches. Variants equipped with the M Sport package add aggressive body-kit styling, larger air intakes, and shadowline trim.

The fourth-generation BMW X3 (G45) features a monolithic mid-size SUV body with clean surfaces, a lower stance, and aerodynamic flush door handles. It showcases an aggressive front end with an enlarged kidney grille—frequently edged with 'Iconic Glow' LED contour lighting—flanked by sharp headlights sporting dual vertical LED signature elements. The rear is defined by an angular tailgate, streamlined T-shaped or thin horizontal LED tail lights, and a sporty lower roofline. Alloy wheel designs range upwards from 19 inches, complemented by wider front and rear tracks.

The F26 BMW X4 is a five-door mid-size coupe-SUV featuring a distinct sloping roofline that descends sharply toward the rear, mimicking a fastback silhouette. Its front end is characterized by a prominent kidney grille flanked by twin-circular headlights that connect directly to the grille frame. The flanks display a raised beltline and contoured character lines above the wheel arches, while the rear features a high boot lid integrated with horizontal LED tail lights.

The BMW X4 (G02) features a fastback, sloping roofline coupe-SUV body style with four doors and a hunkered, athletic stance. It is characterized by a prominent kidney grille flanked by sharp, angular LED headlights and a heavily sculpted front bumper. The rear showcases slim, three-dimensional LED tail lights, a distinct tailgate spoiler lip, and muscular haunches over large alloy wheels. Roof details include a shark-fin antenna and an available panoramic glass sunroof.

The BMW X5 (F15) features a commanding, athletic five-door large SUV body style with a distinctively sculpted shoulder line and upright stance. Up front, it showcases angular, wide-stretching adaptive headlights that connect directly to a prominent kidney grille. The rear is defined by horizontal LED tail light clusters, a split tailgate configuration, and a integrated roof spoiler. Exterior detailing includes muscular wheel arches accommodating large alloy wheels, aerodynamic air breathers behind the front wheel vents, and satin aluminum roof rails.

The BMW X5 (G05) is a large luxury SUV characterized by a commanding, tall stance with muscular shoulder lines and sculpted body sides. Its front end is dominated by a large, single-piece vertical kidney grille flanked by sleek, angular LED headlights with distinct daytime running light signatures. At the rear, it features a practical split-tailgate configuration alongside slim, three-dimensional horizontal LED tail lights. The exterior is completed with athletic alloy wheel options ranging up to large diameters, integrated roof rails, and clean window surrounds.

The BMW X6 (F16) features a large five-door coupe-SUV body style with a prominent, sharply sloping fastback roofline and high-riding proportions. The front end is characterized by a bold, wide chrome kidney grille flanked by wraparound LED headlights that connect to the grille structure. Its side profile highlights muscular rear haunches, athletic character lines, and functional front fender air breathers. The rear sports a tapering tailgate with an integrated spoiler lip and slim, horizontal LED tail lights, riding on large alloy wheels.

The BMW X6 (G06) features a large five-door coupe-SUV body style with muscular proportions, an aggressive stance, and a heavily sloped, fastback roofline. Up front, it showcases an expansive single-frame kidney grille—frequently specified with 'Iconic Glow' illumination—flanked by sharp, angular LED or laser headlights. The rear is dominated by slim, wraparound horizontal LED tail lights, broad shoulders, and a sculpted tailgate. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 22 inches, complemented by distinctive aerodynamic body kits and coupe window lines.

The BMW X7 (G07) is a large, full-size luxury SUV featuring a boxy, commanding stance with four doors and a flat roofline. It is dominated by a massive vertical kidney grille at the front, flanked by slim dual-element headlights (which split into a multi-tier arrangement on post-2022 facelifts). The rear showcases a full-width chrome strip connecting thin, horizontal LED tail lights, complemented by a split tailgate. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 22 inches, with structured body side stampings and distinct window surrounds in chrome or high-gloss shadow-line trim.

The BMW XM performance SUV features a bold, elongated five-door body with an aggressive stance, sharp geometric creases, and a heavily sculpted bonnet. Its front fascia is defined by split LED headlights and a massive octagonal kidney grille equipped with illuminated 'Iconic Glow' contour lighting. In profile, it is characterized by a distinctive contrasting window accent band and large 22- or 23-inch alloy wheels. The rear incorporates sculptural three-dimensional tail lights with a gill-like louvered pattern, dual laser-etched BMW roundels on the glass edges, and stacked quad vertical exhaust tailpipes.

The BMW Z4 roadster features a classic long-bonnet, short-rear-deck sports car proportion with a fabric soft-top roof. Its front end is defined by a wide, low mesh kidney grille flanked by unique vertically-stacked LED headlights. The side profile is sculpted with a sharp, sweeping character line flowing from the front guard into prominent rear wheel arches. The rear features slim, horizontal wraparound LED tail lights and an integrated boot-lid spoiler above dual exhaust outlets.

The Bolwell Mk X Nagari is a low-slung, mid-engined 2-door coupé featuring a carbon-reinforced composite body with sweeping flying buttresses flowing from the rear window deck. It rides on large 19-inch alloy wheels and incorporates distinctive elements such as angular headlamp enclosures and tail-lights sourced from the DC5-generation Honda Integra. The exterior profile displays a wedge-like stance with cab-forward proportions, side air intakes, and a smooth rear fascia.

The Bolwell Nagari 500 is a low-slung, 2-door composite coupé featuring a rounded, aerodynamic nose, large side air intakes, and distinctive flying buttresses at the rear. It rides on wide alloy wheels—19-inch at the front and rear—and incorporates a single windscreen wiper alongside an integrated rear spoiler. The lighting setup includes sleek front headlight clusters and sharp rear tail lights derived from the DC5-generation Honda Integra.

The BYD Atto 1 is a compact five-door light hatchback featuring short overhangs and a stubby, tall-boy stance. It has angular headlamps integrated into a smooth front fascia, connected by a darkened trim piece, alongside a sharp lower bumper intake. The rear showcases wraparound tail lights linked by a full-width LED light bar across the tailgate. It rides on small 15-inch steel wheels with covers, sports a steeply raked windscreen matching its high roofline, and displays rising character lines along its side profile.

The BYD Atto 2 is a compact 5-door small SUV featuring an upright, blocky stance with short overhangs and lower body cladding. The front end incorporates sharp angles, LED headlamps, and slim daytime running lights. At the rear, it sports a roof spoiler and a full-width light bar bridging 'Chinese knot'-style tail lights. It rides on either 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and features a floating roofline.

The BYD Atto 3 is a compact, five-door medium SUV featuring smooth, curved body proportions and aerodynamic lines. The front end is characterized by a sleek closed-off grille section framed by slim LED headlights and a distinctive full-width LED light bar. At the rear, it utilizes a continuous full-width tail light cluster spanning the tailgate, which displays the prominent 'Build Your Dreams' lettering. Side details include distinctive matte-silver scale-pattern trim pieces on the C-pillars and 18-inch aerodynamic alloy wheels.

The BYD Dolphin is a compact five-door electric hatchback characterized by a cab-forward silhouette, short overhangs, and flowing ocean-inspired side character lines. The front fascia features slim, continuous LED headlights linked by a trim piece across a smoothed-out grille-less panel. The rear showcases a full-width LED light bar spanning the tailgate above a subtle roof spoiler. Depending on the variant, it rides on 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and is frequently styled with optional two-tone body paint combinations.

The first-generation BYD Seal is a four-door fastback sedan featuring sleek, low-slung proportions and a coupe-like roofline. The front fascia is highlighted by sharp, wraparound LED headlights and distinctive, double-stacked, boomerang-shaped LED daytime running lights integrated into the bumper. At the rear, it sports a full-width LED tail light bar featuring an intricate, water-drop-inspired dot-matrix pattern. The exterior is further detailed with flush-fitting electronic door handles and multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The first-generation BYD Seal 6 sedan features a sleek, aerodynamic fastback four-door profile with flowing organic lines and a low drag coefficient. The front end incorporates a sculpted lower grille with chrome detailing, flanked by sharp, modern LED headlights. At the rear, it displays a contemporary full-width LED light bar connecting the tail lights, complemented by a clean bumper diffuser design. The exterior is finished with alloy wheels and clean surfacing across the proportions.

The BYD Sealion 5 medium SUV features a traditional five-door crossover stance with a muscular front fascia, sharp LED headlamps, and a clean lower bumper intake. The profile is defined by flowing character lines, body-side cladding, and two-tone 18-inch alloy wheels. At the rear, it sports a full-width LED light bar stretching across the tailgate above a subtle bumper garnish. Higher grades add details like a panoramic glass roof.

The BYD Sealion 6 is a medium 5-door SUV featuring a modern, European-influenced exterior design. It is characterized by sleek LED headlamps flanking a clean front fascia, a wide stance with smooth body lines, and distinctive full-width LED tail lights with sequential indicators. Riding on 19-inch alloy wheels, the exterior profile also incorporates matte roof rails and a standard panoramic glass roof.

The BYD Sealion 7 features a five-door, coupe-style medium SUV body with a sloping roofline and a pronounced rear roof spoiler. It has a low-slung stance with flowing proportions, featuring smooth body panels and flush door handles. The front end showcases angular LED headlights flanking a closed-off, aerodynamic fascia, while the rear incorporates a full-width LED light bar spanning the tail gate. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 19 to 20 inches in diameter, depending on the variant.

The BYD Sealion 8 is a large, five-door plug-in hybrid SUV featuring a spacious three-row cabin and prominent proportions. The exterior incorporates modern styling cues including full-length LED lighting, a bold front grille configuration, and large 20- to 21-inch alloy wheels. Distinctive features encompass a full-width rear light bar, a panoramic glass roof with a power sunshade, and flush-mounted door elements.

The BYD Shark 6 is a large four-door dual-cab ute featuring a muscular stance, high waistline, and a wide black grille dominated by prominent block-letter BYD branding. It is flanked by wraparound LED headlights connected by a full-width daytime running light bar. The rear features rectangular, stacked LED tail lights spanning across the tailgate. It rides on 18-inch alloy wheels and comes equipped with fixed side steps, wheel arch cladding, and a lockable tub with a spray-on liner.

The first-generation Chery Omoda 5 is a five-door small SUV featuring a coupe-like fastback roofline and sharp, angular proportions. Its bold front fascia is dominated by a diamond-matrix frameless grille integrated with slim, T-shaped LED daytime running lights, while the main headlamp clusters are set lower into the bumper corners. The rear features a sloping tailgate topped by a distinctive split roof spoiler, full-width connected LED tail lights, and a high beltline with pronounced body creases. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches and is frequently accented with contrasting color highlights along the lower body and side mirrors.

The first-generation Chery Omoda E5 is a compact electric SUV featuring a smooth, closed-off front fascia that differentiates it from its petrol sibling. It sports sleek LED daytime running lights, angular headlamp clusters, and rides on 18-inch alloy wheels fitted with aerodynamic covers. The side profile is defined by a coupe-like sloping roofline, while the rear showcases sharp LED tail lights spanning the width of the tailgate beneath a subtle roof spoiler.

The Chery Tiggo 4 Pro is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a high-riding stance with protective dark body cladding and roof rails. The front end is dominated by a bold diamond-pattern grille flanked by sharp LED headlights and integrated daytime running lights. Depending on the specification, it rides on either 17-inch black or 18-inch multi-spoke alloy wheels, the latter housing contrasting red brake calipers. The rear showcases wraparound tail lights connected by a subtle trim element above a chunky bumper, with higher grades also adding a power sunroof.

The second-generation Chery Tiggo 7 Pro is a medium SUV featuring a 5-door layout with modern, flowing proportions and a prominent hexagonal front grille accented by diamond-pattern inserts. It is equipped with sharp LED headlights, a full-width LED rear light bar, and a distinct floating roof line capped with a rear spoiler. The vehicle rides on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels and includes clean character lines along its profile.

The Chery Tiggo 8 Pro Max is a large, seven-seat SUV featuring a boxy, long-proportioned body with clean character lines and integrated roof rails. Its front end is dominated by a large diamond-pattern matrix grille framed by a thick chrome or grey surround, flanked by sharp, angular LED headlights. The rear showcases full-width connected LED tail lights with an illuminated light bar. It rides on either 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels and comes equipped with a panoramic glass sunroof on higher grades.

The first-generation Chery Tiggo 9 is a large 7-seat SUV characterized by a bold, prominent diamond-patterned front grille flanked by slim LED headlamps. Its profile features clean body lines, flush retractable door handles, and a floating roof design leading into a rear tailgate dominated by a full-width LED light bar. It rides on large multi-spoke alloy wheels (ranging from 19 to 20 inches depending on the variant) and incorporates a panoramic sunroof.

The second-generation Chrysler 300 sedan features a bold, muscular 4-door profile characterized by high beltlines, chunky wheel arches, and narrow, slit-like side windows. It sports a prominent front grille—refreshed with a larger honeycomb pattern and wing badge in 2015—flanked by projector-style headlights with integrated LED daytime running lights. The rear is defined by vertical LED tail lights accented by a chrome strip spanning the boot lid, sitting atop large 18-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels.

The second-generation Citroen Berlingo van features a stubby, rounded front fascia with an integrated bumper housing the central chevron grille and swept-back teardrop headlights. Offered in short (L1) and long (L2) body configurations, it has a high-roof stance, large flat side panels, practical sliding side doors, and asymmetrical 60:40 split rear barn doors. The utilitarian exterior is typically detailed with black plastic bumpers, body-side mouldings, and simple steel wheels.

The third-generation Citroen Berlingo van features a stubby, high-nosed front profile with a blunt multi-slate grille flanked by slim upper DRL strips and lower-mounted rectangular headlights. Its boxy, utilitarian body style is defined by short overhangs, clean slab-sided door panels with protective lower side moulding inserts, and a high roofline. The rear is fitted with upright, vertical tail light clusters and symmetrical side-hinged barn doors or a top-hinged tailgate. Exterior detailing includes steel or alloy wheels tucked beneath squared-off wheel arches, optional roof rails, and distinct body lengths (short M and long XL variants).

The third-generation Citroen C3 hatchback features a five-door, chunky crossover-inspired stance with rounded proportions and high-set LED daytime running lights linked to a central double-chevron grille. Its profile is characterized by protective rectangular Airbump panels on the lower doors and a contrasting floating roof design available with various color packs. The rear features square-shaped tail lights with a 3D effect and a stout tailgate. It rides on alloy wheels up to 17 inches, emphasizing its quirky, highly customizable aesthetic.

The second-generation Citroen C4 (B7) hatchback features a conservative yet sophisticated five-door profile with flowing shoulder lines and a planted stance. The front end is characterized by a prominent chrome grille featuring integrated double-chevron badges that stretch into the angular, swept-back headlamps. At the rear, it sports wraparound horizontal tail lights and a subtle roof-mounted spoiler. The exterior is finished with alloy wheel options ranging from 15 to 17 inches, smooth body-colored bumpers, and chrome window surrounds on higher trim levels.

The third-generation Citroen C4 features a high-riding, coupe-like five-door hatchback body with crossover proportions and rugged wheel-arch cladding. It is styled with a distinctive V-signature LED lighting arrangement up front, merging into a multi-tier grille design. The rear profile is dominated by a sharply raked tailgate window split by a subtle aerodynamic spoiler and distinctive split LED tail lights. It rides on 18-inch alloy wheels and features a raised, sloping roofline.

The Citroen C4 Cactus Mk1 is a distinctive five-door compact SUV featuring a high-riding stance and a smooth, rounded front fascia. Its defining exterior characteristic is the prominent, protective thermoplastic 'Airbump' panels lining the lower doors and corners. It incorporates a split headlight layout with slim LED daytime running lights positioned high above the lower-set main headlights. The rear features rectangular, horizontally oriented tail lights and rear doors with pop-out hinged windows instead of traditional roll-down glass.

The Mk2 Citroën C4 Picasso is a compact MPV featuring a five-door body style characterized by an expansive panoramic windshield and a plunging glasshouse. Its futuristic front end utilizes a multi-tier lighting arrangement with slim LED daytime running lights flanking a wide upper grille, while the main headlamps are set lower into the bumper. The rear displays distinctive 3D-effect C-shaped tail lights framing a broad tailgate, complemented by alloy wheels and a high, practical roofline.

The Citroën C5 sedan features a sleek, low-slung four-door body style with a distinctively long greenhouse and a concave rear windscreen. Its front end is defined by an aggressive chrome-accented double-chevron grille flowing into sharp, swept-back boomerang headlights. The rear sports wraparound tail lights and a planted stance sitting on alloy wheels, while higher-spec variants benefit from the unique stance-adjusting Hydractive suspension system.

The Citroën C5 Aircross Mk1 is a 5-door medium SUV featuring rounded, muscular proportions and distinctive 'Airbump' plastic cladding panels along the lower doors. The front fascia showcases a multi-tier lighting arrangement with slim LED daytime running lights merging into a wide grille, stacked above separate main headlights. The rear features rectangular, pill-shaped LED tail light clusters with a distinct multi-cube internal graphic. Its silhouette is characterized by a floating-roof design accented by a continuous chrome signature line framing the side window glass.

The Citroen C5 X liftback features a distinct fastback-wagon silhouette with a raised, SUV-inspired ride height and matte black wheel arch cladding. Up front, it showcases a prominent double-chevron grille that merges into a V-shaped LED lighting signature, complemented by a clamshell bonnet. The side profile flows via a long roofline into a steeply raked rear window, dual rear spoilers, and a powered tailgate. It rides on 19-inch alloy wheels and comes standard with a black bi-tone roof paired with a panoramic glass sunroof.

The Mk2 Citroën Grand C4 Picasso features a distinctive five-door compact MPV body with a cab-forward stance, highlighted by a sweeping panoramic windscreen and expansive side glass area. Its front fascia introduces a unique multi-tier lighting arrangement with slim upper LED daytime running lights, lower main headlights, and a wide grille split by the double-chevron badge. The rear features an upright tailgate flanked by 3D-effect LED tail-lights, while a signature contrasting roof arch accentuates its extended profile.

The Cupra Ateca medium SUV features a sharp, angular body style with aggressive front and rear bumper treatments. It has a prominent honeycomb-patterned front grille flanked by angular LED headlights and distinct copper-tinted branding. The rear is defined by LED tail lights, a row of subtle ventilation slots beneath the tailgate, and prominent quad exhaust outlets. It sits on 19-inch alloy wheels that incorporate signature copper accents.

The Cupra Born is a compact, five-door electric hatchback featuring a cab-forward stance, a steeply raked windshield, and distinctive copper-accented exterior detailing. Its front fascia is highlighted by sharp, angular LED headlights flanking a low-profile "shark-nose" upper section and a wide lower grille framed in contrasting copper. The rear profile is defined by a continuous coast-to-coast LED light bar spanning the tailgate, a subtle roof spoiler, and a sporty lower diffuser. It rides on aerodynamically styled alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches, complemented by unique texturing on the C-pillars.

The Cupra Formentor Mk1 is a five-door medium crossover featuring a low-slung, coupe-like stance with muscular body creases and a raked roofline. It sports an aggressive 'shark-nose' front grille paired with sharp LED headlamps and distinctive triangular daytime running lights. The rear is characterised by a full-width LED light bar encompassing an illuminated central badge, complemented on high-tier variants by sporty alloy wheel designs and quad exhaust outlets. Copper-coloured interior and exterior accent details serve as a signature visual hallmark for the brand.

The Cupra Leon Mk4 is available as a five-door hatchback and a lengthened Sportstourer wagon, both sharing athletic, cab-backward proportions. The front features a distinctive shark-nose fascia with an aggressive lower intake, sharp angular LED headlights incorporating triangular daytime running lights, and a copper Cupra badge on the nose. The rear is defined by a full-width LED light bar framing a central illuminated logo, complemented by sculpted body side creases and aero-optimized 18- or 19-inch alloy wheels finished in contrasting black and copper accents.

The Cupra Tavascan Mk1 is a 5-door electric medium SUV coupe featuring an aggressive 'shark nose' front profile, a heavily sculpted V-shaped bonnet, and sharp matrix LED headlights with a distinctive three-triangle signature. Its sleek side profile displays a fastback roofline, athletic creases, flush door handles, and large aerodynamic alloy wheels ranging from 19 to 21 inches. The rear is defined by a full-width coast-to-coast tail light bar housing an illuminated central Cupra logo, complemented by a prominent, aerodynamic lower diffuser.
