The Cupra Terramar Mk1 is a medium five-door SUV featuring an aggressive, wedge-like profile with a tapered 'shark-nose' bonnet and sculpted body sides. It sports angular LED headlights with distinctive triangular daytime running signatures flanking a low-mounted wide grille, accented by signature copper trim details. The rear showcases a full-width LED light bar with an illuminated central Cupra badge, a chiselled bumper, and an integrated diffuser. It rides on large alloy wheels (up to 20 inches) nestled beneath pronounced wheel arches, complemented by a sloping roofline and floating rear pillars.

The Deepal E07 features a distinctive fastback coupe-SUV body style that can electrically transform into an open-bed utility truck via a sliding rear glass dome. The front fascia is dominated by an aerodynamic active grille flanked by sleek, full-width connected LED lighting. It rides on large 21-inch alloy wheels framed by chunky wheel arches, accentuating its long 3,120 mm wheelbase and sloping roofline.

The Deepal S07 is a medium-sized five-door electric SUV featuring a sleek, aerodynamic body style with a sloping fastback roofline and flush electric door handles. The front end incorporates sharp LED headlights, distinctive angular bumper creases, and a smooth closed-off grille design. At the rear, it is defined by a full-width 'Star Flame' LED light bar with an illuminated central logo and a high-mounted hexagonal stop light. It rides on 19-inch alloy wheels and comes equipped with a large fixed panoramic glass roof featuring an electric sunshade.

The Denza B5 is a large, boxy five-door 4x4 SUV featuring upright proportions, squared-off wheel arches, and a side-hinged tailgate carrying a mounted spare wheel. It is characterized by a prominent rectangular front grille integrated with modern LED headlamp clusters and blocky daytime running lights. The rear features vertical rectangular tail lights and robust bumper detailing, riding on alloy wheels with distinct off-road wheel-arch trim and a high ground clearance.

The Denza B8 is a large, boxy, five-door 4x4 SUV featuring imposing, squared-off proportions with a prominent upright grille and modern rectangular LED headlamps. At the rear, it is fitted with a side-hinged tailgate, a full-size spare wheel cover, and vertical pillar-integrated tail lights. The exterior includes robust multi-spoke alloy wheels, a flat roofline equipped with integrated roof rails, and rugged body cladding enhancing its heavy-duty stance.

The Denza D9 is a large, boxy luxury people mover featuring a massive, imposing chrome front grille with thick vertical slats flanked by sharp LED headlights. It has a tall stance with a flat roofline, dual power-sliding rear doors, and a broad upright rear tailgate framed by full-width, interconnected LED tail lights featuring intricate geometric patterns. The exterior details include flush side window surrounds, multi-spoke alloy wheels, and a fixed panoramic glass roof.

The Ferrari 12Cilindri is a two-door grand tourer available as a fastback coupé or retractable hardtop spider. It features classic long-hood, short-deck proportions with an ultra-clean, sculpted profile and a distinctive black front panel connecting the slim headlights. The rear incorporates geometric, rectangular tail lamps alongside active aerodynamic flaps integrated into the rear screen rather than a fixed wing.

The Ferrari 296 GTB is a two-door sports berlinetta featuring a low-slung, compact footprint with short overhangs and muscular, curvaceous rear haunches. Its front fascia is defined by low-profile, swept-back LED headlights flanking a wide lower intake, while the side profile highlights a visor-like wrap-around windshield inspired by classic racing Ferraris. At the rear, it incorporates a central exhaust tip, a distinct Kamm-tail design with slim horizontal LED tail lights, and an active rear spoiler integrated into the bumper. The stance is completed by 20-inch alloy wheels and flying buttresses tapering gracefully toward the rear engine cover.

The Ferrari 488 GTB is a 2-door mid-engine berlinetta sports car featuring a low-slung, aerodynamically sculpted body. Its front end is defined by a double-profile splitter and aggressive radiator air intakes, flanked by swept-back LED headlights. The sweeping flanks are dominated by large, scalloped side air intakes divided by a central splitter, leading to a muscular rear stance with circular tail lights and quad exhaust tips. It rides on 20-inch alloy wheels that house carbon-ceramic brakes, and features an integrated slotted spoiler flap on the rear deck lid.

The Ferrari 812 Superfast features a low-slung, two-door fastback grand tourer body with aggressive aerodynamic proportions, a long sculpted bonnet, and a cab-rearward stance. Its front end showcases sharp LED headlights flanking a wide grille, paired with active aerodynamic vents on the sculpted flanks. The rear is dominated by traditional quad round tail lights set beneath an integrated spoiler lip above a quad-exhaust diffuser setup.

The Ferrari California T is a 2-door retractable hardtop convertible featuring classic front-engine grand tourer proportions with a long bonnet and compact, muscular rear. The front end showcases a prominent egg-crate grille flanked by large cooling intakes and swept-back wedge-shaped LED headlights, complemented by two distinct heat-extractor vents on the bonnet. Its sculpted flanks incorporate side strakes and fender lines inspired by the 250 Testa Rossa, leading into a rear styling characterized by horizontal elements, a subtle integrated boot-lid spoiler, quad horizontal or side-by-side exhaust tips, and a triple-fence diffuser.

The Ferrari F12berlinetta features a classic two-door grand tourer body style characterized by an elongated bonnet, a low-slung stance, and a cabin pushed toward the muscular rear end. Its front fascia showcases an aggressive wide grille flanked by swept-back, full-LED headlights and unique aerodynamic "Aero Bridge" channels sculpted into the hood and side flanks. The rear adopts a Kamm-tail design incorporating dual circular LED tail lamps on either side and an F1-inspired central fog light within the diffuser. It rides on 20-inch alloy wheels and features aerodynamic active brake cooling ducts on the front bumper.

The Ferrari F8 Tributo is a two-door mid-engine sports coupe featuring a low, aerodynamic profile with a heavily sculpted front end incorporating a prominent S-Duct. It is characterized by sleek, slim LED headlights, side air intakes integrated into the beltline, and a rear decklid covered by a clear Lexan engine cover with three functional cooling louvres. The tail features classic twin circular light clusters set beneath a wraparound spoiler and is finished with 20-inch alloy wheels.

The Ferrari GTC4Lusso features a distinctive three-door shooting brake body style with a long hood, tapered fastback-like sloping roofline, and wide athletic proportions. It is styled with a large, single front grille flanked by swept-back headlights, while the rear showcases Ferrari's signature quad circular taillights and an integrated roof spoiler. The stance is complemented by large alloy wheels over sculpted wheel arches, defining its high-performance grand tourer profile.

The Ferrari LaFerrari features a low, wide, aerodynamic stance with a sharp, delta-shaped front nose and slim, angled headlights. It is styled with butterfly doors, a compact teardrop cabin profile, and integrated side vents with active aerodynamic body elements. The rear showcases rounded tail lights, quad exhaust tips, and a large active diffuser and spoiler system.

The Ferrari Portofino is a two-door, 2+2 retractable hardtop convertible featuring a sleek two-box fastback silhouette and a long sculpted bonnet. It features horizontal full-LED headlights with integrated outer air intakes that vent into the front wheel arches, flanking a wide, edge-to-edge radiator grille. The rear sports wide-set LED tail lights and a clean tail volume that conceals the folding hardtop mechanism.

The Ferrari Purosangue features a high-riding, four-door fastback SUV body style with a distinct two-box silhouette and rear-hinged 'suicide' doors. It lacks a traditional upper front grille, utilizing instead a floating aerodynamic suspension element with slim LED daytime running lights flanking the sculpted bonnet. The rear incorporates a horizontal light strip integrated into a sharp cut-line above an aggressive quad-exhaust diffuser. The stance is defined by muscular rear haunches, prominent side aerodynamic 'aerobridges', a carbon-fibre roof panel, and large 22-inch front and 23-inch rear alloy wheels.

The Ferrari Roma is a 2-door fastback coupe featuring clean, minimalist grand-touring proportions inspired by 1960s models. It has a shark-nose front end with a body-colored, perforated grille and ultra-slim horizontal LED headlights. The rear showcases a sloping roofline, an active deployable spoiler, and futuristic minimalist wrap-around horizontal tail lights. It rides on 20-inch alloy wheels and features flush door handles.

The Ferrari SF90 Stradale features a low-slung, cab-forward two-door berlinetta body style with a steeply raked windshield and a remarkably low engine cover. Its front fascia is defined by slender, horizontal matrix LED headlights and a sculpted bumper with integrated aerodynamic vortex generators. The rear showcases horizontal, squared-off rectangular tail lights and a prominent active 'shut-off Gurney' rear wing system designed to manage downforce. It rides on staggered alloy wheels and features a low roofline equipped with distinct flying buttresses flowing into the rear fenders.

The Fiat 500 Type 312 hatchback is a compact, retro-styled three-door city car featuring a rounded silhouette and a stubby, sloping bonnet. Its front fascia is characterized by circular headlamps paired with smaller lower-mounted oval auxiliary lights flanking a thin horizontal grille strip. The side profile exhibits high-arched windows, a gently curved roofline, and alloy wheel options ranging from 15 to 16 inches. At the rear, it features vertical rectangular tail lights with body-coloured center inserts and a subtly integrated roof spoiler above the tailgate.

The Fiat 500C (Type 312) convertible features a compact, retro two-door body style with fixed metal side pillars that preserve the hatchback's profile. It is characterized by an electrically operated fabric soft-top that folds back in a 'sardine-tin' style between the permanent window frames. The front end displays rounded, teardrop-shaped headlights flanking a small grille adorned with a central chrome mustache bar. At the rear, it features rectangular tail lights with body-colored center inserts, riding on small alloy wheels ranging from 15 to 16 inches.

The Fiat 500e hatchback features a compact, retro-inspired three-door body with rounded proportions and smooth aerodynamic surfaces. It is characterised by circular LED headlights intersected by the bonnet line, creating a distinctive 'eyebrow' DRL effect, alongside a clean, smooth front fascia devoid of a traditional grille. The rear sports simple oval-shaped LED tail lights and a curved tailgate carrying the signature '500e' badging. It rides on distinctive 17-inch alloy wheels and features a fixed glass panoramic roof as standard on Australian specifications.

The Fiat 500X (Type 334) is a five-door compact crossover SUV featuring rounded, retro-inspired proportions reminiscent of the smaller Fiat 500. It features a clamshell bonnet, circular upper headlamps paired with lower oval auxiliary lights, and a chrome-accented upper grille housing the brand emblem. The rear end is characterized by rounded square tail lamps with body-colored center inserts, while higher-spec variants include rugged lower body cladding, roof rails, and alloy wheel options ranging from 16 to 18 inches.

The third-generation Fiat Ducato panel van features a utilitarian boxy silhouette with an expansive flat-panel body, large side sliding doors, and vertical double-hinged rear doors. It is characterized by a prominent, steeply raked windscreen that flows seamlessly into the bonnet line. The front fascia showcases high-mounted, swept-back rectangular headlamps flanking a wide grille, which received modern updates including integrated LED daytime running lights in later facelifts. It rides on steel wheels and is available in multiple wheelbase lengths and high-roof configurations featuring distinct overhead bulkheads.

The Fiat Freemont is a 5-door crossover SUV with a long, boxy station-wagon profile. It features a bold front fascia with a cross-hair style honeycomb grille housing the Fiat badge, flanked by angular, wraparound rectangular headlamps. The rear exhibits large, rectangular-rounded LED tail lights spanning the corners of the tailgate, complemented by pronounced wheel-arch flares and a high roofline that can be equipped with chrome roof rails. It rolls on either 17-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels depending on the trim level.

The second-generation Fiat Scudo panel van features a cab-forward semi-bonnet profile with a steeply raked windscreen and a short front overhang. The front end is characterized by a wide, smiling lower bumper intake, a slim upper grille integrated with the Fiat badge, and large, swept-back teardrop headlights that stretch high up the front fenders. In profile, the body exhibits clean side panels with protective black mouldings, dual sliding side doors, and a low-roof configuration. The rear is fitted with vertically stacked tail lamps flanking asymmetrical split barn doors, and the van rolls on 16-inch steel wheels.

The third-generation Fiat Scudo panel van features a utilitarian, aerodynamic boxy silhouette with short- and long-wheelbase configurations, dual sliding side doors, and a low 1.94-meter roof height. The front end is dominated by a flat grille bearing the Fiat Professional badge, flanked by sleek wraparound headlights (halogen on base models or full-LED on Primo trims). The rear incorporates vertical tail lights alongside 270-degree opening barn doors or an optional glazed liftgate. It rolls on 16-inch steel wheels with full-size spares and features clean body sides with available body-coloured door handles on higher grades.

The Ford EcoSport is a high-riding subcompact SUV featuring a tall, boxy 5-door profile with a side-hinged tailgate carrying a distinctive rear-mounted spare wheel. Early models feature a split front grille and high-mounted headlamps, while the 2018 facelift introduces a sculpted bonnet with a central power bulge, a large trapezoidal grille, and angular headlamps. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 17 inches and includes roof rails along its high roofline.

The Ford Endura (CD539) is a five-door, five-seat SUV featuring a broad, muscular stance and a sloping roofline. It features a prominent hexagonal front grille flanked by sleek, angular LED headlights, while the rear showcases an expansive full-width tail light bar. Depending on the variant, it rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches, with sportier trims like the ST-Line adopting unique black exterior grille accents and body kits.

The Ford Escape medium SUV features a contemporary five-door wagon body with smooth, rounded proportions and fluid aerodynamic lines. The front end is dominated by an angular trapezoidal grille flanked by sharp, swept-back headlamps and lower-mounted fog lights. The rear incorporates wraparound LED tail lights, a body-coloured roof spoiler, and a sculpted tailgate. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches, complemented by subtle roof rails on select variants.

The Ford Everest UA features a robust 5-door wagon body style with a muscular, high-riding stance. Up front, it showcases a prominent chrome-accented trapezoidal grille flanked by swept-back projector headlights, which connect to a rugged bumper assembly. The rear profile incorporates wrap-around horizontal tail lights bridged by a chrome garnish strip across the tailgate. Distinctive features include prominent wheel arches, side steps, and alloy wheel sizes ranging from 17 to 20 inches depending on the specification tier.

The third-generation Ford Everest features a muscular, boxy five-door SUV body style with a wider track and longer wheelbase than its predecessor. The front fascia is dominated by a strong horizontal upper grille bar flanked by signature C-clamp LED headlights. The rear showcases horizontal LED tail lights connected by a dark accent strip, while the profile incorporates distinct roof rails and alloy wheel sizes ranging from 17 to 21 inches depending on the variant.

The Ford F-150 utility features a massive dual-cab body style with prominent proportions, sitting on a long wheelbase paired with either a 5.5-foot or 6.5-foot styleside tray. The front end is dominated by a large, upright grille flanked by distinct C-clamp style headlights, which use halogen bulbs on the XLT and full LED setups on the Lariat. It rides on 20-inch alloy wheels and features practical elements such as chrome bumpers, black or chrome running boards, and vertical tail lights framing the tailgate.

The WS, WT, and WZ generation Ford Fiesta hatchback features an aggressive kinetic design with swept-back headlights and a wedge-like profile defined by sharp character lines. Later models (WZ) introduced a prominent trapezoidal chrome grille reminiscent of Aston Martin styling, flanked by elongated headlamp clusters. The rear showcases high-mounted vertical tail lights curving up the D-pillars, a roof spoiler, and a sculpted tailgate. It was available in both 3-door and 5-door body styles, sporting alloy wheel options and a compact, aerodynamic stance.

The Ford Focus LZ features a sculpted hatchback and sleek sedan profile, both defined by low-slung proportions and a dynamic stance. The front end is anchored by a prominent, wide trapezoidal grille flanked by sharp, swept-back headlamps and lower bumper fog light surrounds. At the rear, it is styled with wraparound tail lights (incorporating sleek LED elements on higher variants) and a roof-mounted bee-sting antenna. Alloy wheel designs range from 16 to 18 inches across the variants, complementing its clean body lines.

The Ford Kuga TF is a five-door mid-size SUV featuring a dynamic, aerodynamic two-box profile with swept-back proportions. Early models feature a lower trapezoidal grille opening and wraparound headlights, which were updated during a 2016 facelift to introduce a much taller, prominent upper hexagonal grille and elongated headlamps with LED daytime running lights. The rear is defined by wraparound horizontal tail lights, a sculpted tailgate, and a purposeful stance riding on alloy wheels (ranging from 17-inch to 19-inch depending on the grade). Higher-tier variants feature body-coloured aerodynamic kits, roof rails, and an available panoramic glass sunroof.

The MD-generation Ford Mondeo is offered in five-door hatchback and five-door wagon body styles characterized by a low-slung, athletic profile and sleek proportions. Its front fascia is dominated by an aggressive, high-mounted trapezoidal grille flanked by sharp, swept-back projector or adaptive LED headlamps. The rear features wraparound LED tail lamps connected by clean surface lines, while higher grades sit on large alloy wheels and offer options like a panoramic glass roof.

The S550 Ford Mustang is offered as a fastback coupe and a soft-top convertible with a low, wide stance. It features an aggressive trapezoidal front grille flanked by sharp, angular HID or LED headlamps, which became sleeker and more aggressively slanted following the 2018 mid-cycle facelift. The rear end incorporates iconic tri-bar sequential LED tail lights set above a sculpted decklid and prominent diffuser panel. It rides on large 19-inch alloy wheels and displays classic long-hood, short-deck proportions.

The Ford Mustang S650 coupe features a muscular fastback body style with sharp, angular proportions and a low, aggressive stance. It is characterized by a chiseled front fascia, a wide rectangular grille, and tri-bar LED headlights alongside distinct vertical front air intakes. The rear showcases a sharply recessed vertical-slat tail light treatment, quad exhaust tips, and available aerodynamic spoilers. It rides on 19-inch alloy wheels and features clean roof lines that sweep smoothly into the truncated rear deck.

The first-generation Ford Puma is a compact five-door crossover SUV featuring athletic, coupe-like proportions with a gently sloping roofline, short overhangs, and a planted stance. It is characterized by prominent, swept-back LED headlights positioned high on the front guards flanking a curved bonnet, along with a wide hexagonal front grille (gloss-black on ST-Line variants). The rear showcases wraparound horizontal LED tail lights, muscular rear haunches, and a subtle body-coloured roof spoiler.

The Ford Ranger PX generation features a rugged dual-cab, single-cab, and extra-cab utility body style with a high-riding, muscular stance and prominent body-on-frame proportions. Early models sport a trapezoidal grille flanked by angular, swept-back rectangular headlamps, while subsequent facelifts introduce a sharper, more rectangular grille and projector-style headlights. The rear is fitted with simple vertical tail lights, and the exterior can be configured with alloy or steel wheels, robust side steps, and sports bars depending on the variant.

The Ford Ranger RA features a muscular dual-cab or single-cab utility body style with an increased track width and boxier, upright proportions. Its front end is defined by a bold, blunt grille crossed by a central horizontal bar and flanked by distinctive C-shaped LED daytime running lights. The rear incorporates modern LED tail-light clusters and a clean tailgate stamped with the Ranger name. Exterior details include structured wheel arch flares, robust alloy or steel wheel options, and an integrated box step behind the rear doors for easy tray access.

The Ford Transit features a prominent, trapezoidal upper grille flanked by swept-back, wraparound headlamps and a high-set, aerodynamic windscreen. Its utilitarian body style includes a slab-sided profile with protective plastic side mouldings, sliding side passenger or cargo doors, and vertical rectangular tail lights at the rear. Available configurations range from low-roof models to high-roof jumbo variants with dual rear wheels, complemented by twin rear barn doors that swing open wide.

The Ford Transit Custom VN van features a two-box commercial body style with a short or long wheelbase and dual sliding side doors. It has a prominent trapezoidal front grille flanked by swept-back angular headlights and a steeply raked windshield blending into a flat roofline. The rear utilizes vertical tail lights alongside a tailgate or twin barn doors. Exterior details include steel or alloy wheels and protective side mouldings tailored for commercial utility.

The second-generation Ford Transit Custom is a mid-size panel van featuring a modern, aerodynamic boxy silhouette with short front overhangs and a low roofline designed to clear standard multi-story car parks. The front end is dominated by a wide grille flanked by sleek full-LED headlights connected by an integrated LED light bar graphic. At the rear, it is equipped with vertically oriented LED tail lights and asymmetric side-hinged cargo barn doors. The side profile reveals sculptured body panels, sliding side doors, and alloy wheel options ranging up to larger diameter designs on sport variants.

The Forthing Taikon 5 is a five-door medium SUV featuring a coupe-inspired fastback roofline and athletic proportions. The front fascia is dominated by an aggressive cascading waterfall grille flanked by a split LED headlamp layout with slim daytime running lights. The rear incorporates a full-width LED light bar. It rides on prominent alloy wheels and features clean body surfacing with a floating roof effect.

The Foton Sauvana is a rugged, 5-door, 7-seater large body-on-frame SUV. It features a chunky, utilitarian stance with a wide chrome-accented front grille, wraparound headlights integrated with LED daytime running lights, and high-set fog lamps. The profile includes pronounced wheel arches, side steps, and roof rails, riding on 17-inch alloy wheels. The rear features a broad tailgate, a roof-mounted spoiler, and wraparound tail lights.

The first-generation Foton Tunland dual-cab ute features a traditional, rugged truck stance with conventional four-door proportions and a utilitarian cargo tub. Its front end is defined by a bold, chrome-accented horizontal grille flanked by angular, swept-back headlamps, paired with a chunky front bumper hosting circular fog lights. The side profile includes pronounced wheel arches, available side steps, and typically rides on 16- or 17-inch alloy wheels. At the rear, it features vertical rectangular tail lights flanking a drop-down tailgate with a prominent handle and an integrated rear step bumper.

The Foton Tunland V7 is a large dual-cab ute featuring a muscular, US-style pickup silhouette. It is distinguished by an upright, squared-off front grille with horizontal bars flanked by vertically stacked LED headlights and daytime running lights. The side profile showcases flared wheel arches, side steps, and 18-inch gloss black alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tyres. The rear features a utility-focused cargo tub equipped with a spray-in liner, integrated tie-downs, and LED tail lights.

The Foton Tunland V9 is a large 4-door dual-cab utility featuring a bold, American-inspired full-size pickup stance. It is styled with a broad, sculpted hexagonal front grille flanked by sleek quad LED headlights, accompanied by prominent bonnet lettering and black fender flares over 18-inch alloy wheels. The rear features integrated LED taillights, a damping tailgate, and a spacious cargo tub, complemented by chunky side steps and a full-length sports bar spanning the roofline.

The Foton View CS2 panel van features a boxy, high-roof commercial body style with a length of over 5.3 meters and dual front doors alongside sliding side access. It incorporates a prominent vertical chrome-accented front grille flanked by swept-back wraparound headlights and integrated front bumper fog lights. The rear showcases a tall, flat vertical tailgate configuration with stacked vertical tail lights. It rides on 15-inch wheels and features a high-roofline silhouette optimized for internal cargo volume.

The first-generation Geely EX2 is a compact, five-door electric light hatchback featuring smooth, rounded proportions and short overhangs. It is characterized by feather-inspired LED headlights, a closed-off front fascia, conventional flush door handles, and cloverleaf-inspired 16-inch alloy wheels. The rear profile highlights wraparound tail lights and a rounded tailgate layout, complemented by a distinctive front trunk (frunk) under the bonnet.

The Geely EX5 is a five-door medium SUV featuring clean, modern proportions with smooth body panels and flush electronic door handles. The front end incorporates sleek LED headlights flanking a closed-off panel with an active lower grille shutter. At the rear, it features a full-width light bar configuration and a high-mounted roof spoiler above a lifting tailgate. It rides on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels depending on the variant, and higher trims add an expansive panoramic glass sunroof.

The Geely Starray EM-i is a medium 5-door SUV featuring a modern, aerodynamic silhouette with a sculpted bonnet and clean body side creases. The front end incorporates a streamlined expression with slim LED headlights flanking a minimalist upper fascia. At the rear, clean surfacing is punctuated by a contemporary full-width LED light bar. Depending on the variant, it sits on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels that fill the wheel arches cleanly, and features an available panoramic power sunroof with a sunshade.

The Genesis G70 (IK generation) is a four-door medium luxury sedan featuring a low-slung, rear-wheel-drive stance characterized by a long bonnet, short front overhang, and a swept-back roofline. The front fascia is dominated by a large, crest-shaped mesh grille flanked by slender, split-design multi-lamp headlights. At the rear, it features split wrap-around tail lights, dual or twin oval exhaust outlets, and a subtle boot-lid spoiler. The side profile incorporates functional fender vent garnishes behind the front wheels, complemented by alloy wheel designs and chrome window surround trim.

The facelifted Genesis G70 medium sedan features a low-slung, athletic four-door stance with a long hood and short overhangs. Its aggressive front end is defined by a prominent, low-mounted crest grille flanked by distinctive two-tier 'Quad Lamp' split LED headlights. The rear mirrors this lighting layout with split horizontal tail lights, complemented by an integrated ducktail boot spoiler and large oval exhaust outlets. It rides on staggered 19-inch alloy wheels that fill out muscular rear guards, and includes dark chrome exterior accents on higher sport variants.

The Genesis G70 Shooting Brake features a sleek, five-door medium wagon body with a sloping roofline and a unique single-piece glass tailgate. The front showcases the brand's low-mounted signature 'Crest' grille flanked by split 'Quad Lamp' multi-beam LED headlights. The rear incorporates twin-bar horizontal LED tail-lights stretching into the tailgate alongside a prominent floating roof spoiler. It rides on 19-inch alloy wheels and features twin parabolic side body lines that accentuate the flared wheel arches.

The Genesis G80 generation DH is a large, four-door executive sedan featuring a traditional three-box silhouette with a long bonnet and cab-rearward proportions. It is characterized by a large chrome-framed hexagonal grille, sweeping wraparound headlights with LED daytime running elements, and clean, horizontal body lines along its flanks. The rear incorporates sleek horizontal tail lights, a subtle integrated bootlid spoiler, and dual exhaust outlets framed in chrome. It sits on multi-spoke alloy wheels (with available dark 19-inch rims on Sport Design variants) and features a classic luxury stance.

The Genesis G80 (RG3) is a large luxury sedan featuring a sleek fastback-style roofline, a low-slung stance, and four doors. It is defined visually by a massive, low-mounted Crest grille flanked by signature split dual-line horizontal LED quad headlights. The side profile emphasizes a classic luxury proportion with a long dashboard-to-axle ratio and a single parabolic character line running down the flanks. At the rear, the minimalist boot lid houses matching split horizontal LED tail lights that echo the front lighting theme.

The Genesis DH large sedan features a traditional four-door, rear-wheel-drive silhouette with a long bonnet, short front overhang, and an elongated wheelbase. Its front fascia is dominated by a large, single-piece hexagonal chrome grille flanked by sleek HID headlights and integrated LED daytime running lights. The profile is defined by a sweeping character line along the flanks leading into an aerodynamic bootlid and jewelled LED tail lights. Australian models ride on multi-spoke alloy wheels (18-inch standard or 19-inch with option packs) and feature a flowing roofline with an available panoramic glass roof.

The Genesis GV60 small SUV features a smooth, athletic coupe-crossover body style with a clamshell bonnet and flush, pop-out door handles. Its low-slung front fascia incorporates a low-mounted crest grille flanked by distinctive dual-line 'quad' LED headlights. The sloping rear profile is accented by matching dual-line LED tail lights and an integrated spoiler. It rides on large alloy wheels and features sleek surfacing without traditional side creases.

The Genesis GV70 features a flowing, coupe-inspired medium SUV body style with a distinctively sloping roofline and muscular rear haunches. It is defined by a massive Crest grille flanked by distinctive two-tier 'Quad Lamps' utilizing thin horizontal LED strips that extend along the front fenders. The rear mirrors this lighting signature with slim dual-line horizontal tail lamps. Distinctive side profile details include a dramatic parabolic chrome line sweeping down the flank, while variants feature large aerodynamic alloy wheels and dual or dark-chrome exhaust finishers.

The Genesis GV80 JX1 is a large 5-door luxury SUV defined by a prominent, crest-shaped G-Matrix mesh grille flanked by distinctive double-bar horizontal 'quad' LED headlights. Its substantial profile features a sweeping parabolic shoulder line that arcs along the length of the body, complemented by a smoothly sloping roof contour and large 20-inch or 22-inch alloy wheels. The rear mirrors the front lighting motif with matching split horizontal quad taillights, rounding out a planted and muscular stance.

The Genesis GV80 Coupe features a large, fastback-style sloping roofline that drops aggressively toward the rear, complemented by a distinct integrated rear spoiler. It shares the brand's signature massive double-layered G-Matrix mesh grille and ultra-thin, double-line Micro Lens Array LED headlights. The side profile is defined by a continuous parabolic shoulder line and large 22-inch multi-spoke alloy wheels unique to the coupe variant. The rear end incorporates matching dual-line LED tail lights and prominent dual exhaust finishers.

The GWM Cannon dual-cab ute features a muscular and chunky stance with a prominent, oversized chrome or black grille dominating the front fascia. It is flanked by sleek LED headlights and integrated daytime running lights. The side profile highlights four full-sized doors, flared wheel arches housing 18-inch alloy wheels, and available side steps and sports bars. The rear is fitted with vertical LED tail lights and a practical tailgate that often includes a clever fold-out access step.

The GWM Cannon Alpha is a large, wide dual-cab ute with an elevated, muscular stance and chunky proportions. The front fascia is dominated by a bold, expansive grille flanked by stacked square LED headlights. Along the sides, it features fixed entry side steps and 18-inch alloy wheels. At the rear, it includes a distinctive 60/40 split tailgate design alongside a standard high-mounted LED tray light.

The first-generation Haval H2 is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a prominent chrome-slotted front grille flanked by swept-back headlights and lower LED daytime running lights. Its side profile showcases an upright stance with a rising beltline, chrome window surrounds, and 18-inch alloy wheels, alongside optional contrasting roof color schemes. The rear features wraparound tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and a bumper finished with a silver skid plate and dual exhaust tips.

The third-generation GWM Haval H6 is a medium SUV featuring a modern, rounded body profile with smooth sheet metal and a relatively long wheelbase. The front end is dominated by a large, geometric mesh grille flanked by sleek LED headlights and vertical daytime running light signatures. At the rear, it incorporates a contemporary full-width LED light bar connecting angular tail lamps. Distinctive exterior elements include subtle body cladding, alloy wheels ranging up to 19 inches, roof rails, and a subtle rear roof spoiler.

The first-generation GWM Haval H6 GT features a fastback coupe-SUV body style with a sloping roofline, a subtle rear tailgate spoiler, and a prominent stance. It has a muscular front fascia featuring a wide, aggressive mesh grille flanked by slender LED headlights and angular lower bumper styling. The rear incorporates wraparound LED tail lights spanning the liftgate, accompanied by lower bumper garnish. It rides on 19-inch black alloy wheels and includes body-clad wheel arches as well as integrated roof rails.

The first-generation GWM Haval H7 sold in Australia features a rugged, upright, boxy medium SUV body style with strong, squared-off lines and five doors. It exhibits a commanding stance with a prominent, muscular grille flanked by distinct angular headlights, and incorporates a tailgate-mounted external spare wheel. The rear profile showcases vertical tail light clusters complementing its utilitarian aesthetic, while the exterior is finished with robust wheel arches and roof rails.

The first-generation Haval Jolion is a 5-door compact SUV featuring a modern, flowing silhouette with sweeping character lines, body-side chrome garnishes, and standard roof rails. It features a large, prominent hexagonal mesh front grille flanked by striking LED headlights and distinct, vertical fang-like daytime running light strips extending into the bumper. At the rear, it is equipped with wraparound angular tail lights and a subtle roof spoiler. The exterior is finished with 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels depending on the variant.

The GWM Ora hatchback features a compact, retro-futuristic five-door body with rounded proportions and smooth surfacing. It is characterized by prominent oval-shaped 'cat-eye' LED headlights flanking a smooth, closed-off front fascia. The rear incorporates a clean tailgate design embedded with a distinct horizontal LED light strip running across the width. It rides on alloy wheels up to 18 inches in size, with select sporty variants offering contrasting trim accents, and can be optioned with a fixed glass panoramic roof.

The first-generation GWM Ora 5 is a compact electric SUV featuring a retro-inspired, curved-body design with fluid crossover proportions. It features water drop-inspired LED headlights, a smooth enclosed front fascia, and matching LED tail-lights. The profile is styled with standard roof rails, rear privacy glass, 18-inch alloy wheels (featuring a distinctive four-leaf clover design on select variants), and an available panoramic glass roof with an electric sunshade.

The Great Wall Steed dual-cab ute features a utilitarian four-door body style with standard side steps and a prominent chrome front grille flanked by wraparound headlights and integrated LED daytime running lights. Its profile displays conventional truck proportions with 16-inch alloy wheels, chunky wheel arches, and a rear tray equipped with a stainless-steel sports bar and factory tub liner. The rear features upright vertical tail lights framing the tailgate, while utility-focused exterior details include a high-mounted stop lamp and chrome body side mouldings.

The GWM Tank 300 features a boxy, neo-retro body-on-frame SUV silhouette with a flat roofline, high ground clearance, and flared wheel arches. It is equipped with round LED headlights integrated into a wide horizontal front grille, accompanied by distinctive vertical daytime running light strips slicing through the front fascia. The rear features a side-hinged tailgate mounted with a full-size spare wheel, vertical rectangular tail lights, and chunky bumper profiling. It rides on 18-inch alloy wheels and incorporates rugged protective cladding around the lower perimeter.

The first-generation GWM Tank 500 is a large, boxy, body-on-frame SUV featuring an imposing, upright stance. Its front fascia is dominated by a massive chrome-trimmed or gloss-black grille with thick horizontal bars, flanked by bold LED headlights and daytime running lights. The rear profile incorporates a side-hinged tailgate mounted with a full-size spare wheel and vertical LED tail lights. It rides on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels, features high ground clearance, roof rails, and is equipped with fixed or electrically retractable side steps.

The GWM Cannon dual-cab ute features a muscular, high-riding stance with four full-size doors and a sculpted bonnet. It is fronted by a large, prominent chrome or dark-accented grille flanked by sweeping LED headlights and integrated daytime running lights. The rear showcases vertical tail lights framing the tailgate, which often incorporates a unique integrated pull-out step ladder. Exterior details span across variants with alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches, roof rails, a sports bar, and rugged additions on specific trims like black body cladding, metal side steps, steel bumpers, and a raised air intake snorkel.

The GWM Cannon Alpha is a large dual-cab ute featuring a muscular, commanding stance with broad body proportions. It is characterized by a prominent front fascia incorporating a large chrome-accented grille flanked by distinctive, stacked square LED headlights. The rear features a practical 60/40 split tailgate design that opens both sideways and downwards. Riding on 18-inch alloy wheels, the exterior also includes fixed side steps and an elevated cabin silhouette.

The first-generation GWM Haval H2 is a compact five-door SUV featuring an upright stance, a prominent chrome-trimmed grille, and swept-back headlamps integrated with LED daytime running lights. Its side profile highlights a rising beltline, optional two-tone roof coloring, roof rails, and multi-spoke 18-inch alloy wheels. The rear features wrap-around horizontal tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and a robust lower bumper finished with a faux skid plate and twin exhaust outlets.

The first-generation GWM (Haval) H8 is a large five-door luxury SUV featuring rounded, substantial proportions and a sweeping roofline equipped with integrated roof rails and a shark-fin antenna. The front end showcases a prominent chrome-slat grille flanked by swept-back xenon headlights with integrated daytime running lights, alongside a heavily contoured bumper housing lower fog lamps. At the rear, it features wraparound horizontal tail lights, a chunky bumper with a stainless steel protector, and dual exhaust outlets. It sits on alloy wheels ranging from 18-to-19-inch variants and includes distinctive touches like chrome door handles and side entry steps.

The first-generation GWM Haval H9 is a large, square-bodied, four-door SUV featuring a tall stance and a flat roofline. It features a prominent chrome front grille with thick horizontal slats flanked by wraparound headlamps. At the rear, it is distinguished by a side-hinged tailgate carrying a full-size spare wheel, complemented by vertically oriented tail lights. It rides on large alloy wheels and incorporates side steps and protective lower body cladding.

The third-generation GWM Haval H6 is a medium SUV featuring a contemporary 5-door wagon body style with clean, flowing proportions and a prominent chrome-accented mesh grille flanked by sleek LED headlights and vertical daytime running light signatures. The rear showcases a full-width LED light bar spanning the tailgate beneath an integrated roof spoiler. Exterior details include dynamic alloy wheel options up to 19 inches, silver roof rails, and a panoramic sunroof on higher specification grades.

The GWM Haval H6GT features a dynamic coupe-SUV body style characterized by a sharply sloping fastback roofline, a muscular stance, and flared wheel arches. At the front, it displays a bold, wide mesh grille flanked by sleek LED headlights and aggressive bumper accents. The rear is defined by a split tailgate spoiler, a subtle lip spoiler, and connected LED tail lights. It rides on 19-inch black alloy wheels and includes sporty body cladding and blacked-out exterior trim details.

The second-generation GWM Haval H7 features a tall, boxy, and rugged medium SUV silhouette characterized by straight lines and an upright stance. The front end is dominated by a bold grille flanked by sharp auto LED headlights and distinct daytime running lights. At the rear, it sports signature vertical tail lights and a practical side-hinged tailgate mounted with a full-size external spare wheel. It rides on prominent alloy wheels—up to 19 inches in size—and includes robust roof rails and protective lower body garnishes.

The first-generation GWM Haval Jolion is a 5-door small SUV featuring a contemporary stance with smooth body lines and a heavily sculpted bonnet. It is characterized by a large, chrome-trimmed hexagonal mesh grille flanked by swept-back LED or halogen headlights incorporating distinctive vertical daytime running light strips that drop down into the bumper. The rear profile is styled with angular, boomerang-style LED tail lights stretching inward across the tailgate. Depending on the variant, the exterior is completed with standard roof rails, a shark-fin antenna, and either 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels.

The GWM Ora Good Cat is a compact, five-door electric hatchback featuring retro-inspired, rounded proportions reminiscent of classic European cars. It is styled with prominent circular LED headlamps flanking a smooth, closed-off front fascia, and distinctive tail lights integrated cleanly beneath the rear glass. The profile showcases flowing curves, short overhangs, and available contrasting roof colors paired with stylish alloy wheels.

The GWM Ora 5 features a compact, coupe-like SUV silhouette with a bold, retro-inspired stance and smooth body panels. It is outfitted with distinctive water drop-inspired LED headlights flanking a clean, enclosed front fascia, along with contemporary 18-inch machined alloy wheels. The rear profile is rounded with a sloping roofline, connected tail light styling, and an overall minimalist aesthetic tailored for urban driving.

The GWM Steed dual-cab ute features a traditional, utilitarian truck stance with four doors and a prominent chrome-slatted front grille flanked by swept-back halogen headlamps and integrated LED daytime running lights. Its side profile highlights flared wheel arches housing 16-inch alloy wheels, chunky side steps, and a rear tub fitted with a standard sports bar and tub liner. The rear is styled with vertical, high-mounted LED tail lights and a drop-down tailgate flanked by a chunky bumper.

The GWM Tank 300 features a boxy, neo-retro body-on-frame layout with a prominent upright grille and circular LED headlights. It has flared wheel arches, squared-off proportions, and a side-hinged tailgate carrying a full-size spare tire. Alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches sit beneath high-clearance wheel wells, complemented by vertical rear tail lights and rugged bumper styling.

The GWM Tank 500 is a large, boxy five-door body-on-frame SUV characterized by an imposing stance. It features a massive, prominent chrome grille dominated by thick horizontal bars, flanked by rectangular LED headlights. The rear showcases vertical tail lights and a side-hinged tailgate mounted with a full-size spare wheel cover. Depending on the model variant, it rides on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels and includes fixed or automatic electric side steps alongside a panoramic sunroof.

The first-generation Haval H2 is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a prominent chrome grille flanked by wraparound headlights and integrated LED daytime running lights. Its profile exhibits a high beltline, a subtle roof spoiler, and 18-inch alloy wheels. The rear end is highlighted by horizontal tail lights and twin exhaust finishers.

The first-generation Haval H6 is a five-door medium SUV featuring a traditional, upright station wagon silhouette with chrome window surrounds and standard roof rails. The front fascia is dominated by a prominent, multi-slat chrome grille flanked by swept-back headlights and lower bumper fog lamps. At the rear, it has wraparound tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and a chunky bumper housing dual exhaust tips. Depending on the trim, it rides on 17-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels.

The third-generation Haval H6 is a five-door medium SUV featuring clean, modern proportions with a prominent geometric chrome-accented mesh grille and sleek LED headlights at the front. Its side profile is defined by a rising beltline, alloy wheels, and a subtle roof spoiler, while the rear showcases a contemporary full-width LED light bar.

The first-generation Haval H6 GT features a fastback coupe-SUV body style with a sharply sloping roofline and a lower, more aggressive stance than the standard wagon. It has four doors, wider wheel arches accented in black cladding, and rides on 19-inch alloy wheels. The front end is dominated by a bold, mesh-pattern grille flanked by angular LED headlights and distinct daytime running lights. At the rear, it includes a distinctive split-rear spoiler arrangement—one above the rear glass and another on the tailgate lip—alongside sleek LED tail lights and dual chrome exhaust tips.

The first-generation Haval H7 is a medium five-door SUV featuring a conventional, slightly sloping roofline and a rounded, aerodynamic body silhouette. It is characterized by a prominent hexagonal front grille framed by angular, swept-back headlights with projector lenses and LED daytime running lights. The rear features wrap-around horizontal tail lights connected by a subtle chrome garnish, paired with a sculpted tailgate and dual integrated exhaust tips. It rides on large multi-spoke alloy wheels—typically 19- or 20-inches depending on the specification—and includes standard roof rails.

The first-generation Haval H8 is a large, five-door urban SUV featuring a traditional boxy, rounded-off stance with a prominent chrome-surrounded front grille and swept-back xenon headlights. Its side profile is defined by flowing roof rails, a subtle shark-fin antenna, standard side steps, and either 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels. The rear is equipped with wraparound LED tail lights, a body-coloured bumper with integrated exhaust finishers, and an electric tailgate on higher grades.

The first-generation Haval H9 is a large, tall, body-on-frame 5-door, 7-seat SUV featuring boxy, utilitarian proportions. It is characterized by a prominent vertical-slat chrome grille flanked by wrap-around xenon or projector headlamps, alongside vertical tail lights running up the D-pillars. Australian versions ride on 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and originally featured a side-hinged tailgate mounted with a full-size spare wheel. It is equipped with standard side steps and a high ground clearance stance.

The first-generation Haval Jolion features a compact 5-door SUV body style with modern proportions, defined by a large, sweeping hexagonal mesh grille flanked by striking LED headlights and distinct, vertical fang-like daytime running light signatures cascading down the bumper. The profile is characterized by clean, flowing character lines, chrome window surrounds, and standard roof rails, sitting atop 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels. At the rear, it sports unique vertical or boomerang-shaped tail lights that stretch inward along the tailgate, complemented by a subtle roof spoiler.

The first-generation Holden Acadia is a large, boxy five-door seven-seater SUV characterized by prominent, straight-edged American proportions. It features a bold, forward-slanting front grille flanked by wraparound headlights with integrated LED daytime running lights, and distinctive LED tail lights. Depending on the variant, the exterior is fitted with either 18-inch or larger 20-inch alloy wheels, alongside roof rails and chrome window or door handle accents.

The Holden Astra PJ 3-door hatchback features a sleek, low-slung stance with a steeply raked windshield and a dynamic coupe-like roofline flowing down to an integrated rear spoiler. The front fascia showcases a wide trapezoidal lower grille and sharp, wraparound projector headlights framing a slim upper grille bar bearing the Holden badge. Sculpted character lines sweep upward along the flanks, accentuating flared wheel arches that typically house large alloy wheels. The rear end is defined by wraparound tail lights, a contoured tailgate, and a purposeful lower bumper housing dual or single exhaust outlets depending on the variant.

The BK/BL generation Holden Astra comprises a European-sourced hatchback, station wagon, and a North American-designed sedan. It features a low-slung, aerodynamic profile with a prominent corporate grille bridged by a central chrome bar flanked by swept-back projector headlights and LED daytime running lights. The hatchback and wagon variants showcase a distinctive floating roof design created by a darkened C- and D-pillar graphic, while the rear exhibits angular wraparound tail lights. Alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches complete its contemporary stance.

The sixth-generation Holden Barina TM is offered as a five-door hatchback and a four-door sedan featuring an aggressive wedge-shaped profile with a short nose. Early models feature distinctive exposed, motorcycle-inspired quad headlights alongside a dual-port grille, while post-2016 facelifts transition to a more traditional angular projector headlight design with a hexagonal lower grille. The hatchback distinguishes itself with rear door handles hidden within the C-pillar surrounds and a subtle roof-line spoiler. Depending on the spec level, the exterior sits on 15-inch steel or alloy wheels up to larger 17-inch rims, complemented by rounded tail lights at the rear.

The Holden Caprice WN is a large, long-wheelbase four-door sedan featuring a commanding, formal chrome grille flanked by projector headlights. In profile, it presents low-slung, stretched proportions with generous rear door lengths, accented by chrome window surrounds and 19-inch alloy wheels. The rear features wraparound tail lights, a clean boot lid contour, and prominent exhaust outlets integrated into the lower bumper.

The Holden Captiva is a five-door crossover SUV featuring a tall stance, prominent flared wheel arches, and body-colored or contrasting protective side mouldings. Its front end is characterized by a prominent crossbar grille carrying the Holden lion badge, flanked by wraparound headlamps and a sculpted bonnet. Over its production run, it received exterior refreshes that updated the front fascia, grille mesh, and LED-integrated headlight and tail light clusters. The profile is distinguished by standard roof rails, side fender vent details, and alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 19 inches depending on the variant.

The Holden Cascada is a two-door, four-seater soft-top convertible featuring a sweeping profile and an acoustic fabric roof that operates at speeds up to 50 km/h. Its front fascia is styled with swept-back, eagle-eye headlights flanking a trapezoidal grille adorned with a central chrome bar housing the Holden badge. The rear incorporates wraparound LED tail lights, a pronounced boot lid lip, and dual alloy wheel choices ranging up to 20-inch options on select variants. Character lines along the flanks taper dynamically toward the rear, accentuating its long, premium proportions.

The Holden Colorado RG features a rugged utility and cab-chassis body style with high-riding proportions and squared-off slab sides. Early models showcased a prominent multi-bar chrome grille flanked by angular, swept-back headlights, while the 2017 facelift introduced a sleeker front fascia with a thinner upper grille, restyled bonnet, and slim LED daytime running lights. At the rear, vertical tail light clusters frame the tailgate, which is often paired with alloy sports bars, side steps, and alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches on higher-spec variants.

The Holden VF Commodore sedan and Sportwagon feature a lower, more curvaceous and sculptural exterior design compared to their predecessor, characterized by a prominent trapezoidal grille, jewelled projector headlamps, and a power-domed bonnet. The four-door sedan and five-door wagon share identical front-end sheet metal and front fender vents, but diverge at the glasshouse and rear; the sedan adopts sweeping wrap-around tail lamps and a clean decklid with the license plate relocated to the bumper, while the wagon retains a longer roofline finishing in a flat tailgate. Depending on the variant—ranging from the base Evoke and luxury Calais to the aggressive SS and sports-oriented Redline—they feature varying alloy wheel sizes (from 16 to 20 inches), body-colored or chrome grille treatments, and subtle rear spoiler lips.

The ZB Holden Commodore features a low-slung, European-derived profile offered as a five-door liftback (fastback) and a five-door station wagon (Sportwagon). At the front, it displays a wide, chrome-accented horizontal grille flanked by sleek, angular headlamps that taper into the guards, with higher grades incorporating advanced matrix LED units. The liftback is defined by a sharply raked, fastback-style roofline flowing smoothly into an integrated tail-gate lip, while the wagon features an elongated roofline and D-pillars. The rear showcases wraparound LED tail lights, clean surfacing, and alloy wheel options ranging from 17-inch up to prominent 20-inch designs on flagship sports and luxury variants.

The Holden Equinox is a five-door mid-size SUV featuring a broad, chrome-accented dual-port front grille flanked by sharp, angled headlights with integrated LED daytime running lights. Its profile showcases a long, structured body with flowing character lines, a slightly rising beltline, and options for alloy wheels ranging up to 19 inches. The rear is defined by wraparound horizontal tail lights, a sculpted tailgate, and a subtle roof spoiler. Higher grades also feature twin-exhaust outlets and chrome exterior trim highlights.

The Holden Spark M400 is a compact five-door hatchback featuring a tall, modern stance with hidden rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars. It sports a dual-port front grille paired with swept-back headlights and distinct lower-mounted daytime running lights. The rear is accented by an integrated roof-mounted spoiler and wraparound tail lights. It rides on either 14-inch steel or 15-inch alloy wheels, complemented by crisp character lines along its profile.

The Holden TrailBlazer RG is a rugged, five-door, seven-seat utility-based SUV featuring high-riding proportions derived from its sibling ute. Its front fascia displays a prominent dual-port grille flanked by wraparound headlights integrated with LED daytime running lights and chrome accents. The rear features wraparound tail lights (with LED elements on higher grades), a chunky bumper, and an upright tailgate carrying a full-size spare underneath or a clean surface layout. Exterior details include standard side steps, roof rails, and multi-spoke alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches.

The Holden Trax TJ is a compact five-door SUV characterized by a high greenhouse, short overhangs, and a stubby stance. Its front features a distinctive dual-port grille paired with sweeping headlights (which transitioned to sleeker projector units with integrated LED daytime running lights during its 2017 facelift). The profile exhibits pronounced muscular wheel arches clad in dark protective plastic mouldings, matching the lower bumper trim and side sills. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches, and includes a raked-forward tailgate topped by a subtle roof spoiler.

The Holden VF Ute features a two-door coupe-utility body style with a long rear tray and a longer wheelbase than its sedan sibling. Its front fascia showcases a deep trapezoidal grille with horizontal bars and a prominent chrome surround, flanked by sleek, wraparound projector headlights. The athletic stance is emphasized by flared wheel arches, side body sculpting, and alloy wheels ranging up to large-diameter performance rims. At the rear, it features integrated horizontal tail lights stretching into the tailgate, complemented by dual exhaust outlets on sports variants.

The CR generation Honda Accord sedan features a traditional three-box, four-door profile with a bold chrome grille flanked by wraparound projector headlights and integrated LED daytime running lights. Its sides are defined by a strong, rising character line running from the front guard through the door handles toward the tail, complemented by a sloping roofline and multi-spoke alloy wheels. The rear showcases wide, angular tail lights extending onto the bootlid and a clean, sculpted bumper layout.

The CV-generation Honda Accord is a low-slung, four-door fastback-style sedan with a coupe-like roofline and wide stance. It features a prominent chrome wing grille flanked by sleek, angular LED headlights, sitting above a sculpted lower bumper. The rear showcases distinctive C-shaped, crab-claw horizontal LED tail lights that wrap into the boot lid. It rides on multi-spoke alloy wheels and includes a power sunroof on upper trims.

The eleventh-generation Honda Accord is a low-slung, four-door fastback-style sedan featuring a long hood and a smooth, sloping roofline. It is styled with a wide, hexagonal mesh grille flanked by slim, horizontal LED headlights. The rear incorporates a clean decklid with a sharp integrated spoiler lip and full-width connected LED tail lights. It rides on multi-spoke alloy wheels and features minimal body creases to accentuate its clean, aerodynamic proportions.

The sixth-generation Honda City sedan features a compact four-door body with an angular profile, sculpted side character lines, and a sloping roofline. Its front fascia is highlighted by a bold, prominent chrome grille strip that merges directly into angular segmented headlamps, complemented by LED daytime running lights. The rear exhibits wraparound tail lights connected across the boot lid, riding on either 15-inch or 16-inch alloy wheels alongside a roof-mounted shark-fin antenna.

The tenth-generation Honda Civic features a low-slung, aggressive stance with a fastback-style sloping roofline for both the four-door sedan and five-door hatchback variants. The front end is defined by a prominent chrome or gloss-black wing grille flanked by angular LED headlights and C-shaped daytime running lamps. The hatchback features a shorter rear overhang with dual upper and lower spoilers and distinct C-shaped tail lights, while the sedan adopts a traditional trunk profile with boomerang-shaped rear light clusters. Alloy wheel designs range up to 18 inches on sportier variants, accompanied by sharp body creases and pronounced wheel arches.

The eleventh-generation Honda Civic liftback features a sleek, fastback-inspired five-door body style with clean, flowing character lines and a low-slung stance. The front end displays slim, rectangular LED headlights flanking a wide, low honeycomb mesh grille. At the rear, it incorporates wraparound LED tail lights connected by a horizontal light element, complemented by a practical liftback tailgate and a subtle integrated rear spoiler. It rides on large 18-inch alloy wheels and features a clean roofline ending in a shark-fin antenna.

The Honda Civic Type R FK2 is an aggressive 5-door hatchback featuring a low-slung, wedge-like profile with hidden rear door handles. It sports a sharp front splitter with red accents, deep lower air dams, and a vented aluminium hood scoop. The rear is dominated by a prominent, looping rear wing, vortex generators above the rear window, and quad tailpipes protruding from a pronounced rear diffuser. It rides on large low-profile alloy wheels framed by flared wheel arches.

The FK8 Honda Civic Type R features an aggressive 5-door hatchback body with a low-slung, wedge-like silhouette, flared wheel arches, and carbon-fiber-effect aerodynamic splitters. It is dominated by a sharp front fascia with angular LED headlights, a wide lower grille intake, and a prominent rear wing complemented by a triple-exit central exhaust system. The stance is completed by large 20-inch black alloy wheels wrapped in low-profile performance tyres and vortex generators trailing along the rear roofline.

The FL5 Honda Civic Type R features a low-slung, aggressive 5-door hatchback body with flared front and rear guards that create a wide, muscular stance. It showcases a mesh grille flanked by sleek LED headlights, a vented aluminum bonnet, and functional front fender air outlets. At the rear, it is distinguished by a prominent rear wing mounted on die-cast aluminum stanchions and a central triple-exhaust configuration nestled in a lower diffuser, riding on matte black 19-inch alloy wheels.

The fourth-generation Honda CR-V features a compact, five-door SUV body with an upright stance, large glass areas, and a slightly lower, more aerodynamic roofline than its predecessor. The front fascia is highlighted by a horizontal multi-bar chrome grille flanked by deeply set, wraparound halogen or projector headlights. At the rear, it retains signature vertical, high-mounted tail lights climbing the D-pillars. The exterior is accented by pronounced wheel arches, alloy wheels (typically 17-inch or 18-inch depending on the variant), and an integrated rear tailgate spoiler.

The fifth-generation Honda CR-V features a muscular, athletic five-door medium SUV stance with a longer hood, prominent wheel arches, and a short rear overhang. The front end is defined by a bold chrome wing grille flanked by sharp LED headlights accented by signature daytime running light arrays. At the rear, it sports distinctive, hook-shaped LED tail lights that wrap into the D-pillars, alongside a roof spoiler and dual exhaust outlets. The profile is accented by multi-spoke alloy wheels and integrated roof rails, while higher grades feature a hands-free power tailgate.

The sixth-generation Honda CR-V features an angular, upright medium SUV body with a clean profile and a long bonnet. The flagship RS variant is distinguished by a bold gloss-black grille, matching black door handles, mirror caps, and wheel-arch cladding. It rides on 19-inch black or machined alloy wheels and includes a panoramic sunroof. The front end features slim LED headlights flanking the mesh grille, while the rear showcases vertical L-shaped tail lights framing a hands-free power tailgate. Inside, the cabin features dark headlining, alloy sports pedals, and leather-appointed seats with contrasting red stitching.

The first-generation Honda HR-V features a compact, coupe-inspired SUV body style with a sloping roofline and hidden rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars. The front fascia showcases a prominent chrome or gloss-black grille wing stretching into angular headlights. The rear end is defined by wraparound tail lights and a heavily raked tailgate. Alloy wheels and a rising side character line accentuate its forward-leaning stance.

The third-generation Honda HR-V features a sleek, coupe-inspired compact SUV body with a steeply raked roofline and hidden flush rear door handles. It is characterized by a clean, minimalist front fascia sporting slim LED headlights flanking a body-colored or gloss-black integrated grille. The rear profile is defined by a continuous, full-width LED light bar spanning the tailgate. It rides on prominent 18-inch alloy wheels and features a clean silhouette with minimal body cladding.

The GK-generation Honda Jazz is a 5-door hatchback featuring a cab-forward silhouette, short overhangs, and an angular, wedge-like profile. Its front fascia incorporates a high-gloss black grille seamlessly blending into swept-back headlights, complemented by a sharply sculpted lower bumper. At the rear, it features tall, vertical LED-style tail lights flanking the tailgate, along with a roofline spoiler and a central fuel tank layout that maximizes interior space.

The Honda NSX (NC1) is a low-slung, two-door hybrid sports coupe featuring sharp aerodynamic lines, angular LED headlights, and a prominent front mesh grille. Its mid-engine profile is defined by aggressive side air intakes behind the doors, floating C-pillar roof details, and staggered 19-inch front and 20-inch rear alloy wheels. The rear showcases connected full-width LED tail lights above a functional lower diffuser and quad exhaust tips.

The fifth-generation Honda Odyssey adopts a traditional people-mover silhouette with a taller roofline, flat floor, and dual power-sliding rear doors. Its front fascia features a prominent, multi-slat chrome grille flanked by sleek wraparound LED headlights and distinct lower bumper chrome accents. The rear is highlighted by wide, horizontal LED tail lights that extend into the tailgate. It rides on 17-inch alloy wheels and sports an expansive glasshouse with a chrome window surround.

The Honda ZR-V medium SUV features a sleek, coupe-like five-door body style with smooth, flowing proportions and an elongated hood. The front fascia is highlighted by a distinctive low-set vertical-slat grille flanked by wide, sharp LED headlights. At the rear, it sports a sculpted tailgate with an integrated roof spoiler and wrap-around LED tail lights. The clean profile is aided by laser-brazed roof joints and door-mounted side mirrors, rolling on 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels depending on the variant.

The Gen-F HSV Clubsport sedan features a muscular, low-slung body with a distinctive twin-nostril upper grille and a wide, trapezoidal lower air dam flanked by LED daytime running lights. At the rear, it incorporates angular wrap-around LED tail lights, a subtle boot-lid spoiler, and quad exhaust outlets. It rides on 20-inch alloy wheels filling flared guards, complemented by side skirts and fender vents.

The HSV GTS sedan features an aggressive, low-slung body style with a prominent front fascia incorporating large lower air-intake openings and a subtle front splitter. It is equipped with projector headlamps, dual-function daytime running lamps, and distinctive Pitch Black accents on the side mirrors, fender vents, and window moldings. The rear is defined by a body-coloured Superflow performance spoiler with Pitch Black highlights, LED tail lamps, and quad exhaust outlets with shadow-chrome tips. It rides on 20-inch matte or satin graphite forged-alloy wheels housing multi-piston AP Racing brake calipers.

The Gen-F HSV Maloo is a two-door coupé utility featuring an aggressive front fascia with a large, low-slung trapezoidal grille opening, angular projector headlamps, and integrated LED daytime running lights. Its muscular profile is defined by flared guards, pronounced side vents, and large 20-inch alloy wheels, with higher variants incorporating a performance sail plane over the cargo bay and a hard tonneau cover. The rear features a drop-down tailgate flanked by horizontal tail lights and a lower bumper housing quad exhaust outlets.

The Gen-F HSV Senator Signature is a four-door luxury-performance sedan featuring a broad front grille opening, projector headlamps, and integrated LED daytime running lights. Its sleek profile is accented by chrome-trimmed front fender vents, chrome mirror scalps, side skirts, and large 20-inch forged alloy wheels. The rear showcases a subtle boot-lid lip spoiler, distinctive LED tail lamps, and a lower rear fascia integrated with quad exhaust outlets.

The HSV SportsCat is a dual-cab 4x4 utility featuring an aggressive, muscular front fascia with a unique gloss-black '3D' grille, integrated LED fog lamps, and prominent red recovery hooks. Its high-riding stance is accentuated by a raised front profile, chunky wheel-arch fender flares, 18-inch matte-black 6-spoke forged alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tyres, and a distinctive bonnet bulge on higher specs. The rear is styled with a lockable hard tonneau cover, a sports bar or sail plane, and a bold 'COLORADO' tailgate appliqué.

The Hyundai Accent RB sedan features a compact four-door body style characterized by fluid, coupe-like roofline proportions and a prominent deep trunk. It incorporates swept-back angular headlights framing a hexagonal front grille, along with wraparound horizontal tail lights. Depending on the specification, the exterior is finished with alloy wheel options and clean body-side character lines.

The sixth-generation Hyundai Elantra sedan features a four-door fastback-inspired profile with clean, sweeping character lines along its flanks. At the front, it showcases a wide hexagonal grille flanked by elongated, wraparound headlights. The rear features wraparound tail lights stretching onto the boot lid, complemented by multi-spoke alloy wheel designs.

The Hyundai Elexio features a modern, five-door medium crossover SUV body style characterized by clean surfaces, flush pop-out door handles, and aerodynamic proportions. It incorporates full-width LED light bars on both the front and rear fascia, with the rear light bar featuring subtle downward curvatures at the edges. The front end adopts a smooth, closed-off panel look typical of contemporary electric vehicles, complemented by angular lower bumper geometry. Inside, the minimalist dashboard is anchored by an ultra-thin 27-inch widescreen display unit.

The Hyundai Genesis DH sedan features a large, imposing chrome hexagonal front grille flanked by sleek wraparound projector headlights and LED daytime running lights. Its stately four-door proportions include a long wheelbase, short front and rear overhangs, and a coupe-like sloping roofline flowing into a short boot lid. The rear end is characterized by wide, horizontal LED tail lights, dual chrome exhaust tips, and multi-spoke alloy wheels filling the arches.

The GB-generation Hyundai i20 is a five-door hatchback featuring a contemporary, European-influenced silhouette with balanced proportions and a distinctively blacked-out C-pillar that creates a floating roof effect. The front fascia showcases a wide hexagonal cascading grille flanked by swept-back wraparound headlights, while the rear features horizontal tail lights extending into the tailgate. It rides on compact alloy or steel wheels and incorporates clean character lines along its profile.

The Hyundai i20 N features a compact 5-door hatchback body with a low-slung, aggressive stance and sharp angular lines. At the front, it has a wide chequered-flag patterned grille merging with sleek LED headlights, complemented by a prominent front splitter and side skirts accented in tomato red. The rear profile is dominated by a distinct WRC-inspired roof spoiler, dark-tinted LED tail lights, and a lower bumper diffuser housing a single oval exhaust tip. It rides on 18-inch matte grey alloy wheels revealing signature red N brake callipers, with optional contrast roof finishes available.

The GD-generation Hyundai i30 hatchback features a five-door layout designed with fluid, coupe-like proportions and a swept-back profile. It is highlighted by a prominent hexagonal front grille, sharply angled wraparound headlights, and rising character lines along the flanks. The rear exhibits wraparound horizontal tail lights, a sloping roofline ending in an integrated rear spoiler, and alloy or steel wheel options depending on the spec.

The Hyundai i30 PD hatchback is a five-door, front-wheel-drive small car featuring a clean, cab-backward silhouette and a sloping roofline. The front end is dominated by a cascading or wider 3D-pattern mesh grille flanked by sleek projector headlamps and distinctive V-shaped LED daytime running lights. The rear sports wraparound tail lights, a roof spoiler, and a contoured bumper. Depending on the specification, it rides on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 19 inches, with sportier variants featuring aggressive body kits, side skirts, and dual exhaust outlets.

The Hyundai i30 Sedan features a distinctive fastback-style four-door body with an aggressive, wedge-shaped stance and complex geometric body creases. It showcases a wide parametric grille that integrates sharply angled LED headlights, paired with a sloping roofline that flows cleanly into a short boot lid. The rear is highlighted by a full-width light bar featuring an H-shaped graphic signature connecting the tail lights. Wheel options range from 16-inch alloys up to aggressive 19-inch rims on performance variants.

The Hyundai i40 sedan features a four-door 'fluidic sculpture' body style characterized by a coupe-like, sweeping roofline and an ascending beltline. It has a prominent hexagonal front grille framed by sharply swept-back headlamps featuring integrated LED daytime running lights. The side profile is defined by a distinct character crease running from the front wheel arches to the wrap-around tail lights. Depending on the spec, it sits on 16- or 18-inch alloy wheels and features twin exhaust tips at the rear.

The Hyundai iLoad TQ van features a semi-bonneted, boxy commercial body style with a long 3,200mm wheelbase and short overhangs. It is configured with dual sliding side doors and a choice of a top-hinged liftback tailgate or optional twin-swing barn doors at the rear. The front end is defined by a swept-back wraparound headlight design flanking a prominent grille—updated across its lifecycle to feature a deeper profile with a chrome surround. It rides on 16-inch steel wheels and features high-mounted vertical tail lamps at the rear corners.

The Hyundai iMax TQ generation is a boxy, rear-wheel-drive five-door people mover featuring a cab-over design with a sloping front windscreen and a long wheelbase. It incorporates large rectangular wraparound headlights framing a prominent multi-bar or mesh grille, dual sliding side doors, and a top-hinged liftback tailgate at the rear flanked by tall vertical tail lights. Exterior enhancements across its lifecycle included 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels, front bumper fog light integrations, and a roof-mounted rear aerial.

The Hyundai Inster (generation AX1) is a compact, high-riding small electric SUV featuring a short, boxy silhouette with upright proportions and a wide track. Its distinctive front fascia incorporates circular LED headlights, pixelated turn signals, and a circuit board-style textured bumper. The rear features matching pixel-graphic lighting elements, while the rugged Inster Cross variant adds 17-inch alloy wheels, prominent black body cladding, and optional roof accessories. Flush touch-sensor door handles and a flat roofline complete its modern, tech-forward urban styling.

The Hyundai Ioniq AE hatchback features an aerodynamic, wedge-shaped liftback profile with a sweeping roofline and a tapered tail. It has a smooth face with a low-slung grille flanked by distinctive LED daytime running lights, and wraparound tail lights split by the rear glass window. The exterior sits on alloy wheels and incorporates active aerodynamic flaps on hybrid variants to minimize drag.

The Hyundai Ioniq 5 is a medium five-door crossover SUV featuring retro-futuristic proportions that mimic a large hatchback with a long wheelbase. Its angular body showcases sharp parametric pixel LED headlights and matching rectangular rear tail lights, flush automatic door handles, and a clamshell bonnet. The exterior profile is distinguished by bold geometric side creases, flared wheel arches, and large aerodynamic alloy wheels (ranging from 19 to 21 inches depending on the variant) alongside an available fixed glass panoramic roof.

The Hyundai Ioniq 6 is a four-door 'streamliner' sedan featuring an ultra-low, swooping arch-like roofline and a low-slung nose optimized for aerodynamics. The front fascia incorporates rectangular pixel-style LED headlights flanking a smooth bumper with active air flaps, while the rear showcases a distinctive dual-spoiler setup including a transparent 'whale tail' and a ducktail lip integrated with a full-width pixel LED light bar. It features flush-fitting pop-out door handles, clean body sides, and comes with either aerodynamic 18-inch alloy wheels or larger 20-inch wheels depending on the grade.

The Hyundai Ioniq 9 is a large, boxy electric SUV featuring a smooth, arching 'aerosthetic' roofline and a long wheelbase.
