Its front and rear fascias are defined by distinctive Parametric Pixel LED light graphics, incorporating cube-shaped projection headlights. It is equipped with auto-flush pop-out door handles, sculpted wheel arches, and rides on large alloy wheels up to 21 inches in size. Notably, the exterior design eliminates traditional roof antennas by distributing their functions across the glass and dashboard.

The first-generation Hyundai Kona features a compact, chunky five-door small SUV body style with high-riding proportions and heavily contoured side crease lines. It is characterized by a distinctive split-headlight design, featuring slim upper LED daytime running lights sitting above cascading main headlight clusters flanking a wide cascading grille. The rear features wrap-around tail lights paired with prominent lower plastic bumper cladding and protective body armour trim. Available wheel designs range up to 18-inch alloys, complementing a sloping roofline accented by a subtle rear tailgate spoiler.

The second-generation Hyundai Kona features a futuristic five-door small SUV body style with a noticeably longer, more aerodynamic stance and sculpted geometric body panels. Its fascia is dominated by a distinctive, full-width horizontal 'Seamless Horizon' LED DRL strip running above a low-mounted main headlight assembly. The rear mirrors this futuristic lighting signature with a full-width LED tail light bar. Variants like the N Line incorporate sportier body-colored cladding, aggressive bumpers, and larger 19-inch alloy wheels.

The Hyundai Nexo medium SUV features a streamlined, aerodynamic body with flush electronic door handles and a floating roofline. The front end is defined by a cascading grille, a continuous thin LED light bar running above it, and separate triangular headlight clusters. The rear incorporates triangular tail lights, a full-width visual layout, and a prominent roof spoiler that conceals the rear wiper. It sits on aerodynamic alloy wheels and includes D-pillar air ducts designed to reduce drag.

The Hyundai Palisade LX2 is a large five-door SUV featuring a commanding, boxy stance with a high bonnet and expansive panoramic side glass. Up front, it showcases a massive cascading grille flanked by stacked vertical LED headlight configurations. The rear incorporates distinct, vertically oriented tail lights and a clean tailgate design. It rides on large multi-spoke alloy wheels, complemented by structured character lines along its substantial profile.

The DM-generation Hyundai Santa Fe is a large, five-door SUV styled with Hyundai's 'Fluidic Sculpture' design language, featuring flowing body lines and a rising beltline. The front fascia is dominated by a hexagonal chrome grille flanked by sharply swept-back wrap-around headlights. The rear showcases wraparound horizontal tail lights, a sculpted tailgate, and a lower bumper incorporating dual exhaust outlets. It sits on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches depending on the specification, with a heavily raked greenhouse profile distinguishing its seven-seat proportions.

The TM generation Hyundai Santa Fe is a large, five-door seven-seater SUV featuring a flowing, rugged body style with prominent character lines along its profile. It features a wide cascading grille flanked by distinct composite headlights, highlighted by upper slim LED daytime running lights. The rear showcases wraparound tail lights connected across the tailgate by a slim reflector or light bar. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 20 inches and includes squared-off wheel arches, with higher grades offering body-coloured lower cladding.

The Hyundai Santa Fe MX5 features a boxy, angular large SUV silhouette defined by a high bonnet, flat roofline, and an upright, vertical tailgate. It incorporates distinctive H-shaped LED headlamps linked by a horizontal light bar across a bold front fascia. The rear end is characterized by low-mounted H-signature taillights spanning the wide-opening tailgate. Distinctive profile details include pronounced squared-off wheel arches housing large alloy wheels, flush roof rails, and an expansive greenhouse with hidden-type assist grips on the C-pillars.

The seventh-generation Hyundai Sonata is a four-door, fastback-style medium sedan featuring a clean, coupe-like roofline and confident side character lines. It is fronted by a prominent hexagonal chrome grille flanked by sleek, wraparound headlights, which transitioned to sharper, more angular clusters following its mid-life refresh. The rear incorporates horizontal LED tail lights, while the profile is completed by multi-spoke alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches in diameter.

The Hyundai Sonata DN8 is a low-slung, four-door fastback sedan featuring a sweeping coupe-like roofline and aggressive aerodynamic proportions. The front fascia is defined by a wide mesh grille and a distinct full-width horizontal LED 'Seamless Horizon Lamp' incorporating hidden projector headlamps. At the rear, it sports a continuous H-light LED tail light strip above a trunk lid lip spoiler and quad-exhaust tips. It rides on large 19-inch alloy wheels and includes a panoramic glass sunroof.

The Hyundai Staria people mover features a futuristic, spaceship-like monobox body shape with a steeply raked windshield and a continuous horizontal LED daytime running light bar spanning the front fascia. Its low-slung front grille houses wide, low-mounted LED headlights, while the side profile is defined by an expansive glasshouse and dual sliding doors. The rear features a broad vertical tailgate integrated with large, pixel-style vertical or parametric-pixel tail light clusters.

The Hyundai Staria Load features a futuristic, wedge-shaped one-box van body with a steeply raked windscreen and short front overhang. The front end is defined by a wide, low-set grille flanked by distinct, vertically stacked low-mount LED headlights and a full-width LED daytime running light bar. Profile details include large side glass areas, dual sliding side doors, and 17-inch steel or alloy wheels, while the rear features a high-roof profile with vertical pixel-style tail lights and a choice of either a top-hinged liftback tailgate or twin barn-style swing doors.

The third-generation Hyundai Tucson features a five-door medium SUV body style with a planted, athletic stance and flowing shoulder lines. The front end is dominated by a prominent hexagonal grille flanked by swept-back headlights with integrated LED accents. The rear profile showcases clean horizontal lines, wraparound slim tail lights, and a subtle roof spoiler. Depending on the specification grade, it rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches and features a structured, aerodynamic silhouette.

The Hyundai Tucson NX4 features a distinctive medium SUV body style characterized by sharp, geometric body creases and muscular wheel arches. Its front end is dominated by a parametric jewel-pattern grille that seamlessly integrates hidden geometric daytime running lights. The rear showcases full-width connected tail lights featuring half-hidden triangular signature elements beneath a clean, modern tailgate design.

The first-generation Hyundai Veloster features a low-slung, coupe-like hatchback profile characterized by a unique asymmetrical door layout—one long door on the driver's side and two smaller doors on the passenger side. It showcases a large hexagonal front grille, swept-back wraparound headlights, and prominent wheel arches typically housing 18-inch alloy wheels. The rear exhibits a sloping roofline blending into a rounded tailgate, wraparound tail lights, and a central dual-exhaust setup on turbocharged variants.

The second-generation Hyundai Veloster features an asymmetrical three-door hatchback layout with a single door on the driver's side and two doors on the passenger side. It has a low-slung, sporty stance characterized by a sweeping fastback roofline, a large cascading hexagonal front grille, and sharp LED headlamps. The rear showcases wraparound taillights, a prominent bumper diffuser, and a centrally mounted dual-exhaust setup on turbo models.

The Hyundai Venue features a boxy, compact small SUV body style with a high-set, upright stance and four doors. The front end is characterized by a prominent cascading mesh grille flanked by a split-lighting setup, incorporating square-framed main headlamps encircled by LED daytime running lights. At the rear, it features rectangular LED combination tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and a chunky bumper design. Exterior details include standard roof rails, squared-off wheel arches with protective cladding, alloy wheel options up to 17 inches, and available two-tone contrasting roof paint finishes on select grades.

The IM Motors IM5 is a sleek, low-slung electric liftback featuring a smooth fastback roofline, a subtle ducktail spoiler, and flush-fitting door handles. Its front fascia is defined by sweeping, angular LED headlights flanking a smooth, closed-off nose with lower aerodynamic intakes. The rear features a distinctive continuous light bar combined with a sharp, curved tailgate contour. It rides on large alloy wheels with aerodynamic inserts, complemented by a pillarless glass roof profile.

The first-generation IM Motors IM6 is a sleek, mid-to-large coupe-SUV featuring a flowing silhouette, a low sloping roofline, and an aerodynamic stance. It is equipped with four doors, frameless side glass, and flush pop-out door handles. The front fascia is defined by sharp T-shaped LED headlights paired with a semi-enclosed lower intake, while the rear showcases a full-width LED light bar alongside a subtle ducktail spoiler.

The Ineos Grenadier features a utilitarian, flat-panel boxy body style with a prominent upright grille flanked by round LED headlights. It has five doors, a high-set squared-off roofline with integrated roof protection strips, and external body side-protection rub rails. The rear utilizes asymmetric 30/70 split swing-out doors holding a full-size spare wheel mounted centrally.

The Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster is a utilitarian, boxy dual-cab ute featuring a flat-sided galvanised steel body, upright windscreen, and an extended wheelbase over its wagon sibling to accommodate a rear cargo tray. It shares a prominent, rounded front fascia highlighted by circular LED headlights flanking a squarish grille inset with auxiliary high-beam spot lamps. The rear features practical rectangular tail lights and a full-size spare wheel mounted to the tailgate or cargo structure. Exterior details include chunky exterior protection strips, roof rails, flat side-hinged rear or tailgate configurations, and heavy-duty alloy or steel wheels.

The Infiniti Q30 is a five-door hatchback featuring a raised, crossover-like stance with flowing, highly sculpted body panels and pronounced muscular haunches. The front end is dominated by a sweeping mesh double-arch grille flanked by sharply swept-back headlights with LED daytime running lights. Its profile showcases a distinctive, kinked C-pillar design with a chrome window surround, tapering down towards a sloping roofline. The rear is characterized by wraparound tail lights, a sculpted tailgate, and dual exhaust tips set beneath a sporty bumper arrangement.

The Infiniti Q50 V37 is a four-door mid-size sedan featuring a flowing, sculpted body style with fluid character lines and a distinctive crescent-cut C-pillar. It is styled with a prominent three-dimensional double-arch front grille flanked by swept-back, sharp LED headlights. The rear incorporates slim, wraparound LED combination taillights and dual exhaust tips. Depending on the specification, it rides on 17-inch to 19-inch alloy wheels and features a low-slung, athletic stance with a steeply raked windshield.

The Infiniti Q60 coupe features a low-slung, fastback two-door body style with athletic proportions and flowing, deeply sculpted character lines. The front end is defined by a prominent mesh double-arch grille flanked by slender, sharp LED headlights featuring signature daytime running lights. At the rear, it has horizontal LED tail lights, dual exhaust outlets, and a short decklid. The exterior is finished with alloy wheels up to 20 inches in diameter and distinctive crescent-cut C-pillars.

The Infiniti Q70 Y51 luxury sedan features a curvaceous, aerodynamic four-door body with fluid, flowing proportions, a low-slung bonnet, and a high waistline. Up front, it showcases a prominent double-arch mesh or wave-styled grille flanked by swept-back, crystal-look LED headlights. The rear is defined by wraparound LED tail lights, a clean boot lid with a chrome accent finisher, and dual exhaust outlets. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18-inch multi-spoke designs to sportier 20-inch options, complemented by flared wheel arches and a coupe-like teardrop roofline.

The Infiniti QX30 (H15) is a compact five-door crossover SUV featuring a high-riding stance, a coupe-like low-slung roofline, and a raised ground clearance. Its exterior is defined by deep, undulating character lines along the body sides and a distinctive crescent-shaped C-pillar. The front end showcases Infiniti's signature double-arch grille flanked by sharp, eye-inspired LED headlights, while the rear incorporates wrapped tail lamps, dual rectangular exhaust outlets, and a roof spoiler. It rides on 18-inch alloy wheels complemented by rugged, grained wheel arch moldings and satin chrome-plated body inserts.

The Infiniti QX70 features a distinctive, coupe-like large luxury SUV body style with a long bonnet, a sweeping roofline, and muscular rear haunches. It is styled with a prominent, double-arch front grille flanked by swept-back bi-xenon headlights and prominent fender-mounted chrome or dark chrome air vents. The rear showcases wraparound LED tail lights and dual exhaust finishers, riding on large multi-spoke alloy wheels up to 21 inches in size.

The Infiniti QX80 Y62 is a massive, imposing five-door luxury SUV characterized by bulky, muscular proportions and a towering stance. Up front, it features a prominent chrome double-arch grille flanked by swept-back, eye-inspired LED headlights and a high-set clamshell bonnet. The side profile is defined by chrome fender vents, integrated side steps, and large 22-inch alloy wheels. The rear showcases a broad chrome tailgate strip, a subtle roof spoiler, and wraparound horizontal tail lights.

The second-generation Isuzu D-Max (RT) pickup truck features a high-riding, muscular stance available in single-cab, space-cab, and dual-cab body styles. It is characterized by a prominent, rectangular-themed front grille—often heavily chromed or dark grey depending on the trim—flanked by swept-back angular headlights that received sharper projector and LED daytime running light updates during its production lifecycle. The rear features stacked vertical tail lights set against a utilitarian tailgate, complemented by flared wheel arches and distinct shoulder lines running along its flanks.

The Isuzu D-Max dual-cab and single-cab pickup features a muscular, high-riding stance with prominent flared wheel arches and a chiseled profile. The front end showcases a bold horizontal-bar grille flanked by sharply angled LED headlamps, complemented by a sculpted bonnet with prominent creases. At the rear, it features stacked three-tier LED tail-lights and a flat-topped tailgate, riding on robust alloy or steel wheel options depending on the model grade.

The first-generation Isuzu MU-X is a large, five-door, body-on-frame SUV with a rugged, high-riding stance sharing its foundational front-end architecture with the D-Max utility. It features a prominent chrome-accented front grille flanked by swept-back projector headlights, alongside a tall, utilitarian glasshouse and side steps. The rear is characterised by wrap-around tail lights and a bulkier tailgate profile. Depending on the specification tier, it rides on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches, complemented by subtle roof rails and a muscular, rounded body shape.

The second-generation Isuzu MU-X is a large, five-door, seven-seat SUV characterized by rounded, muscular body proportions and flared wheel arches. The front fascia features a prominent, multi-slanted horizontal grille flanked by swept-back Bi-LED headlights integrated with sharp LED daytime running lights. At the rear, it has wrap-around LED tail lights connected visually across a clean tailgate, paired with a roof-mounted spoiler. Depending on the variant, the exterior sits on 17-inch, 18-inch, or 20-inch alloy wheels, and includes functional side steps and roof rails.

The JAC Hunter PHEV dual-cab ute features a muscular, high-riding body style with prominent, square proportions. Its front fascia is dominated by a bold, dark grille flanked by modern split-type LED headlights and thick-walled sequential turn signals. The rear is defined by vertical LED tail-lights framing a practical tray equipped with an integrated sports bar and roof rails. Exterior details include 18-inch alloy wheels, blue-accented badging specific to the plug-in hybrid variant, and robust body cladding.

The JAC T9 is a four-door dual-cab ute featuring a bold, squared-off front fascia dominated by a massive, high-mounted grille with prominent block lettering and split-level LED headlights. Its high-riding body proportions include flared wheel arches housing alloy wheels, squared-off side windows, and body-colored side cladding. At the rear, it features vertical LED tail lights flanking the tailgate, alongside roof rails and side steps fitted as standard.

The first-generation Jaecoo J5 is a boxy, upright compact SUV featuring a five-door layout and clean, rugged proportions reminiscent of a shrunken Land Rover. Petrol and hybrid variants showcase a prominent vertical-slat waterfall grille flanked by sharp LED projector headlights, while the EV variant substitutes this with a smooth, closed-off front fascia. The rear end is characterized by a full-width LED light bar connecting dark-tinted tail light housings. It rides on 18-inch aerodynamic alloy wheels and offers a suspended floating roof design alongside an optional expansive panoramic glass roof.

The Jaecoo J7 is a boxy, medium-sized five-door SUV defined by upright proportions, clean slab-sided body panels, and flush-fitting electric door handles. The front features a prominent vertical waterfall-style grille flanked by split-level headlights with distinctive matrix daytime running signatures. At the rear, full-width LED tail lights incorporate a vertical block graphic element that mirrors the front lighting design. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 inches upward, complemented by a flat roofline and a subtle rear spoiler.

The first-generation Jaecoo J8 large SUV features a robust 5-door body with clean, minimal 3D surfaces and a prominent rounded waterfall-style front grille. It is flanked by sleek projector-style LED headlights paired with sweeping daytime running lights. The rear showcases a full-width LED tail light bar with integrated lettering, while the side profile is anchored by large 20-inch machine-finished alloy wheels and a smooth roofline.

The first-generation Jaguar E-Pace is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a low, coupe-like roofline, a sculpted bonnet, and muscular rear haunches. The front end is dominated by a mesh-pattern grille flanked by swept-back headlights, while the rear showcases slim LED tail lights. It rides on prominent alloy wheels ranging up to 21 inches and incorporates playful design easter eggs, such as a tiny graphic of a Jaguar and cub on the corner of the windscreen.

The first-generation Jaguar F-Pace is a luxury performance SUV featuring an athletic stance, a prominent mesh front grille, and slim LED headlights with signature double 'J'-blade daytime running lights. Its side profile highlights a sweeping roofline, short front overhangs, and prominent alloy wheel options ranging up to large diameters. The rear end is characterized by slim chicane-effect LED tail lights and an integrated bumper with dual exhaust finishes.

The Jaguar F-Type is available as a sleek two-door coupe and a soft-top convertible featuring traditional long-hood, short-deck sports car proportions and muscular rear haunches. Early models feature a prominent clamshell bonnet, an oval front grille, and swept-back bi-Xenon headlights, while later updates transition to ultra-slim horizontal LED headlamps and a widened grille. The rear is characterized by wrap-around horizontal or curved LED tail lights, flush deployable door handles, and either twin-center or quad outboard-mounted exhaust pipes. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches, complementing its low-slung, aerodynamically sculpted aluminium body.

The Jaguar I-Pace features a distinct cab-forward SUV silhouette with a sweeping, coupé-like roofline and short overhangs. It includes a bold rectangular grille insert, slim LED headlights with signature double-J daytime running lights, and a prominent bonnet scoop. The rear showcases a sloping tailgate with a sharp ducktail spoiler and narrow, wraparound LED tail lights. Signature details comprise flush door handles, muscular rear haunches, a full-length fixed panoramic glass roof, and large alloy wheels ranging up to 22 inches.

The Jaguar XE is a compact four-door sedan featuring a low-slung, coupe-like profile with a long bonnet and short rear deck. It has a prominent mesh grille flanked by sleek LED headlights featuring distinctive 'J-blade' daytime running light signatures. The rear exhibits horizontal LED tail lights that wrap into the quarter panels, accentuating its planted stance. Riding on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches, its aluminum-intensive bodywork incorporates clean, aerodynamic surfacing.

The Jaguar XF (X260) features a sleek, low-slung aluminum-intensive body available as a four-door sedan (saloon) and a five-door estate (Sportbrake). It is characterized by a prominent mesh grille, slender LED headlights with distinctive 'J-blade' or 'Double J' daytime running lights, and a flowing coupe-like roofline. The rear sports wraparound LED tail lights connected by clean surfacing, while upper trims feature aerodynamic bumper styling, side fender vents with the Jaguar Leaper emblem, and stylish alloy wheels.

The Jaguar XJ X351 is a low-slung, four-door luxury sedan featuring a prominent, upright mesh grille flanked by sleek, wraparound headlights with distinctive 'J-Blade' LED daytime running lights. Its elongated silhouette is defined by a sweeping coupe-like roofline, wrap-around rear glass, and dark C-pillar sections designed to conceal the car's width. At the rear, it sports distinctive vertical 'cat's claw' LED tail lights, dual exhaust tips, and large alloy wheels typically ranging from 19 to 20 inches.

The Jeep Cherokee KL is a 5-door compact crossover wagon featuring a streamlined, rounded profile with sculpted body lines and a distinctive split-level front fascia, housing slim upper daytime running lights above prominent main headlights flanking a signature seven-slot grille. At the rear, it features wraparound LED tail lights, a roof spoiler, and a sculpted tailgate. The stance varies from clean city-focused alloy wheel designs on standard variants to beefier rugged body cladding, raised suspension, and red tow hooks on the Trailhawk model.

The MK Jeep Compass is a 5-door compact SUV featuring a boxy, wagon-like stance with squared-off wheel arches. Early models feature distinctive round headlights flanking a classic seven-slot grille, while 2011 and later facelift versions adopt a scaled-down Grand Cherokee fascia with rectangular projector headlights and a cleaner grille design. The side profile includes rear door handles integrated into the C-pillar frames, and the rear features wraparound rectangular tail lights and a tailgate-mounted spoiler. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches and is equipped with standard black roof rails.

The Jeep Compass features a compact 5-door SUV body with rounded rectangular wheel arches and a strong horizontal shoulder line. The front fascia is defined by a signature seven-slot vertical grille flanked by slim LED headlamps. Rear styling includes wraparound tail lights, a raked rear hatch window, and a sculpted bumper. Available details across variants include contrast-painted black roofs, underbody skid plates, and alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches.

The Jeep Gladiator dual-cab ute features rugged, boxy proportions built on an extended Wrangler platform, complete with a distinctive vertical seven-slot front grille flanked by round headlights. It showcases a fold-down windscreen, fully removable doors, and a modular three-piece hardtop. The rear features a utilitarian steel bed with a tailgate and square tail lights, riding on 17-inch alloy wheels fitted with chunky all-terrain tyres.

The Jeep Grand Cherokee WK2 features a muscular 5-door wagon body with a squared-off stance and trapezoidal wheel arches. It is defined by a signature seven-slot front grille flanked by sleek, wraparound headlights and a chunky bumper assembly. The rear features wide horizontal tail lights and a sculpted tailgate, complemented by clean roof rails and alloy wheel options ranging from 18 to 20 inches.

The Jeep Grand Cherokee WL is offered in both a standard 5-door wagon and an extended 7-door wagon (Grand Cherokee L). It features a boxy, squared-off silhouette with an upright front fascia, a wide signature seven-slot grille, and slim horizontal LED headlights. The rear incorporates sleek, wraparound LED tail lights connected by a dark trim element, while upper trims feature color-coded or black wheel arch flares sitting above large alloy wheels.

The Jeep Patriot features a boxy, traditional upright 5-door SUV body style reminiscent of classic Jeep designs, characterized by flat panels and a high beltline. The front fascia is dominated by a signature seven-bar vertical grille flanked by distinct round headlights and a squared-off bumper. At the rear, it has an upright tailgate flanked by simple, rectangular vertical tail lamps and a chunky rear bumper. Its profile showcases squared wheel arches, a flat roofline typically equipped with rails, and multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Jeep Renegade BU features a boxy, upright five-door SUV stance with a flat roofline and muscular proportions. It is characterized by a signature seven-slot front grille flanked by round headlights, squared-off wheel arches, and distinctive tail lights housing an integrated 'X' military-fuel-can motif. Depending on the model variant, it sits on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches and offers rugged black plastic lower body cladding.

The Jeep Wrangler JK features a boxy, utilitarian body style available as a short-wheelbase 2-door or a stretched 4-door Unlimited variant. It features an iconic vertical seven-slot grille flanked by round headlights, flat fender flares, and exposed exterior door hinges. The rear is characterised by a side-hinged tailgate carrying a full-sized spare wheel and upright rectangular tail lights. It is configured with removable doors, a fold-flat windshield, and choices of a fabric soft-top or a modular three-piece hardtop.

The Jeep Wrangler JL features an iconic, boxy off-road stance available in both compact 2-door and elongated 4-door body styles with removable doors, a fold-down windshield, and soft-top or hard-top convertible configurations. The front end is characterized by a signature vertical seven-slot grille (with a slight historical bend) flanked by round LED headlights that curve into the outer fenders. At the rear, it features square tail lights, an external spare wheel mounted to a side-hinged tailgate, and chunky fender flares housing rugged alloy wheels beneath a flat-topped roof.

The third-generation Kia Carnival features a chiselled, SUV-inspired people-mover body with a cab-forward profile, a lower roofline, and a distinctive tapering rear side window line. It is fronted by Kia's signature 'tiger-nose' grille flanked by swept-back headlights with available LED daytime running lights. The rear presents a clean, squared-off hatch design with contemporary wrap-around tail lights and an integrated roof spoiler. Alloy wheels and sliding side doors complete its functional yet modern profile.

The fourth-generation Kia Carnival is a large five-door people mover featuring SUV-inspired proportions, a long wheelbase, and a prominent 'tiger nose' grille integrated with sleek headlights. It features a distinctive textured C-pillar chrome fin that visually separates the cabin roofline from the body, sliding rear doors, and a full-width LED tail light bar across the tailgate. The exterior rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 19 inches, with the updated models incorporating vertical-oriented lighting signatures and revised front and rear fascia designs.

The third-generation Kia Cerato features a European-inspired low-slung stance available as a sleek four-door sedan and a rounded five-door hatchback. It showcases swept-back wrap-around headlights flanking Kia's signature 'tiger-nose' grille, complemented by a steeply raked windshield and a flowing roofline. The rear incorporates wraparound tail light clusters, with higher-spec trims riding on 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels.

The fourth-generation Kia Cerato is available as a fastback-styled four-door sedan and a five-door hatchback, featuring a sleek, cab-backward silhouette with a long bonnet and swept-back roofline. The front end is anchored by Kia's signature 'tiger-nose' grille flanked by sharp, angular headlamps with available distinctive LED daytime running light signatures. The rear showcases wraparound tail lights—connected across the boot lid on higher spec variants—and a sporty lower bumper treatment. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches on GT variants, complemented by clean flank character lines.

The Kia EV3 features a compact, angular crossover SUV body style with a steeply raked windshield and a blocky, futuristic silhouette. The front end showcases distinctive vertical LED 'Star Map' signature headlights positioned at the outer edges, framing a smooth, flush-surfaced panel in place of a traditional grille. The side profile highlights squared-off wheel arches with dark cladding, flush door handles, and a floating roof effect created by blackened pillars. At the rear, it has geometric, sharply angled tail lights that wrap into the tailgate, mirroring the lighting language of the front.

The Kia EV5 is a medium five-door electric SUV characterized by a boxy, squared-off silhouette and upright proportions resembling a scaled-down EV9. It features a closed-off 'Tiger Face' front fascia framed by distinctive signature LED daytime running lights and vertically stacked headlamps, coupled with a full-width geometric rear light signature. Aerodynamic touches include flush-fitting pop-out door handles, while wheel options range from 18-inch to 20-inch alloy designs depending on the variant. Higher-spec models also benefit from a prominent panoramic glass roof and contrasting roof color finishes.

The first-generation Kia EV6 features a low-slung, dynamic electric crossover body with a swept-back roofline and a heavily raked rear window. The front showcases a distinctive 'Digital Tiger Face' with sleek, angled LED headlights and a closed-off nose. At the rear, a continuous light bar curves upward over the rear haunches above a pronounced integrated spoiler. It sits on alloy wheels ranging from 19 to 21 inches and incorporates flush, pop-out door handles.

The Kia EV9 (Gen 1 / MV1) is a large, boxy, five-door electric SUV featuring a commanding, upright stance with sharp geometric lines and flush door handles. Its front fascia incorporates a blanked-out digital tiger face with vertical LED projector headlights and constellation-style signature daytime running lights. The rear features thin, vertically oriented LED tail lights that stretch upward along the D-pillars. Exterior details include squared-off wheel arches housing aerodynamic alloy wheels ranging from 19 to 21 inches, a flat roofline, and a cleanly integrated rear spoiler concealing the rear wiper.

The first-generation Kia K4 features a low-slung, fastback sedan silhouette with a planted stance and wide rear fenders. The front end is defined by futuristic, vertically oriented T-shaped LED headlamps flanking a wide, streamlined grille layout. At the rear, sharp LED tail lights stretch horizontally across the width of the tailgate, mirroring the striking lighting signature up front. The side profile is accentuated by flush-mounted rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars and dynamic geometric alloy wheel designs.

The first-generation Kia Niro (DE) features a conventional crossover-hatchback body style with a sloping roofline and practical five-door layout. It has a rounded front fascia incorporating Kia's signature 'tiger-nose' grille flanked by swept-back halogen or bi-LED headlights, accompanied by lower bumper-mounted fog lights. The rear is characterised by wraparound LED combination tail lights framing a sculpted tailgate, while the profile rides on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches and includes standard factory roof rails. Electric variants feature a solid, unique front insert hiding the charging port, distinguishing them from the open-grille hybrid and plug-in hybrid models.

The second-generation Kia Niro is a compact 5-door small SUV featuring a low-slung, aerodynamic silhouette with distinct proportions. The front end showcases angular LED headlamps flanking a narrow 'tiger face' grille, while higher-grade variants feature a prominent contrasting C-pillar design that acts as an air duct. At the rear, boomerang-shaped vertical LED tail lights wrap around the upper edges of the body alongside a rugged lower skid plate. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 17 inches and features a roof-mounted shark-fin antenna.

The fourth-generation Kia Optima is a four-door medium sedan featuring a sleek, fastback-inspired roofline and an evolution of Kia's signature 'tiger nose' grille connected directly to sharp, swept-back projector headlights. The side profile is defined by a clean shoulder line, chrome window surrounds with a distinct Hofmeister-style kink on the C-pillar, and alloy wheel designs ranging from 17 to 18 inches. At the rear, it features wraparound LED tail lights, a subtle integrated boot-lid spoiler, and a lower bumper insert housing a diffuser and dual or oval exhaust tips depending on the variant.

The Kia Picanto JA is a five-door city car featuring a compact, upright stance with short overhangs and an extended wheelbase relative to its overall length. It features a prominent 'tiger-nose' grille flanked by swept-back headlights, which incorporate distinct projector elements and LED daytime running lights on later iterations. The rear profile is defined by C-shaped or angular wraparound tail lights, a flat tailgate, and a lower bumper housing integrated fog lamps or a faux diffuser. Throughout its lifecycle in Australia, it has been offered with various alloy wheel designs up to 16 inches, body-coloured door handles, and a contrasting roof option on select sporty variants.

The third-generation Kia Rio features a wedge-like profile available as a 5-door hatchback or 4-door sedan, characterized by swept-back headlights and a signature 'tiger-nose' upper grille. It displays clean body side character lines, a rising beltline, and wraparound tail lights. Depending on the specification grade, it rides on steel or alloy wheels and features a relatively upright rear stance with a clean tailgate or boot lid design.

The fourth-generation Kia Rio hatchback features a lower, wider, and more mature stance with sharp character lines stretching along its profile. It is equipped with a slimmed-down interpretation of Kia's signature 'tiger nose' grille that flows directly into angular headlights. The rear showcases a steeply raked tailgate, a planted bumper design, and wraparound tail lights. Depending on the specification, it rides on alloy wheels ranging from 15 to 17 inches and features a structured C-pillar design.

The first-generation Kia Seltos is a compact five-door small SUV featuring a boxy, upright stance and muscular body lines. It is characterized by a prominent 'tiger-nose' front grille flanked by sharp multi-element LED headlights and distinctive, stepped daytime running lights. The rear showcases angular horizontal tail lights connected across the tailgate by a chrome or metallic trim piece, while the profile is completed by squared-off wheel arches and alloy wheel options ranging up to 18 inches.

The third-generation Kia Sorento is a five-door, large seven-seater SUV featuring a longer, wider, and lower stance with fluid proportions. It features a prominent 'tiger-nose' mesh grille flanked by swept-back headlights, accompanied by rounded rectangular fog lamps embedded in the lower bumper. The rear showcases wraparound horizontal tail lights, a roof spoiler, and a clean tailgate design. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches, complemented by sleek body-side character lines and integrated roof rails.

The fourth-generation Kia Sorento is a large five-door, three-row SUV featuring a boxy, muscular stance and sharp geometric proportions. Early models feature wide 'tiger nose' grilles flanked by horizontal multi-element LED headlights, while the later facelift introduces a prominent upright grille paired with distinctive vertical T-shaped LED headlight clusters. At the rear, it is characterized by split vertical or connected angular LED tail lights, integrated roof rails, and alloy wheel sizes ranging up to 20 inches depending on the variant.

The fourth-generation Kia Sportage features a 5-door medium SUV body style with a rounded, aerodynamic silhouette and muscular side character lines. Its front end is defined by a raised 'tiger-nose' grille flanked by swept-back headlights that sit high on the fenders, alongside distinct lower bumper fog light housings. The rear showcases wraparound horizontal tail lights connected by a slim garnish panel, sitting above a chunky bumper valance. Depending on the spec, it rides on alloy wheels up to 19 inches and can feature a panoramic glass roof.

The fifth-generation Kia Sportage features a striking medium SUV body style characterized by sharp character lines, a steeply raked rear window, and a prominent piano-black geometric grille spanning the width of the front fascia. It is distinguished by boomerang-shaped LED daytime running lights framing low-set projector headlights. The rear showcases slim, horizontal LED tail lights connected by a sleek central light bar across the tailgate.

The first-generation Kia Stinger features a low-slung, fastback sedan body style with four doors and an aggressive, cab-rearward stance. It showcases a signature 'tiger-nose' grille flanked by sharp LED headlights, complemented by a sloping roofline that flows cleanly into a liftback rear tailgate. The rear is defined by distinct tail lights—upgraded during its lifecycle to a continuous full-width light bar—above quad exhaust outlets and a sporty diffuser. Multi-spoke 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels fill the guards, often highlighting high-performance Brembo brake calipers underneath.

The first-generation Kia Stonic is a five-door light SUV featuring a compact, raised hatchback stance with short overhangs and chunky plastic body cladding around the wheel arches and sills. It incorporates Kia's signature 'tiger-nose' upper grille flanked by swept-back headlights, often accented by striking LED daytime running lights. The rear features wraparound tail lights, a subtly integrated roof spoiler, and a scuff plate element on the bumper. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 17 inches and is frequently optioned with a contrasting two-tone floating roof color scheme.

The Kia Tasman dual-cab ute features an assertive, boxy body style with upright doors, a wide roof, and prominent, squared-off fender flares. The front fascia is defined by a wide, rectangular grille flanked by vertically oriented LED headlights positioned near the outer edges. At the rear, it features simple vertical tail lights framing a functional tailgate with integrated corner bumper steps. Depending on the variant, it rides on 17-inch steel or alloy wheels up to 18-inch rims, with rugged off-road variants offering increased ride height and all-terrain tires.

The Lamborghini Aventador S Roadster features an ultra-low, wedge-shaped two-door body with scissor doors and a removable two-piece carbon-fiber hardtop roof. Its aggressive front end incorporates a shark-nose profile with an elongated splitter and large air intakes, flanked by angular LED headlights. The rear showcases a prominent active wing with three positions, a massive black diffuser, and triple central exhaust outlets beneath slim, horizontal LED tail lights. It rides on staggered alloy wheels (20-inch front, 21-inch rear), exposing a visible mid-mounted V12 engine beneath a slatted or transparent bonnet.

The Lamborghini Aventador S coupe features a low-slung, wedge-shaped body with two scissor doors and an extremely low roofline. Its aggressive front fascia incorporates a sharper nose with prominent aerodynamic splitters and distinct side air intakes, complemented by sharp, angular LED headlights. The side profile exhibits dramatic creases and large side air scoops, accented by rear wheel arches inspired by the classic Countach. At the rear, it displays a black diffuser with vertical fins, a triple-outlet exhaust housed centrally in a hexagonal surround, and an active rear wing adjustable to multiple positions.

The Lamborghini Aventador SVJ coupe features an ultra-low, wedge-shaped two-door body with signature scissor doors and aggressive aerodynamic styling. It is distinguished by a prominent front splitter, active aerodynamic slats (ALA 2.0), side air intakes, and a massive fixed rear carbon-fibre wing. The front end displays sharp angular headlights flanking deep bumper vents, while the rear showcases high-mounted dual exhaust outlets and Y-motif LED tail lights sitting above a large diffuser.

The Lamborghini Aventador SVJ Roadster features a low-slung, wedge-shaped two-door body style with scissor doors and removable lightweight carbon fibre roof panels. Its aggressive front fascia showcases a wide grille with active aerodynamics (ALA) and sharp, angular LED headlights. The rear profile is dominated by a prominent high-mounted carbon fibre wing, central dual exhaust outlets, and sleek Y-signature LED tail lights. It rides on staggered center-lock forged wheels paired with massive side air intakes and a prominent rear diffuser.

The Lamborghini Huracán LP610-4 coupe features a low-slung, wedge-shaped body with angular lines and a cab-forward silhouette. It sports sharp Y-signature LED headlights flanking a low hexagonal grille, large side air intakes, and aggressive Y-motif LED tail lights at the rear. The exterior is completed with a smooth sloping roofline, quad exhaust outlets, and multi-spoke alloy wheels hiding carbon-ceramic brakes.

The Lamborghini Huracán LP580-2 coupe features a sharp, wedge-shaped two-door body with a low-slung stance and forward-forward cabin proportions. Its front fascia is distinguished by a unique, more aggressive bumper design with enlarged, distinctively shaped outer air intakes compared to its all-wheel-drive stablemates. At the rear, it sports slim Y-signature LED tail lights flanking a louvered engine cover and dual exhaust outlets exiting from a low diffuser. It rides on staggered alloy wheels—typically 19-inch 'Kari' rims—framing steel brake discs, while retaining a smooth, low-profile roofline sweeping into a flat decklid.

The Lamborghini Huracán Spyder is a two-door roadster featuring a lightweight fabric soft-top roof that folds into a rear compartment behind the cabin. It showcases angular wedge proportions, aggressive geometric air intakes on the front fascia, and sharp Y-signature LED headlights and tail lights. The rear deck integrates distinctive aerodynamic fins framing the engine cover, while alloy wheels house large carbon-ceramic brake discs.

The Lamborghini Huracán Performante coupe features a low-slung, wedge-shaped two-door body with ultra-lightweight forged composite carbon-fibre aero elements on the aggressive front splitter, engine cover, and rear diffuser. It showcases sharp, angular LED headlights flanking a low-profile front grille, alongside an aggressive fixed rear wing integrated with active aerodynamic air ducts. The rear sports slim LED tail lights, dual high-mounted exhaust outlets, and rides on 20-inch alloy wheels with available center-locks. Accents of Italian tricolour livery stripe the lower flanks of the body.

The Lamborghini Huracán Performante Spyder is a two-door roadster featuring an electrically retractable soft top and an aggressive aerodynamic body kit with forged composite elements. It sports angular Y-shaped LED headlights flanking a low, sharp nose, along with high-mounted dual exhaust tips integrated into the rear diffuser. The rear is dominated by a fixed carbon-fiber wing utilizing active aerodynamics (ALA), paired with slim LED tail lights and large alloy wheels framing carbon-ceramic brakes.

The Lamborghini Huracán EVO Spyder is a two-door roadster featuring a lightweight electrohydraulic soft top that opens in 17 seconds. Its wedge-shaped profile is defined by aggressive front Y-shaped aerodynamic air intakes, integrated front splitter, and sharp LED headlights. The rear sports high-mounted dual exhaust outlets, a slotted rear spoiler, and slender Y-signature tail lights flanking a mesh engine cover.

The Lamborghini Huracán EVO coupe features a sharp, wedge-shaped two-door body with an aerodynamic front bumper incorporating Y-motif air intakes and distinct Y-shaped LED headlights. Its profile showcases mid-engine proportions with angular side intakes and a low-slung roofline flowing into an integrated rear spoiler. The rear is distinguished by high-mounted dual exhaust outlets, a pronounced diffuser, and slim Y-shaped LED tail lights.

The Lamborghini Huracán STO is a two-door, low-slung coupe featuring an aggressive, track-derived carbon-fibre body. Its front end is defined by a single-piece 'Cofango' clamshell combining the hood, fenders, and bumper. Distinctive aerodynamic elements include a roof-mounted air snorkel, an integrated vertical rear 'shark fin', a prominent adjustable rear wing, and a specialized rear engine cover. It rides on lightweight center-lock wheels framed by wider, louvered fenders housing large cooling ducts.

The Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica coupe features a low-slung, two-door body with an extended profile and a lightweight carbon-fiber hood and engine cover. Its front fascia incorporates an aggressive black Ypsilon design motif, while the rear showcases vertical glass, a revised bumper, an integrated diffuser, and hexagonal exhaust tips. It rides on staggered lightweight alloy wheels and features sharp aerodynamic channeling along its flanks and side air intakes.

The Lamborghini Huracán Sterrato is a two-door, raised-stance coupe featuring an angular body profile with increased ground clearance and an aluminum front skid plate. It is characterized by prominent riveted matte-black composite wheel arch flares, extended side sills, and standard roof rails. A distinctive air snorkel is mounted on the rear roof to feed clean air to the V10 engine, complemented by optional bumper-mounted LED driving lights. It rides on 19-inch alloy wheels wrapped in custom all-terrain run-flat tyres.

The Lamborghini Revuelto coupe features a low-slung, wedge-shaped body with signature scissor doors and dramatic sharp-edged surfacing. It showcases distinct Y-shaped daytime running lights framing the slim headlamp units, paired with matching Y-signature LED tail lights. The rear end highlights a completely exposed V12 engine bay flanked by high-mounted hexagonal exhaust tips and an active rear spoiler.

The Lamborghini Temerario coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamic two-door body with sharp geometric lines and hexagonal design motifs. It is characterized by ultra-slim LED headlights integrated with distinctive hexagonal daytime running lights, a sharply raked windshield, and muscular rear haunches. The rear showcases slim hexagonal tail lights, an aggressive high-mounted exhaust outlet, and an advanced aerodynamic diffuser.

The first-generation Lamborghini Urus features an aggressive, coupe-like SUV body style with a low-slung, highly sculpted profile and four frameless doors. The front fascia showcases sharp Y-shaped LED headlights flanking a heavily creased bonnet, above a massive hexagonal lower grille and broad air intakes. Its athletic stance is defined by muscular, sharp-edged wheel arches that accommodate large alloy wheels up to 23 inches, a fast-sloping roofline, and an angular rear layout featuring slim horizontal LED tail lights and a prominent roof spoiler.

The Lamborghini Urus SE features a low-slung, coupe-like SUV body style with four doors, sharp character lines, and a muscular stance. It incorporates a redesigned floating bonnet, sleeker matrix LED headlights with a distinct daytime running light signature, and a revised front grille and lower bumper layout. At the rear, it sports updated, interconnected tail lights above a revised grille and an aggressive lower diffuser. The profile is anchored by large 23-inch alloy wheels sitting beneath pronounced wheel arches, alongside a sloping roofline and optimized aerodynamic underbody elements.

The Land Rover Defender L663 is offered in three distinct body lengths—the three-door 90, five-door 110, and extended five-door 130 SUV variants. It features a boxy, squared-off silhouette with a high waistline, alpine roof windows, and a side-hinged rear tailgate carrying a full-sized spare wheel. The front end showcases a rounded rectangular grille flanked by distinct, squared-off LED headlights with circular signature DRLs, while the rear features minimalist, segmented rectangular LED tail lights.

The Land Rover Discovery 5 is a large five-door luxury SUV characterized by a smooth, rounded body profile that departs from the boxy silhouette of its predecessors. It features a clamshell hood, swept-back LED headlights flanking a slim mesh grille, and an asymmetrical rear license plate recess on the tailgate. Notable design elements include a stepped roofline that nods to historical Discovery models, wide stance proportions, and alloy wheel options ranging up to 22 inches.

The Land Rover Discovery Sport (L550) is a compact five-door SUV featuring a sloping roofline, a clamshell bonnet, and a relatively rounded profile compared to its boxy predecessors. It features a mesh grille flanked by sleek LED headlights with signature daytime running lights, alongside rectangular tail lights. Alloy wheel options range up to 20 inches, while the rear showcases a subtly raked tailgate and a distinctive offset rear license plate recess.

The Range Rover L405 features a full-size, five-door luxury wagon body style with a distinctively squared-off silhouette, a characteristic 'floating' roof structure, and a clamshell bonnet. It incorporates a prominent rectangular mesh grille flanked by sleek, swept-back rectangular headlamp clusters featuring signature LED daytime running lights. The rear profile is defined by wraparound vertical tail lights and a practical split-opening tailgate. The exterior proportions emphasize an upright glasshouse, clean aluminum-paneled body sides with minimal ornamentation, and large alloy wheel options ranging up to 22 inches.

The fifth-generation Land Rover Range Rover (L460) features a clean, monolithic five-door SUV body with flush door handles and exceptionally smooth, minimalist surfacing. It is characterized by a prominent rectangular grille paired with slim digital LED headlights up front, while the rear showcases distinctive vertical tail-lights hidden beneath a wraparound gloss-black horizontal panel. Available in standard and long-wheelbase configurations, it rides on large alloy wheels and features a floating roof design with seamless glass-to-body transitions.

The first-generation Range Rover Evoque features a distinctive wedge-like profile with a dramatic downward-sloping roofline and an upward-sweeping beltline. It was offered in three-door coupe, five-door SUV, and two-door convertible body styles, all sitting on chunky proportions with high shoulder lines. The front showcases a rectangular mesh grille flanked by narrow, angular headlights with signature LED daytime running lights, while the rear features slim horizontal tail lights and a prominent spoiler. Details include flush-fitting elements, large alloy wheels, and an available contrasting roof color.

The Land Rover Range Rover Evoque (L551) features a compact, coupe-like luxury SUV body style characterized by a sloping roofline, a rising beltline, and flush deployable door handles. It is distinguished by super-slim Pixel LED headlights framing a simplified grille, alongside wrap-around minimalist tail lights. The exterior stance is emphasized by clean, reductive surfaces, large alloy wheels, and an available contrasting roof.

The L494 Range Rover Sport is a large five-door luxury SUV featuring a muscular, athletic stance with short overhangs and a sloping floating roofline. It is styled with a relatively slim front grille flanked by sleek, wrap-around headlights (updated to matrix LED units in the 2018 facelift). The side profile showcases distinctive front fender vents and prominent alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 22 inches, while the rear features a clean horizontal tailgate layout with wraparound LED tail lights. High-performance SVR variants are visually distinguished by aggressive body styling, larger front air intakes, quad exhaust tips, and an optional carbon fibre bonnet.

The Land Rover Range Rover Sport (L461) is a 5-door luxury SUV characterized by a reductive, modernist design with smooth surfacing, flush-fitting deployable door handles, and a low stance. At the front, it features an ultra-slim grille flanked by narrow horizontal LED headlights, positioned above a pronounced lower bumper intake. The rear profile is defined by a clean, full-width black horizontal graphic element that integrates slim, hidden-until-lit tail lights. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging up to 23 inches, complemented by short overhangs and a dramatic sweeping roofline.

The Land Rover Range Rover Velar (L560) is a mid-size luxury SUV featuring a sleek, aerodynamic five-door body style with flush deployable door handles and a sweeping coupe-like roofline. Its minimalist exterior is defined by a prominent mesh grille flanked by ultra-slim pixel LED headlights, clean reductive body surfaces, and connected horizontal LED tail lights. It rides on large alloy wheels (ranging up to 22 inches) and often features a contrasting black floating roof.

The first-generation LDV D90 is a large, square-shouldered, five-door body-on-frame SUV with a commanding stance and three-row proportions. It features a prominent, expansive multi-slat chrome front grille flanked by slim horizontal LED headlamps and a high-set bumper. The profile is defined by an upright roofline, full-length roof rails, prominent side steps, and alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 19 inches. At the rear, it has wraparound LED tail lights connected by a subtle chrome trim strip across the tailgate.

The first-generation LDV Deliver 7 van features a modern panel van body style with short and long wheelbase low-roof configurations. It showcases a futuristic front fascia dominated by a distinctive matrix-style grille flanked by sharp, dusk-sensing LED headlights. The side profile highlights a boxy, aerodynamic silhouette fitted with standard steel wheels (or optional alloys), a single sliding side door, and a low height under two metres. The rear is equipped with vertical LED tail-lights and 50/50 split barn doors capable of opening up to 180 degrees.

The first-generation LDV Deliver 9 features a utilitarian large van, bus, and cab-chassis silhouette characterized by a tall, slab-sided profile and a prominent, chrome-accented octagonal front grille. It is framed by swept-back headlights and features vertical-stack front bumper elements. At the rear, the van variants incorporate tall, vertical tail lights flanking dual barn-style doors, riding on steel wheels with varying roof-height configurations ranging from mid to high-roof options.

The LDV eDeliver 5 is a fully electric mid-size van featuring a boxy yet rounded, modern silhouette available in short-wheelbase low-roof and long-wheelbase low- or high-roof configurations. It comes equipped with narrow LED headlights flanking a smooth, sealed front fascia, dual windowless side sliding doors, and windowless 50/50 split rear barn doors. The exterior is anchored by short overhangs, a tall stance with a distinctive curved roofline, and 16-inch alloy wheels.

The LDV eDeliver 7 is a medium-to-large commercial panel van featuring a clean, aerodynamic front fascia with a closed-off grille housing the charge port, flanked by sleek LED headlights. It has a boxy, utilitarian side profile with sliding side doors, riding on 16-inch steel wheels, and is available in various short-wheelbase, long-wheelbase, low-roof, and high-roof configurations. The rear is equipped with vertical tail lights and a 50/50 split two-stage opening barn door setup.

The LDV eDeliver 9 is a large box-style electric van featuring a tall, flat-sided silhouette available in long-wheelbase mid-roof and high-roof configurations. Its front end is dominated by a large, enclosed angular grille flanked by swept-back vertical headlights and a prominent front bumper. The side profile includes a single passenger-side sliding door and 16-inch alloy wheels, while the rear features vertical tail lights and 236-degree opening barn doors with an integrated step.

The first-generation LDV G10 features a typical two-box commercial van and passenger-mover silhouette with a short, steeply raked bonnet blending into a large panoramic windscreen. It is configured with dual sliding side doors and a rear liftgate or split barn doors. The front end is characterized by swept-back wraparound headlights framing a trapezoidal grille, complemented by a lower bumper air intake. At the rear, vertically oriented rectangular tail lamps sit high on the corners of the high-roof body, which rides on 16-inch wheels.

The LDV Mifa is a large, boxy five-door people mover featuring a commanding upright front fascia with an expansive chrome-accented or body-colored grille and slender LED daytime running lights flanked by lower-mounted headlights. Its side profile highlights a long wheelbase with large glass areas, power-sliding side doors, and multi-spoke alloy wheels. The rear is defined by a flat tailgate framed by distinctive full-width LED tail lights with intricate signature graphics and a subtle roof-mounted spoiler.

The LDV Mifa 9 is a large, boxy electric people mover featuring a wide stance, clean character lines, and power-sliding side doors. The front fascia is dominated by a high, closed-off nose integrated with slim full-LED headlights and sharp daytime running light strips. At the rear, it features expansive signature LED tail lights with intricate dynamic indicators spanning the width of the tailgate beneath a roof-mounted spoiler. Depending on the variant, it rides on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels and offers contrasting black roof options on select dual-tone paint schemes.

The LDV T60 dual-cab ute features a muscular four-door body configuration with prominent, squared-off wheel arches and practical side steps. The front end showcases a bold, dominant chrome or dark grille flanked by sharp, swept-back LED headlights and integrated daytime running lights. The rear is defined by vertical rectangular tail lights framing a drop-down tailgate, often complemented by factory roof rails and a sturdy sports bar over the tray. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches depending on the variant.

The LDV Terron 9 is a large, imposing dual-cab utility with a prominent, slab-sided stance and an unusual integrated single-body side panel where the cab flows directly into the tray. Its aggressive front fascia features a wide grille flanked by striking LED headlights with distinctive T-shaped lighting signatures. It rides on large alloy wheels (such as 20-inch rims) and includes practical exterior details like side steps, a lift-assisted tailgate, and available cargo lighting and sliding rails.

The first-generation LDV V80 features an upright, boxy commercial van and bus silhouette with short-wheelbase low-roof or long-wheelbase high-roof configurations, alongside a dedicated cab-chassis variant. It is styled with a prominent chrome-slatted front grille, swept-back vertical headlight clusters integrated with LED daytime running lights, and dual sliding side doors. The rear incorporates split barn-style doors opening up to 180 degrees, paired with high-mounted vertical tail lights, sitting typically on 16-inch wheels.

The Lexus CT 200h is a five-door luxury hybrid hatchback featuring a low-slung, wedge-like profile with a steeply raked windscreen and a distinctively tapered rear. Up front, it showcases a prominent spindle grille flanked by swept-back headlights integrated with signature arrowhead daytime running lights. The rear sports an abrupt tailgate drop, a subtle roof spoiler, and horizontal L-shaped tail lights. It sits on 15-inch to 17-inch alloy wheels and features a roof-mounted shark-fin antenna.

The sixth-generation Lexus ES is a four-door luxury sedan characterized by a flowing, coupe-like roofline and an assertive stance. Its front fascia is dominated by a bold, hourglass-shaped spindle grille flanked by swept-back headlights featuring integrated arrowhead daytime running lights. Following a 2015 update, the exterior received a wider grille frame, sharper LED headlight clusters, and a revised rear with wraparound tail lights stretching into the boot lid. It sits on 17-inch alloy wheels and features a power sunroof and a discreet boot lid spoiler on hybrid variants.

The Lexus ES (XV70) is a four-door luxury sedan featuring a coupe-like sloping roofline and a long, low-slung stance. It is defined by a massive, aggressive spindle grille dominating the front fascia, flanked by sharp, angular LED headlights with integrated arrow-head daytime running lights. The rear displays wraparound LED tail lights connected by a subtle boot-lid spoiler and clean sheet-metal surfacing. It sits on multi-spoke alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches, with chrome window surrounds accentuating its executive profile.

The L10-generation Lexus GS sedan features a prominent hourglass-shaped 'spindle' grille flanked by sharp headlights with distinct L-shaped LED daytime running lights. It has a traditional three-box executive saloon profile with a planted stance, wide track, and a gently sloping roofline ending in a short boot lid. The rear showcases wraparound LED tail light clusters with an inner L-pattern motif, while higher-spec and F Sport variants add aggressive lower bumper styling, unique mesh grilles, rear lip spoilers, and large alloy wheels.

The Lexus GX J250 is a large, boxy, body-on-frame SUV defined by a strong, upright stance and flat, squared-off bonnet lines. It features a modern interpretation of the spindle grille flanked by slim, horizontal LED headlights, and a continuous full-width light bar spanning the rear tailgate. The profile showcases squared wheel arches, high ground clearance, and a stepped beltline, with wheel sizes ranging up to 22-inch alloys depending on the grade.

The third-generation Lexus IS sedan features a low-slung, coupe-like profile characterized by a prominent hourglass spindle grille and sharply angled headlights featuring separate arrowhead daytime running lights. Its flanks are defined by a dramatic, upward-sweeping lower character line that cuts across the doors into muscular rear wheel arches. The rear end incorporates sharp, wrap-around tail lights with distinct 'L'-shaped signatures stretching toward the boot lid. Rolling stock includes multi-spoke alloy wheel designs, while F Sport variants add a mesh grille insert, more aggressive bumper geometry, and a subtle boot-lip spoiler.

The Lexus LBX is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a low-slung, broad stance with short overhangs and a stubby, athletic profile. Up front, it showcases a low-set interpretation of the spindle grille flanked by slim, sharp LED headlights integrated with angular daytime running lights. The rear is characterised by a clean tailgate design spanned by a continuous, slim LED light bar beneath a prominent roof spoiler. Variants commonly ride on 18-inch alloy wheels and feature an available two-tone contrasting black roof.

The Lexus LC features a dramatic, low-slung grand tourer stance with a sweeping fastback roofline for the coupe and a multi-layered acoustic soft-top for the convertible. Up front, it is dominated by an expansive, diamond-mesh spindle grille flanked by slim, independent triple-projector LED headlights and boomerang daytime running lights. The sculpted body exhibits muscular rear haunches, flush door handles, and sharp, multi-dimensional LED tail lights that draw inspiration from jet exhaust flames. It rides on large 21-inch forged alloy wheels, complemented by aerodynamic creases and an aggressive rear diffuser layout.

The Lexus LM (EM10) is a large luxury people mover featuring a boxy, aerodynamic silhouette with sliding side doors and blacked-out pillars. The front showcases a modern, frameless color-matched 'Unified Spindle' grille that blends into the bodywork, flanked by sharp LED headlights. The rear is defined by a full-width LED light bar that sweeps upward at the outer edges. It rides on 19-inch multi-spoke alloy wheels and includes dual independent roof windows over the cabin.

The fourth-generation Lexus LS is a large, formal four-door luxury sedan featuring a conservative three-box silhouette, available in standard and long-wheelbase variants. Early models feature a wide chrome-accented horizontal-slat grille flanked by wrap-around projector headlights, which evolved through mid-cycle refreshes to incorporate a prominent hourglass 'spindle' grille and aggressive LED lighting configurations. The rear profile is defined by clean trunk lines, integrated dual exhaust tips, and wide horizontal tail lights wrapping into the quarter panels. It rides on multi-spoke alloy wheels and features subtle chrome window surrounds and flush body panels.

The Lexus LS XF50 is a large, low-slung four-door luxury sedan characterized by a coupe-like fastback roofline and a sweeping, aerodynamic profile. Its front fascia is dominated by a massive, intricate spindle grille flanked by ultra-slim, multi-projector LED headlamps featuring boomerang-shaped daytime running lights. The rear features angular, wrap-around LED tail lights connected by chrome trim accents, while the sides sit on large multi-spoke alloy wheels. Distinctive elements include deeply sculpted character lines along the body sides and a wide, planted stance.

The J200 Lexus LX is a large, body-on-frame luxury SUV featuring a boxy, robust stance with upright proportions and a split-fold tailgate. Across its production run, it evolved from a traditional horizontal chrome grille and wraparound rectangular headlights into an aggressive, massive 'spindle' grille design paired with sharp, multi-element LED headlamps and arrow-shaped daytime running lights. The rear is defined by wide wrap-around tail lights and a clean, flat tailgate design, while the profile is marked by squared-off wheel arches typically housing large alloy wheels and an upright greenhouse with a standard roof spoiler.

The Lexus LX (J300) is a large, body-on-frame luxury SUV featuring a towering stance, squared-off proportions, and traditional four-door layout. The front is dominated by a massive, three-dimensional spindle grille flanked by slim, sharp LED headlights and blade-style daytime running lights. The profile is characterized by muscular wheel arches and a high beltline, accommodating large alloy wheels up to 22 inches. At the rear, it features a full-width continuous LED tail light bar with layered optics, a minimalist tailgate bearing spaced-out 'LEXUS' lettering, and an integrated roof spoiler. Roof rails and side steps complete its utilitarian yet upscale exterior profile.

The first-generation Lexus NX features an angular, wedge-like medium SUV body style with four doors and sharply creased character lines. It is dominated at the front by a prominent, hourglass-shaped spindle grille flanked by slim, multi-beam LED headlamps and independent tick-shaped daytime running lights. The rear showcases sharp, three-dimensional LED tail lights that wrap into the side profile, complemented by a heavily raked rear window. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches, with F Sport variants displaying a mesh grille design, sportier lower bumper treatments, and black mirror caps.

The second-generation Lexus NX features a medium crossover SUV body style with sharply sculpted character lines and athletic proportions. The front end is defined by a prominent spindle grille flanked by sleek LED headlights with integrated daytime running lights. At the rear, it sports a distinctive full-width 'blade' LED light bar connecting the tail lights. The side profile is accentuated by flowing body creases, dynamic window lines, and varying alloy wheel designs depending on the variant.

The Lexus RC coupe features a low-slung, aggressive stance characterized by a prominent hourglass spindle grille and sharp, angular headlamps integrated with separate L-shaped daytime running lights. Its two-door body exhibits muscular, flowing proportions, sweeping side character lines, and a fastback roofline. The rear is defined by distinct, wraparound L-signature LED tail lights and athletic bumper contours. It rides on multi-spoke alloy wheels, ranging up to 19 inches, and includes aero-stabilising details molded into the side window frames and rear corners.

The Lexus RX AL20 is a five-door large SUV characterized by a sharp, angular silhouette and a prominent, massive spindle grille flanked by slim, arrowhead-style LED headlights. Its profile features a distinctive floating-roof effect created by blackened C-pillars that visually wrap into the rear glass. At the back, it is fitted with sharp, L-shaped LED tail lights that extend into the tailgate, complemented by clean body surfacing and alloy wheel designs ranging from 18 to 20 inches.

The AL30 generation Lexus RX features a low-slung, athletic large SUV stance with a distinctive 'spindle body' front design where the upper grille seamlessly merges into the bumper bodywork. It is equipped with sharp, slim LED headlamps featuring integrated L-shaped daytime running lights, and a full-width LED light bar spanning the tail gate. The side profile showcases a floating roof effect created by a blacked-out rear pillar, underlined by prominent alloy wheels up to 21 inches in size.

The Lexus RZ medium SUV features a dynamic five-door fastback-crossover silhouette with a long wheelbase and short overhangs. Its front end adopts a unique body-coloured "spindle body" structure flanked by slim LED headlights and an enclosed lower grille area. The side profile is defined by sharp character lines, muscular rear haunches, and a sloping roofline that flows into a split rear spoiler. At the rear, it sports a full-width LED light bar connecting angular tail lamps, while higher variants feature distinctive multi-spoke alloy wheel designs and optional two-tone exterior paint schemes.

The Lexus UX compact SUV features a low-slung, hatchback-like stance with sharply sculpted bodywork and flared wheel arches. It is defined by a bold, three-dimensional spindle grille up front, flanked by angular L-shaped arrowhead daytime running lights and slim LED headlights. The rear is characterised by a distinctive full-width light bar featuring aero-stabilising blade fins that taper toward the center. The profile is topped by a subtle rear wing spoiler and rides on aerodynamically styled alloy wheels.

The Lotus Eletre is a large, low-slung 5-door electric performance SUV featuring a coupe-like sloping roofline and extensive aerodynamic air-channeling across its body. The front end showcases razor-thin LED DRL strips positioned above segmented main headlight clusters flanking a multi-element active grille. The rear is dominated by a full-width LED light bar with a cascading light signature and a floating dual-piece roof spoiler. Profile details include flush-fitting pop-out door handles, optional camera-based side mirrors, and staggered large-diameter alloy wheels ranging up to 22 inches.

The Series 3 Lotus Elise is a compact, two-door roadster featuring lightweight fibreglass bodywork over an extruded aluminium chassis with ultra-low proportions and short overhangs. Its front end is defined by a crisp lower grille opening, side air intakes, and single-piece, swept-back headlights with integrated LED daytime running lights. The profile exhibits mid-engine side air scoops and an engine cover featuring a distinctive twin-spine design, leading down to a wide rear bumper housing round taillights and a prominent lower diffuser. Staggered lightweight alloy wheels (16-inch front and 17-inch rear) complete its track-focused stance.

The Lotus Emeya is a sleek, four-door electric grand tourer sedan featuring a low-slung, coupe-like silhouette and a distinctive shark-nose front end. It is characterized by split multi-pixel Matrix LED headlights, flush door handles, and an active aerodynamic package including an active front air dam and rear spoiler. The rear is defined by an ultra-thin, full-width light bar, while the stance is anchored by large alloy wheels (typically 20-inch or 21-inch) and complemented by a sweeping panoramic glass roof.

The Lotus Emira is a low-slung, two-door mid-engine sports coupe featuring dramatic aerodynamic sculpting and sharp character lines influenced by the Evija hypercar. It showcases vertical LED headlamps flanking a wide, low-set grille opening, alongside deeply sculpted door air intakes and athletic haunches. At the rear, it features slim horizontal LED tail lights connected by a subtle visual element above dual exhaust outlets, while riding on lightweight alloy wheels.

The Lotus Evora Series 2 (including the Evora 400 and GT series) is a lightweight mid-engine coupe featuring aggressive aerodynamic styling, a low nose, and a composite mesh grille. It rides on staggered 19-inch front and 20-inch rear lightweight alloy wheels paired with prominent cross-drilled brakes and red-painted AP Racing calipers. The sleek fastback profile showcases a cab-rearward stance, sharp side cooling ducts, wraparound windows, and an integrated rear wing or spoiler. Distinctive round tail lights anchor the tail end alongside a central exhaust outlet and a prominent rear diffuser.

The Series 3 Lotus Exige coupe features an aggressive, low-slung aerodynamic profile with a fixed roof, sharp front splitter, and a prominent rear wing. The front fascia incorporates angular headlight clusters flanking a wide mesh lower grille opening, while the rear showcases circular dual tail lights set into a flat tail panel with a lower diffuser. It rides on staggered alloy wheels, and its compact mid-engine proportions are accented by side air intake scoops and a wraparound clamshell rear hatch.

The Mahindra Genio features a utilitarian, forward-control cab-chassis and utility body style characterized by a very short, abruptly sloping bonnet and a high-set seating position. It incorporates large, wrap-around headlamps flanking a simple mesh grille, vertical tail lamps at the rear, and large rectangular door openings designed for easy cabin access. It rides on 15-inch steel or optional alloy wheels, paired with either a long single-cab drop-side alloy tray or a compact dual-cab tray. Integrated side steps and a high ground clearance accentuate its practical, function-first workhorse profile.

The first-generation Mahindra Pik-Up features a rugged, utility-focused body style available in single-cab and dual-cab configurations with a tall, upright stance. It sports a utilitarian front fascia dominated by a tooth-style mesh grille, prominent rectangular headlights, and a distinctive functional bonnet scoop. The side profile displays squared-off wheel arches, side steps, and a conventional high-sided load tub or cab-chassis layout, riding on 16-inch steel or alloy wheels. Vertical tail lights frame the tailgate at the rear, accentuating its traditional, no-nonsense commercial design.

The Mahindra Scorpio-N is a large, tall-stance 5-door ladder-frame SUV featuring an upright profile and high-set sculpted bonnet. Its front fascia is defined by a bold multi-slat grille carrying the manufacturer's emblem, flanked by signature double-barrel LED projector headlamps and distinct C-shaped LED daytime running lights framing the lower bumper. The rear showcases vertically stacked LED tail lamps alongside a side-hinged tailgate. The exterior is complemented by prominent roof rails, skid plates, and diamond-cut alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches depending on the specification.

The Mahindra XUV 3XO features a short, stout, and athletic five-door compact SUV body style with a high bonnet line. Its front fascia is defined by a wide grille flanked by striking LED headlights and C-shaped daytime running lights. The rear is anchored by a distinctive full-width infinity LED light bar across the tailgate. Depending on the variant, it rides on 16-inch or 17-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels, complemented by fixed roof rails and an available contrasting black roof with a panoramic glass sunroof.

The first-generation Mahindra XUV500 is a five-door medium SUV featuring a muscular stance with a high bonnet line, flared wheel arches, and a rising beltline. The front end showcases an aggressive grille flanked by wraparound projector headlights integrated with distinctive claw-like styling elements and vertical or low-mounted fog lights. Its profile is characterized by sculpted body side creases and 17-inch alloy wheels, while the rear features a contoured tailgate, a roof spoiler, and split-design tail light clusters.

The Mahindra XUV700 features a modern medium SUV body style with a muscular stance, prominent rear wheel haunches, and flush-fitting smart door handles that retract into the bodywork. The front end is dominated by a prominent vertical-slatted grille housing the Twin Peaks logo, flanked by sharp LED clear-view headlamps with distinctive C-shaped LED daytime running light extensions flowing down into the bumper. At the rear, it sports sharp arrow-tip LED tail lights and a tailgate spoiler, riding on 18-inch alloy wheels beneath a sweeping roofline equipped with a large panoramic sunroof.

The Maserati Ghibli M157 is a four-door executive sedan featuring a coupe-like roofline, a low-slung stance, and frameless door glass. Its front end is dominated by an aggressive concave grille housing the prominent Trident emblem, flanked by swept-back headlights.
