The rear incorporates wraparound LED tail lights, a subtly integrated boot lid spoiler, and quad exhaust outlets. Distinctive side profile details include triple fender vents and muscular rear haunches, complemented by multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Maserati GranCabrio (M145) features a classic two-door convertible body style with a long hood, sculpted flanks accented by triple front-fender vents, and a tailored multi-layer fabric soft top. Its front fascia is defined by an oval concave grille housing vertical chrome slats and a central Trident emblem, flanked by swept-back bi-xenon headlights. The rear displays triangular LED-accented tail lamps and quad oval exhaust outlets integrated into the lower bumper. It typically rides on multi-spoke 20-inch alloy wheels.

The Maserati GranCabrio (M189) is a 2-door luxury convertible featuring a long, sculpted clamshell hood, a low-slung stance with a prominent oval grille bearing the iconic trident logo, and distinct vertical LED headlights. It is styled with a power-operated fabric soft-top roof, smooth fuselage-like door panels, and muscular rear fenders. The rear is fitted with wide wraparound LED tail lights, dual twin exhaust outlets, and rides on staggered 20-inch front and 21-inch alloy wheels.

The M145 Maserati GranTurismo is a low-slung, two-door luxury coupe featuring classic grand tourer proportions with a long hood and set-back cabin. Its front end is defined by an oval-shaped concave grille bearing the prominent Trident logo, flanked by swept-back headlights that stretch back over the front fenders. The side profile exhibits muscular haunches, sweeping character lines, and triple fender vents. At the rear, it features wide triangular tail lights, dual or quad exhaust outlets depending on the variant, and alloy wheels typically ranging from 19 to 20 inches.

The Maserati GranTurismo (M189) is a sleek two-door coupe featuring a long, clamshell bonnet, muscular rear wheel arches, and a low, wide stance. Up front, it showcases a prominent oval grille bearing the iconic Trident logo, flanked by vertically oriented, swept-back LED headlights. The profile is punctuated by traditional triple side air vents on the front guards, while the rear highlights horizontal LED tail lights and staggered alloy wheels (20-inch front, 21-inch rear).

The Maserati Grecale is a 5-door luxury SUV featuring a low, imposing front grille flanked by vertically-oriented LED headlights inspired by the MC20 supercar. Its flowing, muscular body lines present a coupe-like roofline, a wide stance with wheels pushed to the corners, and clean flank surfacing. The rear is distinguished by boomerang-shaped tail lights reminiscent of the historic 3200 GT, complemented by quad exhaust tips on performance variants.

The Maserati Levante M161 is a 5-door luxury SUV featuring a sweeping, coupe-like roofline, athletic proportions, and distinctive frameless door windows. Its front fascia is dominated by a deep concave-vertical-slat grille carrying the prominent Trident emblem, flanked by slim, swept-back headlights. At the rear, it sports boomerang-shaped LED tail lights and quad exhaust outlets. The exterior sits on large alloy wheels ranging from 19 to 21 inches, complemented by fender vents on the front guards.

The Maserati MC20 is a low-slung, mid-engine two-door sports car featuring dramatic upward-opening butterfly doors and a clean, sculptural carbon-fibre composite body. Its front end showcases a low grille and sleek, horizontally-oriented LED headlights without aggressive over-styled vents, while the rear features wide haunches, slim LED tail lights, dual exhaust outlets, and a clear engine cover. It rides on 20-inch alloy wheels with a low-profile stance and incorporates subtle C-pillar Trident branding.

The sixth-generation Maserati Quattroporte is a large, flowing four-door luxury sedan featuring a low-slung profile, frameless door glass, and signature triple side air vents on the front guards. The front is defined by a prominent concave vertical-slat grille bearing the Trident emblem, flanked by sharp, wraparound headlamps. Its rear end incorporates wrap-around LED tail lights and a lower bumper housing dual twin-exhaust outlets. Distinctive details include triangular C-pillars with the Saetta logo and large alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 21 inches.

The Mazda BT-50 (UP/UR generation) dual-cab and single-cab ute features rounded, passenger-car-inspired body contours contrasting with its rugged mechanical platform. It is characterized by sweeping, leaf-shaped headlights, a smiling multi-slat chrome front grille, and prominent undulating side character lines flowing into flared wheel arches. The rear exhibits simple, wraparound horizontal tail lights and a utilitarian tailgate configuration.

The Mazda BT-50 (TF generation) is offered in single-cab, freestyle-cab, and dual-cab ute body styles with muscular, curvaceous proportions influenced by Mazda's 'Kodo' design language. The front fascia features a prominent, deep-set chrome or dark-accented grille flanked by swept-back LED headlights. At the rear, it sports vertically-oriented tail lights framing a clean tailgate panel. Riding on robust alloy or steel wheels, the exterior balances rugged utility lines with smooth, passenger-car-inspired surfacing.

The Mazda CX-3 (DK generation) is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a raised ride height, heavily sculpted body lines, and protective black plastic cladding wrapping the lower bumpers and wheel arches. It is characterized by a prominent signature wing grille flanked by sleek, swept-back headlights, and a tapered roofline that gives it a dynamic, coupe-like stance. Depending on the grade, it rides on 16-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and features wraparound tail lights and a compact tailgate.

The Mazda CX-30 (DM generation) is a 5-door compact SUV featuring a sleek, coupe-like sloping roofline and prominent dark plastic body cladding along its lower perimeter. It showcases a wide, dark mesh grille framed by a signature wing that flows into slim, angular LED headlights. The rear features tapered, circular-accented LED tail lights and a subtle tailgate spoiler. Depending on the specification tier, it rides on 16-, 17-, or 18-inch alloy wheels.

The first-generation Mazda CX-5 features a five-door medium SUV body with an athletic stance characterized by curved sheet metal and pronounced wheel arches. The front end showcases a prominent five-bar mesh grille framed by swept-back, teardrop-shaped headlights. At the rear, it is fitted with wrap-around, angular tail lamps and a subtle roof spoiler. Riding on alloy wheels, the exterior design incorporates a rising beltline and flowing window graphics.

The KF-generation Mazda CX-5 is a 5-door medium SUV featuring a sleek, athletic silhouette with clean, sculpted body panels and minimal sharp creases. It is characterized by a prominent mesh-pattern front grille framed by a thick chrome wing that extends underneath slim, wraparound LED headlights. The rear profile incorporates tapered horizontal tail lights and a heavily raked rear window line, while higher trim grades in Australia feature distinct body-colored or gloss-black lower wheel arch and bumper moldings paired with multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Mazda CX-60 (KH generation) is a 5-door medium SUV characterized by a long-bonnet, rear-biased stance emphasizing its longitudinal engine layout. The front fascia features a wide, prominent grille flanked by slim, horizontal LED headlights integrated with distinctive L-shaped daytime running lights. At the rear, it has sleek, wraparound horizontal tail lights and a sculpted tailgate. Depending on the specification grade, it rides on 18-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels, with higher variants featuring body-coloured or contrasting gloss-black wheel arches and lower cladding.

The Mazda CX-70 is a large 5-door SUV characterized by an assertive, long-proportioned body style with a prominent upright grille framed by slim, adaptive LED headlights. It features high-gloss black or body-coloured lower body cladding, muscular rear haunches, and 21-inch alloy wheels filling the arches. The rear end is styled with horizontal LED tail lights, a roof spoiler, and a hands-free power tailgate, while the roofline incorporates a standard panoramic sunroof and a shark-fin antenna.

The Mazda CX-8 is a 5-door, long-wheelbase SUV featuring an elongated profile, a sloping roofline, and a prominent Kodo-design stance. It showcases a wide signature wing grille—updated with horizontal slats or a block-mesh pattern depending on the year—flanked by slim, angular LED headlamps. The rear features wraparound combination tail lights connected by a clean tailgate contour, riding on 17-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels.

The Mazda CX-80 is a five-door, three-row SUV featuring an elongated, sophisticated silhouette with a long wheelbase and a prominent, upright front fascia. It is styled with a wide mesh grille flanked by slim LED headlamps, and a clean tail with horizontal LED tail lights wrapping into the rear quarter panels. Depending on the grade, it sits on 18-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels and features a long roofline designed to maximize passenger space.

The Mazda CX-9 (TC generation) features a large 5-door SUV body with sleek, elongated proportions and a prominent wheelbase. It is styled with a signature large, dark mesh or horizontal-slat front grille framed by chrome wings that extend into slim, wraparound LED headlights. The rear showcases sleek, horizontal tail lights linked by subtle detailing, twin or quad exhaust outlets depending on the spec, and a steeply raked rear window. Depending on the model grade, it rides on 18-inch or large 20-inch alloy wheels and features a clean roofline with an integrated rear spoiler.

The Mazda CX-90 is a large, imposing 5-door SUV featuring long-hood proportions that accommodate its longitudinal engine layout. It showcases a prominent black mesh grille framed by a signature chrome wing, flanked by sleek, wraparound LED headlights. The rear features slender, horizontal LED tail lights stretching across the tailgate, complemented by clean body surfacing and large 19-inch or 21-inch alloy wheels.

The Mazda2 hatchback features a compact, dynamic five-door stance characterized by Kodo design proportions, featuring a prominent front grille flanked by swept-back headlights and a curving, fluid body profile. Later updates introduced body-coloured or black grilles with asymmetrical colour accents, matching highlights on the rear bumper, and sleek tail light clusters. Depending on the grade, it sits on 15-inch or multi-spoke alloy wheels and can be equipped with a contrasting black roof film and a modern shark-fin antenna.

The Mazda3 BM/BN five-door hatchback features a low-slung, athletic stance characterized by fluid 'Kodo' body sculpting, arched fenders, and a swept-back roofline. It is defined by a large, prominent shield-shaped front grille framed by a chrome signature wing that extends under its sharp, wraparound headlights. The rear sports compact, horizontally oriented tail lights, a body-colored roof spoiler, and a rounded tailgate layout. Alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches complete its dynamic exterior proportions.

The Mazda3 BP 5-door hatchback features a low-slung, organic profile characterized by a dramatic, thick C-pillar and voluptuous body curves. It sports a wide, dark-finished signature wing grille flanked by ultra-slim LED headlights, and a minimalist tail featuring circular twin-element LED tail lights. The rear hatch slopes steeply beneath a subtle roof spoiler, while the stance is rounded out by alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches tucked beneath muscular arches.

The third-generation Mazda 6 sedan features a sleek, fastback-inspired four-door profile with a cab-rearward stance and a long, sculpted bonnet. Its front fascia is defined by a prominent, wing-accented grille framed by sharp, wraparound LED headlights. The body exhibits fluid character lines running along the flanks, tapering into compact tail lights connected by a chrome trim strip. It sits on large alloy wheels (up to 19 inches) and features a clean roofline flowing smoothly into a short, integrated boot lid.

The Mazda MX-30 (DR) is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a coupe-like sloping roofline and distinctive pillarless 'Freestyle' rear-hinged doors. It is characterized by a deeply recessed, slender front grille flanked by sharp, horizontal LED headlights and a broad lower bumper clad in dark plastic. The rear showcases recessed circular tail lights set beneath a raked tailgate topped by a subtle roof spoiler. Its side profile is marked by chunky contrasting wheel arches housing 18-inch alloy wheels and thick C-pillars bearing embossed Mazda lettering.

The Mazda MX-5 ND is a compact 2-door roadster characterized by low-slung, aggressive proportions with sharply sculpted body creases and a short rear deck. It features a wide, low-mounted smiling grille flanked by ultra-slim, angular LED headlamps that sweep back into the front guards. The rear incorporates rounded LED tail lights with distinct circular signature elements. It rides on 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels and utilizes either a manual folding fabric soft-top or a rigid folding targa roof structure (RF variant).

The Mazda MX-5 ND RF features a two-door fastback body style with a power-retractable hardtop roof and signature flying buttresses that mimic a coupe silhouette. It features aggressive, swept-back LED headlights flanking a low-set, wide grille, alongside slim horizontal rear tail lights. The athletic proportions include a long bonnet, short rear deck, and 17-inch alloy wheels.

The McLaren 540C coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamic body with a sculpted bonnet flanked by distinctive LED headlights and lower aero blades. It utilizes signature dihedral doors with floating tendons that channel air into side intakes, feeding into flying buttresses at the rear. The tail incorporates slim LED light strips, a unique rear diffuser, and twin exhaust tips. It rides on staggered 19-inch front and 20-inch rear alloy wheels.

The McLaren 570GT features a two-door coupé body style with signature upward-swinging dihedral doors and a low-slung, aerodynamic nose. Its front end is defined by teardrop-shaped headlights and a sculpted lower splitter, while the side profile incorporates deep air intakes integrated into the rear fenders. Uniquely, the roofline flows into a panoramic glass sunroof and a side-hinged, carbon-framed glass rear hatch that opens to reveal an additional touring deck. The rear fascia sports a slightly elevated integrated spoiler lip, sleek LED tail light strips, and dual exhaust outlets exiting beneath the bumper.

The McLaren 570S coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamic two-door body style equipped with dramatic dihedral doors and a carbon-fibre monocoque structure. Its front end is defined by sleek, teardrop-shaped LED headlamps that echo the brand's Speedmark logo, accompanied by large lower intake channels. The rear sports slim, wraparound LED tail light strips flanking an aggressive diffuser and dual exhaust outlets. It rides on staggered alloy wheels (19-inch front, 20-inch rear) and features flying buttresses on the rear pillars that channel airflow over the glass hatch.

The McLaren 570S Spider features a low-slung, aerodynamic convertible body style with iconic upward-opening dihedral doors. It incorporates a two-piece retractable hardtop roof, tear-shaped LED headlights with sweeping daytime running lights, and a sharply sculpted front bumper with deep air intakes. The rear profile is characterized by slim LED tail lights, a slightly raised rear spoiler, and a prominent diffuser framing dual exhaust outlets. It rides on staggered 19-inch front and 20-inch rear alloy wheels.

The McLaren 600LT coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamic two-door body style with signature dihedral doors. It is distinguished by an extended 'Longtail' carbon-fibre splitter, enlarged side air intakes, and unique top-exit exhaust pipes emerging directly through the rear deck. The front end showcases angular LED headlamps flanking a low nose, while the rear integrates a fixed carbon-fibre wing above slim LED tail lights and an aggressive diffuser.

The McLaren 600LT Spider is a two-door convertible featuring a lightweight carbon-fibre Monocell II chassis and signature dihedral doors. Its elongated 'Longtail' body incorporates an aggressive aerodynamic package with an extended front splitter, a fixed rear wing, and distinctive top-exit exhaust pipes emerging behind the retractable hardtop's rear buttresses. It rides on ultra-lightweight alloy wheels framing carbon-ceramic brakes, and features slim LED headlights alongside wraparound rear taillight blades.

The McLaren 650S coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamic two-door body style with dihedral doors and a fixed carbon-fibre roof structure. Its front fascia incorporates striking, 'boomerang'-shaped LED headlights inspired by the McLaren P1, matched with large side air intakes and a sculpted front bumper. At the rear, it features slim horizontal LED tail lights, an active airbrake spoiler, and dual-exhaust outlets exiting high in the bumper. The car rides on lightweight alloy wheels (19-inch front, 20-inch rear) framing carbon-ceramic brake discs.

The McLaren 650S Spider is a two-door convertible featuring striking dihedral doors and a three-piece retractable hard-top roof. Its low-slung stance incorporates P1-inspired swept-back LED headlights and a clean front bumper design with an integrated splitter. The rear features slim horizontal LED tail lights flanking a deployable active airbrake wing, complemented by lightweight alloy wheels (19-inch front, 20-inch rear) hiding carbon-ceramic brakes.

The McLaren 675LT coupe features a lightweight carbon-fibre body with an elongated rear profile, a prominent carbon front splitter with endplates, and extended side skirts. It is equipped with swept-back headlights, large side air intakes, ultra-lightweight 10-spoke forged alloy wheels, and an active 'Longtail' airbrake that is significantly larger than the standard 650S variant. The rear end showcases a dramatic carbon-fibre diffuser and circular twin titanium exhaust tips exiting centrally through a heavily vented lower bumper.

The McLaren 675LT Spider features a two-door convertible body style with an extended 'Longtail' carbon-fibre rear deck and an active aerodynamic airbrake wing. It shares the low-slung proportions, sweep-back LED headlamps, and dramatic side air intakes of the 650S architecture, but is distinguished by an aggressive carbon-fibre front splitter and a lightweight vented polycarbonate engine cover. The exterior sits on 10-spoke ultra-lightweight forged alloy wheels (19-inch front and 20-inch rear) framing carbon-ceramic brakes, complemented by a retractable hardtop roof.

The McLaren 720S coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamic body style with dramatic dihedral doors that incorporate a double-skin design to channel airflow. Its front end is defined by striking, recessed LED headlamps integrated into deep eye-socket air intakes. In profile, it showcases a teardrop-shaped glasshouse cockpit and sculpted flanks. The rear is dominated by slim, wraparound LED tail lights and a full-width active deployable rear spoiler. It rides on 19-inch front and 20-inch rear alloy wheels and features a transparent engine cover.

The McLaren 720S Spider features a low-slung, aerodynamic convertible body style with dramatic dihedral doors and distinctive glazed flying buttresses. It incorporates ultra-slim LED headlights integrated into deep, functional cooling sockets, a sleek wraparound windscreen, and a one-piece carbon fibre retractable hardtop. The rear showcases thin, elongated LED tail lights stretching across a louvered mesh grill section beneath an active rear spoiler/airbrake. It rides on staggered lightweight alloy wheels (19-inch front, 20-inch rear) that accentuate its aggressive, sculptural stance.

The McLaren 750S coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamic two-door body style with signature dihedral doors. At the front, it sports narrowed 'eye-socket' LED headlight apertures integrated with air intakes alongside an extended front splitter. The rear profile is dominated by a larger, active carbon-fibre rear wing and mesh-covered bumper vents that expose mechanical elements. It rides on ultra-lightweight forged alloy wheels and features a sweeping glasshouse roofline tapering into the rear deck.

The McLaren 750S Spider is a low-slung, mid-engine convertible featuring signature dihedral doors and a power-retractable hardtop housed under body-colored tonneau buttresses. Its aerodynamics include slim, elongated LED headlamps inset within distinct front 'eye socket' intakes, alongside a prominent front splitter. The rear is defined by a larger, active carbon-fibre rear wing and a mesh grille fascia flanked by narrow LED tail lights. It rides on lightweight alloy wheels—19 inches at the front and 20 inches at the rear—with visible side air intakes carved into the lower flanks.

The McLaren 765LT coupe features an aggressive, low-slung two-door body style characterized by an extended rear 'Longtail' profile and extensive carbon fibre aerodynamics. It showcases slim, elongated LED headlights flanking deep front bumper intakes, a prominent front splitter, and an active rear wing positioned higher than the standard 720S. The rear end is defined by a massive carbon diffuser and quad-exit exhaust pipes mounted high centrally in the rear deck. It rides on ultra-lightweight 10-spoke alloy wheels wrapped around a heavily track-focused silhouette.

The McLaren 765LT Spider is a low-slung, two-door convertible featuring an electronically operated single-piece carbon-fibre retractable hardtop. Its aggressive aerodynamic profile includes an extended front splitter, deep carbon-fibre side skirts, and a prominent active rear wing. The front fascia showcases slim, swept-back LED headlamps flanking large cooling intakes, while the rear integrates a wraparound bumper housing a quad-exit titanium exhaust system. It rides on lightweight 19-inch front and 20-inch rear alloy wheels wrapped in track-focused rubber.

The McLaren Artura coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamic two-door body style equipped with signature dihedral doors and crisp proportions. It showcases slim, wedge-shaped LED headlights flanking a sleek front nose cone, alongside deep side air intakes sculpted into the carbon-composite bodywork. The rear is dominated by slim horizontal LED tail lights, an integrated diffuser, and elevated dual exhaust outlets, while the roofline flows cleanly down into the rear decklid over lightweight alloy wheels.

The McLaren Artura Spider features a low-slung, sculpted two-door convertible body style with an electrically retractable hardtop and forward-hinged dihedral doors. Its front end showcases a signature hammerhead nose, slim LED headlamps with integrated air intakes, and distinct front fender louven vents. The rear integrates flying buttresses and a carbon-fibre tonneau cover, housing a flat-topped tail light strip beneath a mesh engine cover.

The McLaren GT is a low-slung, two-door coupe featuring signature front-hinged dihedral doors and a teardrop cabin profile that stretches back over a carbon-fibre rear deck. It possesses a clean, aerodynamic front fascia with swept-back LED headlamps, side air intakes integrated into the lower body panels, and a distinctive rear end topped by a front-hinged, full-length glazed tailgate. It rides on 20-inch alloy wheels with a low-slung stance and elongated rear overhangs relative to traditional mid-engine supercars.

The McLaren GTS coupe features a low-slung, aerodynamically sculpted body with forward-hinged dihedral doors and a distinctive 'hammerhead' front styling featuring pronounced air intakes. In profile, it has a cab-forward silhouette, a long glazed rear tailgate opening over a mid-mounted engine luggage area, and taller air scoops integrated into the rear fenders. It rides on 20-inch front and 21-inch rear forged alloy wheels, complemented by slim LED headlamps and a full-width rear fascia framing dual exhaust tips.

The W176 Mercedes-Benz A-Class hatchback features a low-slung, dynamic five-door stance with a coupé-like roofline and sweeping character lines along its flanks. The front end is defined by a prominent diamond-pattern or single-bar grille bearing the central three-pointed star, flanked by swept-back headlights with distinct LED daytime running light signatures. At the rear, it features wraparound LED tail light clusters and a bumper design incorporating integrated exhaust tips on higher trims. Sportier variants like the AMG Line add aggressive body kits, larger alloy wheels, and lowered proportions.

The Mercedes-Benz A-Class W177 hatchback features a 5-door compact layout with low-slung, dynamic proportions and a lengthened wheelbase. The front end is defined by a shark-nose profile, a wide hexagonal or diamond-pattern grille, and sharply angled, low-profile LED headlights. The rear incorporates two-piece, tapered LED tail lights that widen the appearance of the tailgate. Australian models are predominantly equipped with AMG Line exterior styling featuring aggressive bumper sculpting, side skirts, and prominent alloy wheels.

The Mercedes-Benz A-Class Sedan (V177) features a compact, four-door three-box profile with smooth, flowing roofline contours and short overhangs. The front fascia is dominated by a low-slung, sharp-angled grille flanked by sleek, angular LED headlights with integrated daytime running lights. At the rear, it sports two-piece horizontal wrap-around LED tail lights, a clean boot lid with an integrated lip spoiler, and alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches depending on the trim line.

The Mercedes-AMG GT coupe features a classic long-hood, cab-rearward silhouette with two front-hinged doors and a fastback sloping roofline leading into a practical tailgate. It showcases swept-back LED headlights flanking a wide grille—transitioning from a single horizontal slat design to a prominent vertical-slat Panamericana style during its lifecycle—alongside a low hood with distinct power domes. The rear is defined by slim horizontal LED tail lights, broad wheel arches, and a discreetly integrated active rear spoiler. Staggered alloy wheels (typically 19-inch front and 19- or 20-inch rear) and signature side vents behind the front wheel arches complete its athletic stance.

The Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe (X290) features a low-slung, fastback sedan body style with four frameless doors and a sleek liftback tailgate. The front end is dominated by a prominent Panamericana grille with vertical slats flanked by swept-back Multibeam LED headlights. Its side profile showcases muscular proportions, a flowing roofline, and large alloy wheels, while the rear incorporates narrow horizontal LED tail lights and an active deploying rear spoiler.

The Mercedes-AMG GT Coupe (C192) features a fastback two-door body style characterized by a prominent long hood, a sharply raked windshield, and a sweeping, muscular roofline that tapers down to a rounded rear. At the front, it displays a large, aggressive Panamericana vertical-slat grille flanked by angular, swept-back LED headlamps and a prominent lower A-wing apron. The rear end is defined by slim, horizontal triangular tail lights and an active retractable rear spoiler. Rolling on large alloy wheels, its stance is wide and low, blending traditional grand tourer proportions with athletic curves.

The Mercedes-AMG SL (R232) is a 2-door 2+2 convertible roadster featuring a classic long hood, short rear deck, and a lightweight multi-layer fabric soft top. Its aggressive front end showcases a signature wide Panamericana grille with vertical slats, flanked by sharp, swept-back triangular LED headlights. The sleek body side profile is accented by flush, power-retractable door handles and large 21-inch alloy wheels. At the rear, it features slim horizontal LED tail lights, quad exhaust outlets, and an active rear spoiler that deploys flush from the trunk lid.

The W246 Mercedes-Benz B-Class features a five-door compact MPV body style with tall-roof proportions and a heavily raked windshield. The front fascia displays a two-louver grille flanked by swept-back headlights, updated during the 2014 facelift to feature a diamond-pattern grille and integrated LED daytime running lights. The side profile exhibits a rising beltline, aerodynamic contouring, and alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches, while the rear highlights wrap-around horizontal tail lights and a practical flat tailgate.

The W205 Mercedes-Benz C-Class sedan features a sleek, aerodynamic four-door body style with fluid, cab-rearward proportions heavily inspired by the flagship S-Class. At the front, it showcases a prominent grille housing a central three-pointed star (or a traditional upright grille on exclusive trims) flanked by swept-back LED headlights. The rear profile is defined by curved, soft shoulders and rounded LED tail lights, while alloy wheel sizes range from 16 to 19 inches depending on the specification.

The W206 C-Class sedan features a sleek, cab-rearward silhouette with a longer wheelbase and shorter front overhang compared to its predecessor. The front end is characterized by angled LED headlights flanking a wide grille featuring the prominent central three-pointed star. At the rear, slim, two-piece triangular tail lights extend horizontally onto the boot lid. The smooth body sides feature clean, minimal character lines, complemented by alloy wheel options and a low, flowing roofline.

The Mercedes-Benz C-Class Cabriolet (A205) features a two-door convertible body style with a sleek, low-slung profile and an acoustic fabric soft-top. It has a prominent diamond-pattern or single-louvre grille flanked by sweeping LED headlights, and a rear featuring wrap-around horizontal LED tail lights with distinct light signatures. Riding on alloy wheels, its proportions are defined by a long sculpted bonnet, frameless door glass, and a clean rear deck lid housing the folding roof mechanism.

The Mercedes-Benz C-Class Coupe (C205) features a sleek, two-door fastback body style with a long hood, a low-slung sloping roofline, and frameless side windows. The front showcases a prominent diamond-pattern grille paired with swept-back LED headlights, complemented in Australia by standard aggressive AMG Line lower bumpers and side skirts. The rear is defined by rounded, horizontally oriented wrap-around LED tail lights and a short, clean decklid. It rides on athletic alloy wheels, with distinct wheel arches and fluid sheet metal emphasizing its grand-tourer proportions.

The S205 Mercedes-Benz C-Class Estate features a sleek 5-door station wagon body with flowing, curved rooflines and soft character lines along its flanks. It is characterized by a prominent front grille featuring a central three-pointed star, flanked by rounded LED headlights. The rear incorporates teardrop-shaped, wrap-around tail lights and a heavily raked tailgate with an integrated roof spoiler. Alloy wheel designs range from clean multi-spoke layouts to sporty AMG variants.

The Mercedes-Benz C-Class Estate (S206) is a five-door luxury station wagon featuring a sleek, elongated profile with smooth body surfacing and a dynamic sloping roofline. At the front, it showcases a wide trapezoidal grille adorned with a prominent three-pointed star and slim, angular LED headlamps. The rear end is defined by two-piece, triangle-shaped horizontal tail lights that extend into the tailgate. It rides on flush alloy wheels and incorporates subtle chrome window framing and integrated roof rails.

The Mercedes-Benz C117 CLA-Class features a low-slung, four-door fastback sedan body style with a heavily raked roofline and frameless door windows. It is characterized by swept-back headlights flanking a prominent single-louver grille featuring a diamond-pattern mesh insert. The rear profile showcases wraparound LED tail lights, a swooping boot lid with an integrated lip spoiler, and lower bumper styling incorporating integrated exhaust finishers. Side proportions display a distinctive character line sweeping upward across the doors, paired with multi-spoke alloy wheel options.

The C118 Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class features a low-slung, four-door fastback body style with a sweeping roofline and frameless doors. It has a shark-nose front fascia sporting a low-set diamond-pattern grille flanked by sharp, angular LED headlights. The rear profile is defined by slim, two-piece triangular tail lights and a sculpted boot lid with an integrated lip spoiler. The side profile highlights clean proportions, minimal overhangs, and alloy wheel options ranging up to large diameter multi-spoke designs paired with a planted stance.

The Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class Shooting Brake features a low-slung, five-door station wagon body with a sweeping, coupe-like roofline and frameless side windows. The front showcases a wide diamond-pattern grille flanked by sleek, angular LED headlights, while the rear exhibits slim, two-piece horizontal tail lights and an integrated tailgate spoiler. It rides on alloy wheels up to 18 inches with athletic proportions, highlighted by a long bonnet, a steeply raked windshield, and a gently tapering rear hatch profile.

The Mercedes-Benz CLE-Class coupe features a sleek, two-door fastback silhouette with a low-slung, forward-leaning 'shark nose' front profile and power domes on its long bonnet. It is styled with a low-positioned, A-shaped single-bar radiator grille accompanied by streamlined, swept-back LED headlights. The rear showcases a muscular stance with two-piece LED tail lights connected by a dark glossy trim element. Fluid character lines run along its flanks above large alloy wheels, accentuating its athletic mid-size proportions.

The Mercedes-Benz CLE-Class Cabriolet (A236) is a two-door sports convertible featuring a sweeping silhouette, a multi-layer acoustic fabric soft top, and a low-slung stance. It is characterised by a prominent shark-nose front grille accented by a central three-pointed star, flanked by sharply angled LED headlamps. The rear exhibits slim, two-part LED tail lights connected across the boot lid by a dark trim element, sitting above athletic body styling and large alloy wheels. Distinctive open-air features include a wind-deflecting AIRCAP system above the windscreen and neck-level AIRSCARF heating integrated into the front seats.

The C218 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class sedan features a sleek, four-door fastback body style with a long bonnet, a heavily raked roofline, and frameless side windows. Its front end is defined by a prominent upright grille housing a central three-pointed star, flanked by swept-back angular headlights (upgraded to Multibeam LEDs in the facelift). The profile is characterized by a distinctive 'dropping line' running down the flanks above muscular, flared rear wheel arches. The rear features wrap-around LED tail lights connected by a clean bootlid contour and dual exhaust outlets.

The C257 Mercedes-Benz CLS features a four-door fastback sedan body style characterized by a low, sweeping roofline and muscular proportions. It showcases an aggressive shark-nose front end with a wide, downward-expanding diamond-pattern grille and low-profile, angular LED headlamps. The rear features split, horizontally-oriented triangular tail lights set above a clean bumper design, while the profile flows over alloy wheels and a sleek, arching greenhouse.

The tenth-generation Mercedes-Benz E-Class sedan (W213) features a flowing, coupe-like four-door silhouette with a long wheelbase and short overhangs. The front end is dominated by a rounded grille—varying from traditional louvres with a bonnet star to sportier diamond or single-louvre variants with a central star—flanked by swept-back LED headlights. The rear showcases horizontal, two-piece wraparound LED tail lights that feature a distinctive crystalline 'stardust' effect. Its athletic stance is complemented by clean shoulder lines, sculpted power domes on the bonnet, and alloy wheel options ranging up to large AMG multi-spoke designs.

The W214 Mercedes-Benz E-Class sedan features a traditional three-box silhouette with a heavily raked windscreen, a sweeping coupe-like roofline, and flush-fitting door handles. Its front end is distinguished by a wide grille linked to the headlamps by a high-gloss black panel reminiscent of Mercedes' EQ models. The rear incorporates a short boot lid and split tail-lights featuring an illuminated three-pointed star motif. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging up to 21 inches and features clean, taut body lines along its flanks.

The Mercedes-Benz E-Class Cabriolet (A238) features a two-door convertible body style with a multi-layer acoustic fabric soft top. Its clean, low-profile silhouette includes a diamond-patterned grille with a central star, swept-back LED headlights, and frameless side windows. The muscular rear is characterized by slim, two-piece LED tail lights with a crystalline jet-engine glow effect. The exterior is finished with polished aluminum trim around the windscreen frame and soft-top compartment, sitting on alloy wheels up to 20 inches in diameter.

The Mercedes-Benz E-Class Coupe (C238) features a sleek two-door pillarless body style with a flowing roofline and frameless side windows. Its front fascia is defined by a low, wide diamond-pattern grille and swept-back LED headlights, complemented by soft, curved body side panels devoid of harsh creases. At the rear, it sports elongated, horizontal multi-element LED tail lights and a rounded boot lid, riding on large alloy wheels that accentuate its grand touring proportions.

The Mercedes-Benz E-Class Estate (S213) is a five-door luxury station wagon characterized by a long wheelbase, short overhangs, and a sloping, aerodynamic roofline. It features a prominent front grille flanked by swept-back LED headlights with signature dual-eyebrow daytime running light graphics. The rear showcases wraparound, two-section horizontal LED tail lights and a powered tailgate above a spacious cargo area. Alloy wheel designs and lower bumper styling vary across trims, ranging from clean executive layouts to aggressive AMG-Line body styling.

The Mercedes-Benz EQA (H243) is a compact 5-door electric SUV featuring a rounded, aerodynamic stance with short overhangs. At the front, it showcases a smooth, closed-off black gloss grille panel flanked by swept-back LED headlights, connected across the top by a distinctive full-width LED light bar. The rear profile is defined by a tapered tailgate with a continuous LED tail light strip running horizontally across the boot lid. It rides on large alloy wheels (typically ranging up to 20 inches) and features a sloping roofline finished with a subtle rear spoiler and flush roof rails.

The Mercedes-Benz EQB (X243) is a boxy, upright 5-door compact SUV featuring a long wheelbase and a glasshouse designed to maximize interior space. Its front end is distinguished by a enclosed gloss-black 'Black Panel' grille flanked by sleek LED headlamps, which are often connected across the front by a signature light bar. The rear profile showcases a flat tailgate with full-width LED tail lights, while the side profile is defined by flush lines, aluminum roof rails, and aerodynamic alloy wheels.

The Mercedes-Benz EQC (N293) features a five-door medium crossover SUV body style with smooth, coupe-like sloping roof proportions. At the front, it showcases a gloss-black enclosed grille panel seamlessly linked to wrap-around multibeam LED headlights by a distinct horizontal daytime running light band. The rear end is defined by a continuous, full-width LED light bar spanning the tailgate. Australian models commonly ride on large 20-inch or 21-inch alloy wheels and feature aerodynamic surfacing with flush trim details.

The Mercedes-Benz EQE sedan features a distinct 'one-bow' aerodynamic profile with cab-forward proportions and a high-arch roofline. Its smooth front fascia integrates a gloss-black panel enclosing swept-back LED headlights, while the rear showcases a continuous, curved LED light bar spanning the width of the bootlid. Flush door handles and flush-fitting alloy wheels complement its minimalist, low-drag body styling.

The Mercedes-Benz EQE SUV features a five-door, cab-forward 'one-bow' aerodynamic crossover silhouette with smooth, rounded proportions and flush door handles. Its front end is dominated by a glossy black closed-off panel grille featuring a constellation of small three-pointed stars, flanked by swept-back LED headlights. At the rear, it has a continuous LED light bar linking curved, helix-patterned tail lights. The exterior is fitted with large alloy wheels (ranging up to 21-inch AMG multi-spoke designs) and features a panoramic glass roof.

The Mercedes-Benz EQS (V297) is a large, aerodynamic fastback sedan featuring a distinct 'one-bow' arched roofline and four frameless doors. It is characterized by a smooth, blanked-off front panel seamlessly integrated with slim, swept-back LED headlights, and connected tail lights utilizing an edge-to-edge helix light bar design. Rolling on large alloy wheels ranging up to 21 inches, its low-slung, highly streamlined silhouette yields an exceptionally low drag coefficient.

The Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV features a large, aerodynamic five-door body style characterised by a sweeping 'bow' roofline and smooth, bulbous proportions. The front end showcases a glossy black blanked-off grille panel integrated seamlessly with sleek, angular LED headlights connected by a signature light bar. At the rear, continuous helix-pattern LED tail lights stretch across the tailgate, while the profile is defined by flush door handles, large aerodynamic alloy wheels, and minimal body creases.

The Mercedes-Benz G-Class (W463) features an iconic, boxy, flat-panel body shape with an upright windscreen and external door hinges. It has a distinctive rectangular grille flanked by round LED headlights, a side-hinged rear tailgate carrying a full-sized spare wheel, and prominent flat-edged front fender indicators. The exterior profile is defined by high ground clearance, straight-line character creases, protective side rub strips, flat roof details, and large alloy wheels ranging from 19 to 22 inches.

The Mercedes-Benz G-Class (W465) retains its iconic, boxy, slab-sided five-door SUV silhouette with exposed door hinges and flared wheel arches. Up front, it features a traditional rectangular grille updated with four horizontal louvres, flanked by classic round LED headlights and mounted indicators on the front guards. Subtle aerodynamic updates include a revised windscreen pillar cladding and a lip spoiler on the leading edge of the roof. At the rear, it maintains a flat tailgate carrying a full-sized spare wheel enclosed in a hard cover, complemented by squircle-themed front and rear bumper inserts.

The Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class (X156) is a compact five-door crossover SUV featuring a low, coupe-like roofline, plastic body cladding, and a slightly raised stance. The front end is defined by a twin-slat chrome grille featuring a central three-pointed star and swept-back headlights with integrated fiber-optic daytime running lights. The side profile is characterized by sculpted body lines and pronounced wheel arches filled with alloy wheels ranging up to 19 inches. The rear showcases wraparound horizontal tail lights, a subtle tailgate spoiler, and a bumper integrated with a simulated underbody guard.

The H247 Mercedes-Benz GLA is a compact, upright luxury SUV featuring a rounded front grille with a central three-pointed star, flanked by swept-back LED headlights. Its profile showcases short overhangs, flowing rooflines with standard roof rails, and alloy wheels ranging from 18 inches upwards. The rear end is defined by a subtle floating roof spoiler and wraparound, two-piece horizontal LED tail lights.

The Mercedes-Benz GLB-Class (X247) features a distinctive, upright, boxy SUV body style with five doors and a flat roofline that maximizes interior headroom. Its proportions include a relatively long wheelbase relative to its compact overall length, contributing to short overhangs. The front end showcases a prominent rectangular grille flanked by angled LED headlights with integrated daytime running lamps. The rear features wraparound LED tail lights, a tailgate-mounted spoiler, and a flat vertical hatch leading to a practical cargo area. Alloy wheel designs typically range from 18 to 20 inches depending on the variant and styling package.

The Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class (X253) SUV features a smooth, rounded body style with a coupe-like greenhouse and a relatively short front overhang. Up front, it showcases an upright, three-dimensional radiator grille housing a central star emblem, flanked by swept-back headlights. The rear profile is defined by broad shoulders and rounded LED tail lights. It rides on alloy wheels and features a flowing roofline complemented by an available panoramic sunroof.

The Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class (X254) SUV features an aerodynamic five-door body style with smooth, flowing flank lines and a longer, planted stance. The front end showcases a wide grille featuring a central three-pointed star flanked by flattened, swept-back LED headlights. At the rear, it is equipped with slim, two-section horizontal LED tail lights linked by a dark trim element across a clean tailgate. It rides on large alloy wheels (ranging from 19 to 21 inches depending on the specification) and features short overhangs with optional aluminum-look running boards.

The Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class Coupe (C253) features a four-door SUV coupe body style defined by a distinctive, sweeping fastback roofline and a raked rear window. The front end is characterised by a prominent diamond-pattern grille centred around a large three-pointed star, flanked by angled LED headlights and aggressive AMG Line lower bumper styling. At the rear, it sports slim, horizontal LED tail lights that wrap into the haunches above a sculpted tailgate with an integrated lip spoiler. Australian-specification models commonly roll on large 20-inch alloy wheels and feature aluminium-look running boards along the lower sills.

The Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class Coupe (C254) is a five-door luxury SUV coupe featuring a low, sweeping roofline that flows dynamically into a prominent liftback tailgate with an integrated lip spoiler. Its front end is characterised by sharp, tapered LED headlights that connect directly to a wide grille accented by a three-pointed star pattern. The side profile exhibits muscular haunches, a cab-rearward stance, flush window lines, and aluminium-look running boards, riding typically on large alloy wheels. At the rear, slim horizontal LED tail lamps are linked by a dark trim element above a sculpted bumper incorporating integrated exhaust finishers.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class W166 SUV features a robust five-door body style with athletic, muscular proportions and a characteristic steeply raked C-pillar. The front fascia is defined by a large, upright grille featuring a central three-pointed star, flanked by angular LED headlights. The rear showcases rounded horizontal LED tail lights and a sculpted bumper with integrated exhaust outlets. Alloy wheel options range up to 21 inches, complemented by standard roof rails and subtle chrome exterior accents.

The V167 Mercedes-Benz GLE SUV features a cohesive, rounded body style with soft surfacing and a distinctively raked C-pillar reminiscent of its M-Class lineage. The front fascia is defined by an octagonal grille and rounded angular LED headlights, complemented by a broad lower intake. At the rear, it sports split, horizontal LED tail lights and a sculpted tailgate. The side profile exhibits clean body lines, alloy wheels ranging up to large AMG specifications, and an integrated roof spoiler.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class Coupe (C292) features a high-riding four-door SUV body style paired with a dramatic, steeply sloping fastback roofline. Up front, it showcases an upright single-louver or diamond-studded grille flanked by rounded, multi-element LED headlamps, sitting above a heavily sculpted bumper with large lower intakes. The rear is dominated by broad, muscular haunches, a high boot lid with an integrated lip spoiler, and slim horizontal tail lights connected by a chrome trim strip. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 22 inches, filling pronounced wheel arches that accentuate its aggressive, ground-hugging stance.

The Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class Coupe (C167) is a five-door luxury SUV coupe featuring a commanding stance, muscular haunches, and a sweeping, fastback-style sloping roofline. It incorporates an aggressive front fascia with a wide, single-louvre diamond or pin-pattern grille flanked by raked LED headlamps, and a clean tail featuring slender, two-part horizontal LED tail lights. Large alloy wheels ranging up to 22 inches fill the flared wheel arches, complementing its lower-slung, athletic proportions compared to the standard wagon variant.

The Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class X166 is a large five-door luxury SUV featuring a commanding, upright stance with muscular body contours and three rows of seating. The front fascia is dominated by a bold twin-louver grille carrying a prominent central three-pointed star, flanked by swept-back headlights with integrated angular LED daytime running lights. Its high-riding profile incorporates sweeping character lines, large alloy wheels, and standard roof rails, while the rear showcases wraparound LED tail lights and a chrome-accented bumper.

The Mercedes-Benz GLS-Class (X167) is a large 5-door luxury SUV characterized by a massive, upright octagonal front grille, rounded proportions, and sweeping LED headlights featuring multi-segment daytime running light signatures. Its side profile features clean surfacing over an extended wheelbase, large alloy wheels (ranging up to 22-inches), and flush roof rails. The rear is dominated by two-piece horizontal LED tail lights linked by a slender chrome strip, accented by a muscular shoulder line and a wide lower bumper apron.

The W222 S-Class sedan features a stately four-door fast-saloon profile characterized by a long sculpted bonnet, a sweeping domed roofline, and a prominent "dropping line" running down its flanks. The front is dominated by a large, upright chrome grille flanked by sleek, multi-beam LED headlights with integrated curved daytime running lights. The rear incorporates rounded C-pillars flowing into a short bootlid, framed by completely encased, multi-layer horizontal LED tail lights. Alloy wheel designs range up to large-diameter multi-spoke units, paired with lower bumper chrome highlights and integrated exhaust finishers.

The Mercedes-Benz S-Class sedan features a sleek, aerodynamic silhouette with a long wheelbase and clean, flush-fitting pop-out door handles. The front is defined by a large, prominent upright chrome grille flanked by sleek, angular LED headlights. At the rear, it sports distinctive horizontal, triangular tail lights that extend inward onto the boot lid.

The Mercedes-Benz S-Class Cabriolet (A217) is a large, two-door luxury convertible featuring a long, flowing hood, a low-slung cabin profile, and a multi-layer acoustic fabric soft top. The front end is defined by a sweeping grille containing the central three-pointed star, flanked by LED headlights and lower intakes that vary from elegant chrome-accented bars to aggressive AMG-specific bumpers. Along the sides, the vehicle exhibits muscular rear wheel arches, clean character lines, and large alloy wheels ranging up to 20 inches. The rear features sleek horizontal LED or advanced OLED tail lights, a subtle integrated boot-lid spoiler, and chrome exhaust finishers. Distinctive exterior elements include the acoustic soft top—which operates at speeds up to 50 km/h—alongside specialised wind-buffeting deflectors.

The Mercedes-Benz S-Class Coupe (C217) is a grand-touring, two-door hardtop featuring a pillarless profile, a long sculpted hood, and a gently sloping, low-slung roofline. The front fascia is defined by a wide diamond-pattern or vertical-slat Panamericana grille flanked by swept-back LED headlights, which could be optioned with crystalline 'Stardust' elements. At the rear, it features thin, horizontal wrap-around LED or OLED tail lights, a clean bumper with integrated dual exhaust tips, and a subtle bootlid lip spoiler. It rides on large multi-spoke alloy wheels (up to 20 inches) and often included a panoramic glass roof.

The R231 Mercedes-Benz SL-Class is a two-door retractable hardtop convertible featuring classic long-hood, short-deck roadster proportions. It features a wide front grille accented by swept-back headlights—which transitioned from angular units to more horizontal LED clusters during its mid-cycle refresh—and a sculpted bonnet with subtle power domes. The rear is defined by wraparound LED tail lights, dual exhaust integrated into the lower bumper, and a lightweight all-aluminum body structure.

The R172 Mercedes-Benz SLK/SLC is a two-door retractable hardtop convertible featuring classic roadster proportions with a long, contoured bonnet and short rear deck. Its front end is highlighted by an upright, wide grille flanked by angular, swept-back headlights and lower LED daytime running lights. The rear showcases horizontal, LED-infused tail lights wrapping into a curved boot lid. Exterior details include side mirrors positioned lower on the doors, multi-spoke alloy wheels, and a folding metal or glass-paneled Vario-roof. Facelifted models (SLC) introduced subtle updates to the bumper contours and headlamp graphics.

The Mercedes-Benz X-Class dual-cab ute features a rugged ladder-frame chassis silhouette with uniquely styled front-end sheet metal, a prominent twin-louvre grille, and sleek angular headlamps. Higher grades showcase body-coloured or chrome bumpers, LED lighting signatures, and alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches. The rear profile retains a traditional drop-side tray flanked by upright, stacked tail-lights.

The MG Cyberster is a two-door electric roadster featuring a classic low-slung sports car profile with a long bonnet and a power-operated fabric soft-top. Its exterior styling is defined by striking motorized scissor doors, a sharp pointed nose with slim LED headlights, and aerodynamic body sculpting. At the rear, it incorporates a distinctive truncated Kammback tail complete with eye-catching LED tail lights featuring a prominent Union Jack motif. It rides on large 20-inch alloy wheels paired with visible Brembo brake calipers.

The MG GS Mk1 is a 5-door medium SUV featuring a boxy, upright silhouette with angular body creases and a relatively flat bonnet. It has a prominent front grille flanked by swept-back halogen or xenon headlights and integrated LED daytime running lights. The rear features wraparound horizontal tail lights, a roof spoiler, and a chunky bumper assembly. Exterior details include available 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, roof rails, and an optional contrasting roof colour on select specifications.

The first-generation MG HS is a 5-door medium SUV featuring flowing body lines, silver roof rails, and an athletic stance. The front end is dominated by a prominent starburst-pattern grille framing a large octagonal MG badge, flanked by sweeping wrap-around headlights with LED daytime running lights. The rear features rounded LED tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and twin exhaust outlets on select trims. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches in diameter, depending on the variant.

The second-generation MG HS medium SUV features an athletic, sleeker body style with an extended wheelbase and increased width compared to its predecessor. It is characterized by a prominent front grille incorporating MG's updated design language, flanked by commanding, slimline LED headlights and daytime running lights. The rear profile is defined by a trendy full-width LED light bar, integrated roof spoiler, and a lower diffuser. Depending on the variant, it rides on 18-inch or distinctive 19-inch alloy wheels, and higher-spec models feature silver roof rails, rear privacy glass, and a panoramic sunroof.

The first-generation MG3 sold in Australia is a compact 5-door light hatchback characterized by an upright, blocky stance and flat roofline. It features a prominent front grille split by a horizontal body-coloured bar bearing the octagonal MG badge, flanked by angular, swept-back headlamps. The rear profile incorporates vertically stacked tail lights running up the outer edges of the tailgate. Depending on the trim level, exterior details include 14-inch to 16-inch alloy or steel wheels, optional contrasting roof colors or body graphics, and a distinct chunky bumper assembly.

The second-generation MG3 is a five-door light hatchback featuring a sharper, more aggressive front fascia inspired by the MG4. It showcases swept-back angular headlights, a low-slung lower grille, and a sculpted bonnet line. The profile displays a rising beltline, flowing body contours, and 16-inch alloy wheels on higher grades, while the rear features wraparound tail lights and an integrated roof spoiler.

The MG MG4 Mk1 is a five-door electric hatchback characterized by a sharp, wedge-like profile with angular body creases and a short, steeply raked bonnet. At the front, it features aggressive, swept-back LED headlights flanking a smooth, flush nose panel with lower geometric air intakes. The rear sports a distinctive full-width LED light bar, an elaborate multi-layered geometric pattern, and a prominent twin-wing roof spoiler on select variants. Depending on the specification, it rides on 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and can feature a contrasting black roof.

The second-generation MG5 is a low-slung, four-door fastback sedan featuring an aggressive sports-oriented stance, sharp lines, and a sloping roofline. The front fascia incorporates angular LED headlights with a distinct 'lightning blade' signature flanking a wide, low-set chrome-accented grille. The rear showcases wraparound LED tail lights, a subtle integrated boot lip spoiler, and dual exhaust-style finishers. It rides on either 16-inch or two-tone 17-inch alloy wheels, and higher grades feature a power-operated glass sunroof.

The MG MG7 Mk1 is a sleek, low-slung five-door fastback sedan featuring a sloping roofline, a liftback tailgate, and frameless doors. The front end is characterized by a wide, aggressive grille and sharp LED headlights with integrated daytime running lamps. At the rear, it displays full-width LED tail-lights, quad exhaust outlets, and an active three-stage deployable rear spoiler. The stance is completed by 19-inch star-shaped alloy wheels wrapped in low-profile tyres.

The MG QS large SUV features a bold, athletic stance spanning nearly five metres in length, complemented by a distinctive diamond-pattern front grille and aggressive, slanted headlights. Its profile showcases a sleek silhouette with flush pop-out door handles, silver roof rails framing a panoramic sunroof, and large 20-inch or 21-inch alloy wheels. The rear is defined by a full-width LED light bar spanning the tailgate, accented by subtle chrome trim.

The MG S5 EV is a compact, rear-wheel-drive electric SUV featuring a smooth, enclosed front fascia complemented by sharp LED headlights and split bumper-mounted main beams. Its side profile showcases short overhangs, sculptured door panels, a wavy waistline, and 18-inch alloy wheels with aero caps. The rear is defined by a full-width continuous LED light bar stretching beneath the back window, while the roofline features a panoramic sunroof and subtle rails.

The MG S6 EV is a mid-size electric SUV featuring a modern four-door fastback-influenced silhouette with a clean, closed-off front fascia. It is characterized by sleek split-LED headlights, smooth body proportions, and flush door handles. The rear incorporates a full-width LED light bar spanning the tailgate, while the exterior rolls on large 20-inch alloy wheels and includes a fixed panoramic glass roof.

The MG U9 dual-cab ute features a large, squared-off body with an imposing, high-sided stance and a prominent chrome grille. It is styled with sharp LED matrix headlights flanked by distinctive L-shaped daytime running lights and sequential indicators at the front. The rear incorporates wrap-around tail lights and a tailgate featuring an integrated electric drop-down step. Depending on the model, it rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches, with roof rails and side steps fitted as standard equipment.

The MG U9 EV features a broad-shouldered, dual-cab ute body style with four doors and a rugged ladder-frame stance. It incorporates a prominent front fascia with sleek LED headlights, a blocked-off aerodynamic grille, and distinctive black or two-tone 20-inch alloy wheels fitted with aerodynamic inserts. The rear features wraparound LED tail lights, a practical cargo tub with side steps, and a hands-free power tailgate. Distinctive visual elements include a power-operated front bonnet accessing a 'frunk' storage compartment and an electronic air suspension system that modifies the vehicle's ride height.

The Mk1 MG ZS is a compact five-door SUV featuring a conventional, upright stance with soft-rounded body lines and a distinctive chrome-outlined hexagonal front grille. It is equipped with swept-back halogen or LED headlamps featuring integrated LED daytime running lights, alongside clean side profile character lines and silver roof rails. The rear showcases wraparound tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and alloy wheel options ranging from 16 to 17 inches depending on the specification.

The second-generation MG ZS is a compact five-door SUV featuring a modern, sleek silhouette with sharply sculpted body lines and striking front air inlets. It is styled with angular LED headlights flanking a prominent grille, accompanied by sleek LED tail-lights at the rear. Depending on the variant, it rides on 16-inch, 17-inch, or larger 18-inch alloy wheels, and features silver roof rails and an available electronic panoramic glass sunroof.

The Mk1 MG ZS EV is a compact five-door SUV featuring conventional crossover proportions with a raked roofline and standard roof rails. Early models feature a traditional starburst grille housing a hidden charging port, while 2022-2024 facelift versions adopt a body-coloured, smooth 'grille-less' front fascia with an offset side-hinged charging port. It is styled with swept-back LED headlights, distinct LED tail light clusters, and rides on 17-inch alloy wheels.

The Mini Aceman is a compact 5-door electric crossover featuring angular LED headlights flanking an octagonal blanked-off grille and a slightly raised, squared-off stance with black body cladding. Its profile highlights a flat roofline, short overhangs, flush door handles, and aerodynamic alloy wheel options. The rear incorporates distinctive vertical tail lights carrying a Union Jack-inspired graphic motif within a stubby tailgate design.

The second-generation Mini Clubman features an elongated, low-slung estate body style with four conventional side doors and a signature pair of vertical split 'barn doors' at the rear. It sports a rounded hexagonal front grille flanked by oval-shaped headlights with LED rings, and horizontal wraparound tail lights that can feature a distinct Union Jack motif. The stance is planted with short overhangs, a long flat roofline, and alloy wheel sizes ranging up to 19 inches.

The third-generation MINI Convertible features a compact two-door body style with a wide stance, short overhangs, and a power-operated fabric soft-top that functions as a sunroof. The front end is characterised by rounded headlights flanking a prominent hexagonal or bar-accented grille, while the rear showcases vertical tail lamps. It rides on various multi-spoke alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches and includes a wraparound chrome beltline.

The fourth-generation Mini Convertible (F67) features a compact, two-door drop-top body style with a fully automatic fabric soft top that retracts in 18 seconds. It showcases clean, minimalist surfaces paired with a prominent octagonal front grille and signature round LED headlights. The rear is defined by distinct triangular LED tail lights incorporating a Union Jack motif, while the profile highlights short overhangs, flush door handles, and a choice of stylish alloy wheel designs.

The second-generation Mini Countryman (F60) features a chunky, five-door SUV body with a rounded yet muscular stance, a relatively flat roofline, and standard roof rails. The front end showcases a prominent hexagonal grille flanked by softer, rounded-rectangular LED headlights, while the rear incorporates upright vertical tail light clusters—often styled with a Union Jack motif in post-2020 facelift models. It rides on distinctive light-alloy wheels with short body overhangs and plastic wheel-arch cladding emphasizing its rugged crossover proportions.

The third-generation Mini Countryman (U25) features a larger, more upright 5-door SUV body with cleaner, minimalist surfaces and flush door handles. It showcases an octagonal front grille flanked by angular LED headlights with customizable daytime running light signatures. The rear is defined by blockish, vertical tail lights, a clean tailgate design, and wide wheel arches emphasizing its rugged stance.

The third-generation Mini Hatch is available as a compact 3-door (F56) or slightly stretched 5-door (F55) hatchback, featuring classic bulldog proportions with short overhangs. It is styled with a prominent hexagonal radiator grille, large circular headlights enclosed by distinct daytime running light rings, and chunky oversized rectangular-oval tail lights. Signature visual details include a contrasting floating roof color option, black wheel-arch cladding, and athletic alloy wheels.

The fourth-generation Mini Hatch features a compact, aggressive stance with short overhangs, available in 3-door (F66) and 5-door (F65) body styles. The front end is characterized by a prominent octagonal grille flanked by signature round LED headlights with customizable light signatures. The rear showcases flush surfacing, a clean minimalist bumper devoid of visible exhaust tips on standard models, and distinctive triangular tail lights connected by a black trim piece. It rides on flush door handles, dynamic alloy wheel designs ranging up to 18 inches, and can be optioned with contrasting roof and mirror cap colors.

The Mitsubishi ASX GA features a high-riding compact crossover body style with five doors and a stubby, rounded stance. Its front end is defined by a prominent trapezoidal grille and angular wrap-around headlights, which evolved through several updates to incorporate Mitsubishi's signature 'Dynamic Shield' chrome-accented bumper styling and sharp LED daytime running lights. The profile displays a rising beltline, rugged black plastic wheel-arch cladding, and available alloy wheel designs ranging up to 18 inches. At the rear, it features wraparound horizontal tail lights, a roof-mounted spoiler, and a liftgate with a clean, upright glass area.

The Renault-based Mitsubishi ASX is a compact five-door SUV featuring toned, curvaceous body proportions with a sloping roofline and a heavily sculpted lower side profile. The front end incorporates sleek LED headlamps flanking a revised upper grille housing the brand's triple-diamond emblem, complemented by a unique front bumper design. At the rear, it features sharp C-shaped LED tail lights and distinct brand lettering spelled across the tailgate. Alloy wheel sizes span from 17 to 18 inches depending on the variant, with higher grades offering a contrasting two-tone roof option.

The Mitsubishi Eclipse Cross features a coupe-inspired compact SUV body style with a steeply raked roofline, muscular proportions, and an extended rear profile. The front end is defined by Mitsubishi's signature 'Dynamic Shield' grille design, flanked by slim LED daytime running lights and lower-mounted main projector headlights. The rear features a sharply sculpted hexagonal tailgate layout paired with single-piece wrap-around three-dimensional LED tail lights. It rides on prominent 18-inch alloy wheels and can be equipped with a dual-pane panoramic sunroof on higher specification grades.

The Mitsubishi Express WA van features a boxy, utilitarian body style available in short and long wheelbases with dual sliding side doors and 50/50 split rear barn doors. Its front end is defined by a rounded bonnet, a distinctive twin-louvre grille bearing the three-diamond badge, and wraparound halogen headlights. It sits on 16-inch steel wheels and incorporates an integrated rear bumper step.

The CJ generation Mitsubishi Lancer sedan features a wedge-shaped profile with a low-slung stance, long bonnet, and short boot. Its front end is defined by a prominent 'Jet Fighter' shark-nose grille flanked by angular, deep-set headlights. The rear incorporates wrap-around tail lights, while upper variants ride on multi-spoke alloy wheels up to 18 inches in diameter alongside a boot-mounted rear spoiler.

The LA-generation Mitsubishi Mirage is a compact five-door hatchback featuring a tall, rounded body profile with short overhangs and a stubby bonnet. The front fascia is styled with a slender upper grille flanked by swept-back angular headlights and a wide lower bumper intake. The rear end is upright with a standard roof spoiler and wraparound tail lights, while the side profile is defined by subtle character lines and small 14-inch or 15-inch wheels.

The third-generation Mitsubishi Outlander features a five-door medium SUV body with soft, rounded proportions that evolved through major facelifts. Early models showcased a conservative chrome grille and wraparound headlights, while later updates introduced the bold 'Dynamic Shield' front fascia featuring prominent angular chrome boomerang accents flanking the grille and sharper LED headlight clusters. The rear styling incorporates wide, horizontally oriented tail lights stretching onto the tailgate, complemented by clean sheet metal and varying alloy wheel designs up to 18 inches across the generations. Roof rails and a subtly tapered roofline complete its family-oriented profile.

The Mitsubishi Outlander GN features a blocky, muscular medium-SUV body style with a dominant 'Dynamic Shield' front grille. It incorporates a split headlight arrangement with ultra-slim LED daytime running lights near the bonnet edge and main clusters lower on the bumper. The side profile is defined by sharp character lines, prominent overhanging guards, and available 20-inch alloy wheels, while the rear showcases slender horizontal LED tail lamps and a hexagonal tailgate motif.

The fourth-generation Mitsubishi Pajero features a boxy, robust four-door station wagon body style with a prominent upright stance and flared wheel arches. It is characterized by a bold front grille flanked by angular, wraparound headlamps and a side-hinged rear tailgate carrying a full-sized spare wheel. Over its production run, exterior updates introduced revised horizontal grille slats, bumper shapes, and modern LED daytime running lights while retaining its utilitarian proportions.

The new-generation Mitsubishi Pajero is a large, rugged five-door SUV featuring a bold, blocky body shape with a pronounced centre bonnet edge and a distinctive C-pillar design. At the front, it sports a T-shaped LED lighting signature alongside a contemporary grille structure. The rear is complemented by full-width LED tail light styling and practical tailgate proportions. Depending on the model grade, it rides on 18-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels and can be optioned with a two-tone panoramic roof.

The Mitsubishi Pajero Sport QE is a 5-door large SUV featuring Mitsubishi's 'Dynamic Shield' front design, characterized by prominent chrome grille bars and slim, swept-back headlights coupled with cascading vertical LED daytime running lamps and fog light clusters. Its high-riding, muscular body profile showcases high-set character lines, flared wheel arches housing multi-spoke alloy wheels, and a distinctive window line that kicks up sharply at the rear pillar. At the rear, it is defined by intensely polarizing, elongated vertical LED tail light lenses that drop dramatically down the flanks of the tailgate.

The MQ-generation Mitsubishi Triton features a distinctive 'J-line' curve separating the cab and the tub on dual-cab models, creating a sweeping profile. It has rounded body proportions with a low drag coefficient, featuring swept-back headlights and a prominent chrome multi-bar grille. Higher-grade variants ride on 16-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and include LED daytime running lights alongside wraparound tail lights that extend onto the tailgate sides.

The Mitsubishi Triton MR features a dual-cab, club-cab, or single-cab ute body style with a squared-off, high-set bonnet and muscular proportions. Its front fascia is dominated by Mitsubishi's 'Dynamic Shield' design, incorporating a prominent chrome-accanted or blacked-out grille flanked by slim upper headlights and stacked lower bumper light clusters. The side profile displays squared wheel arches and angular body creases, while the rear features vertical rectangular tail lights and a tailgate with a subtle integrated spoiler lip. Higher grades add roof rails, sports bars, side steps, and alloy wheel options ranging up to 18 inches in black or metallic finishes.

The sixth-generation Mitsubishi Triton features a muscular, blocky dual-cab or extra-cab ute body style with a longer wheelbase and squarer proportions than its predecessor. The front end is dominated by a high, flat bonnet and a prominent, three-dimensional rectangular grille flanked by a tiered lighting arrangement, featuring slim upper L-shaped LED daytime running lights above separate main headlamp clusters. The side profile showcases squared-off wheel arches with pronounced fender flares, while the rear is defined by distinct T-shaped LED tail lamps and a practical bumper with integrated side-step corners. It rides on 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels depending on the model grade.

The Bolwell Nagari Mk X is a low-slung, mid-engine two-door coupé featuring a lightweight carbon-composite body with sweeping aerodynamic lines, a low roofline, and large side air intakes. It incorporates a wide front stance, angular headlamp assemblies, and distinctive rear tail lights sourced from the DC5-generation Honda Integra. The exterior sits on large multi-spoke alloy wheels and showcases a wraparound windscreen leading into a compact cabin profile.

The Bolwell Nagari 500 is a lightweight, mid-engined 2-door coupé featuring a low-slung composite body built around a carbon-fibre and Kevlar tub. Its exterior styling includes a steeply raked windscreen, side glass windows positioned just behind the doors, and wide rear haunches designed to accommodate large 19-inch alloy wheels. The rear layout incorporates distinctive tail lights sourced from the Honda Integra (DC5), while the overall stance presents a classic, aerodynamic supercar silhouette with minimal overhangs.

The Nissan 370Z features a low-slung, aggressive fastback coupe or two-door convertible body style defined by a long hood, short rear deck, and a distinctive cantilevered roofline. It is characterized by striking boomerang-shaped bi-xenon headlights and matching LED tail lights that sweep sharply into the fenders. The front end incorporates a wide, angular grille opening flanked by vertical LED daytime running lights. In profile, it sits on wide track stances with flared guards, frequently equipped with 19-inch multi-spoke RAYS forged alloy wheels.

The L33 Nissan Altima is a four-door mid-size sedan featuring flowing, coupe-like roofline proportions and prominent character lines along its flanks. It is characterized by a V-motion-inspired chrome grille flanked by swept-back angular headlights, and wide wraparound tail lights extending onto the boot lid. Exterior details across the Australian lineup include 16-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, chrome window surrounds, and an integrated rear spoiler lip on select grades.

The R35 Nissan GT-R is a two-door 2+2 sports coupe featuring a muscular, low-slung stance with sharp aerodynamic lines, a prominent mesh front grille flanked by angular HID/LED headlights, and large cooling intakes. Its rear end is defined by iconic quad circular tail lights, a distinct rear wing spoiler, and a quad-exhaust system. It rides on multi-spoke alloy wheels, fills out broad flared fenders, and features a sloping roofline with flush door handles.

The first-generation Nissan Juke features a quirky, high-riding compact SUV body with distinctive muscular wheel arches and a coupe-like sloping roofline. Its polarizing front end showcases a multi-tier lighting layout with prominent, bug-eye circular headlights paired with upper boomerang-shaped daytime running lamps flanking a V-motion grille. The rear includes boomerang tail lights that wrap into pronounced haunches, while the rear door handles are cleverly concealed within the C-pillar frame.

The F16 Nissan Juke features a coupe-like compact SUV body style with hidden rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars, athletic sculpted flanks, and a prominent 'floating roof' design. The front end is defined by Nissan's V-motion grille flanked by slim upper daytime running lights and distinctive round main headlight units incorporating Y-shaped LED signatures. At the rear, sharp angular tail lights sit on broad shoulder lines above a heavily raked rear window. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches, filling out pronounced, muscular wheel arches.

The first-generation Nissan Leaf is a five-door hatchback featuring a distinctive, aerodynamic silhouette with a low-slung, abbreviated front end. It is characterized by prominent, swept-back bug-eye headlamp housings designed to channel airflow away from the side mirrors. At the rear, it sports vertically stacked, narrow LED tail lights flanking the tailgate, complemented by a subtle roof spoiler and multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Nissan Leaf (ZE1) features a dynamic five-door hatchback body style characterized by sharp character lines and a floating roof design. The front end incorporates Nissan's signature V-motion grille panel paired with sleek, angular LED headlamps and a charging port integrated into the nose. At the rear, it sports boomerang-shaped tail lights alongside a prominent roof spoiler and a lower diffuser. The stance is defined by balanced compact proportions complemented by multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Nissan Navara D23 is offered in single-cab, king-cab, and dual-cab ute body styles with muscular proportions and high-riding ground clearance. The front fascia is dominated by a prominent interlocking frame grille framed by squared C-shape quad LED projector headlights and a heavily sculpted, raised bonnet. Dual-cab versions feature deep cargo tubs with high sides, a stamped tailgate, and wrap-around LED tail lights, riding on 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels alongside robust side steps.
