The Nissan Pathfinder R52 is a large, five-door unibody crossover SUV featuring rounded, aerodynamic proportions that departed from the boxy frames of its predecessors. Up front, it showcases a prominent V-motion chrome grille flanked by angular, swept-back wraparound headlights, which received a sharper-edged refresh with boomerang-style LED daytime running lights in later model years. The profile exhibits a flowing roofline, pronounced wheel arches, and subtle chrome window surrounds, while the rear features wraparound horizontal tail lights and a sculpted tailgate. It sits on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches depending on the specification tier.

The Nissan Pathfinder R53 features a boxy, muscular SUV body style with a squared-off front end, shorter overhangs, and flared wheel arches. It is styled with a prominent three-slat V-motion grille flanked by slim C-shaped LED headlights. The rear incorporates slimline horizontal LED tail lights framing a prominent tailgate with model lettering. Exterior details include a 'floating' roofline with available two-tone paint options, a shark-fin antenna, and alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches.

The Nissan Patrol Y62 is a massive, full-size five-door SUV characterized by commanding, curvaceous proportions and prominent chrome exterior accents. It features a bold front fascia dominated by a large V-motion grille flanked by wraparound LED headlights, complemented by a broad, vertically opening tailgate at the rear. Over its production run, it rolled on chunky 18-inch alloy wheels, integrated side steps, and featured angular front bumper updates along with large horseshoe-shaped LED tail-light clusters.

The Nissan Patrol Y63 is a large, full-size luxury SUV featuring a boxy, commanding stance with muscular body lines and prominent wheel arches. Its front fascia is defined by a bold V-Motion grille flanked by signature C-shape LED headlights. At the rear, it incorporates slim, modern LED tail lights connected across a wide tailgate. The exterior can be configured with dual-tone paint options, a panoramic sunroof, and alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 22 inches (with black 20-inch wheels and robust fender flares on the off-road-focused Pro-4X variant).

The B17-generation Nissan Pulsar is available as a traditional 4-door sedan and a sweeping 5-door hatchback. It features smooth, conservative body proportions accented by a chrome-accented trapezoidal front grille, wraparound headlights, and distinct tail light clusters. Standard models ride on 16-inch alloy wheels, while sporty SSS variants upgrade to 17-inch sports alloys alongside more aggressive bumper treatments.

The Nissan Qashqai J11 is a compact five-door SUV featuring an athletic stance with flowing body lines and a distinctive V-motion front grille. Pre-facelift models feature swept-back headlamps and wrap-around tail lights, while post-2017 facelift variants introduce sharper LED lighting signatures and a more prominent front bumper design. It sits on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches, complemented by a subtle rear roof spoiler, body-coloured cladding, and an optional panoramic glass roof.

The Nissan Qashqai J12 is a five-door compact SUV featuring sharp, athletic proportions and a muscular stance. The front end is defined by a wide, intricate 'samurai armor' grille flanked by ultra-slim, sharp LED headlights. At the rear, it features tapered LED tail lights, a sculpted tailgate with stamped lettering, and an optional floating contrasting roof paired with low-profile roof rails. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches in diameter, depending on the variant.

The T32 Nissan X-Trail features a five-door mid-size SUV body with flowing, aerodynamic proportions that replaced the boxy styling of earlier generations. It is characterised by a prominent V-motion front grille, swept-back wraparound headlights with integrated LED daytime running lights, and boomerang-shaped tail lights. Exterior details include roof rails, a subtle rear spoiler, and alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches depending on the specification grade.

The Nissan X-Trail T33 is a five-door mid-size SUV featuring a boxy, muscular profile with squared-off wheel arches and a floating roofline. Up front, it showcases a prominent V-motion grille flanked by split-level LED headlamps with slim upper signature DRLs. The rear incorporates angular LED tail lights, a sculpted tailgate, and a robust lower bumper. Higher trims ride on alloy wheels up to 20 inches in diameter and offer distinctive two-tone body paint configurations.

The Nissan Z coupe features a classic fastback silhouette with a long bonnet and short rear deck, heavily influenced by heritage Z-cars. It showcases a prominent rectangular grille and semi-circle LED headlights inspired by the 240Z, paired with rectangular 300ZX-style horizontal tail lights. The stance is rounded out by 19-inch forged alloy wheels and a low-slung roofline that can be accented with a contrasting black roof.

The first-generation Omoda 5 is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a coupe-like sloping roofline with a distinct rear ducktail spoiler. Its front fascia is defined by a frameless geometric diamond-pattern grille flanked by sharp T-shaped LED daytime running lights, with main headlights integrated into the bumper sides. The profile is characterized by a rising waistline, tapering side glass, and pronounced wheel arches riding on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels. At the rear, it features aggressive wraparound LED tail lights connected by a dark trim element, complemented by sequential indicators.

The first-generation Omoda 9 is a large, five-seat plug-in hybrid SUV featuring a modern coupe-inspired crossover silhouette with a low-slung, sloping roofline. The front end is defined by a bold cascading diamond-shaped grille flanked by slim projector LED headlights connected by a full-width light bar, complemented by vertical daytime running lights. Its profile is styled with flush, retractable door handles, multi-spoke 20-inch alloy wheels, and a subtle metallic spear accent piercing the front doors and fenders. The rear showcases a full-width horizontal LED light bar, a powered tailgate, and a broad contoured stance.

The Peugeot 2008 P24 generation is a compact 5-door SUV featuring a muscular, un-boxy stance with a distinctive stepped roofline profile. It showcases a wide, prominent front grille integrated with the brand's lion emblem, flanked by sleek, angular headlights and dramatic three-claw vertical LED daytime running lights on the bumper. The rear displays horizontal tail lights housing triple-claw LED light signatures, complemented by stylish alloy wheels and black body-cladding elements highlighting its crossover silhouette.

The Peugeot 2008 compact SUV features a muscular body style with sharp creases, sculpted side panels, and a distinctive stance. The front end is dominated by a wide grille with body-colored slats, framed by full LED headlights and signature triple-claw daytime running light strips. At the rear, horizontal LED tail lights create a three-dimensional claw effect, complemented by black door mirror caps and diamond-cut alloy wheels.

The first-generation Peugeot 208 hatchback features a compact, dynamic body style available in both 3-door and 5-door configurations with short overhangs. Its front fascia is highlighted by a floating, satin-chrome trimmed grille flanked by expressive headlights with integrated LED daytime running light eyebrows. The rear showcases distinctive boomerang-shaped LED tail lights and a sculpted tailgate. The profile is characterized by organic, flowing lines, a sweeping roofline, and alloy wheel options ranging from 15 to 17 inches depending on the variant.

The Peugeot 3008 P84 features a robust five-door medium SUV body with an athletic stance, high beltline, and distinctive flowing chrome roof-arch trim. The front end showcases an assertive frameless or chequered grille flanked by sharp, feline-inspired LED headlights with integrated daytime running light 'fangs'. At the rear, glossy black trim connects dramatic 3D claw-effect LED tail lights. Exterior highlights include two-tone diamond-cut alloy wheels and available contrasting black diamond roof finishes.

The Peugeot 3008 (P64 generation) features a striking fastback SUV silhouette with a raked roofline and an aerodynamic floating rear spoiler. Its front end is defined by a frameless grille that blends into the bodywork, flanked by slim LED headlights incorporating Peugeot's signature three-claw daytime running light motif. The rear showcases a sloping tailgate accentuated by dynamic 3D claw-effect LED tail lights. The stance is planted on large diamond-cut alloy wheels, complemented by clean, creased body side surfacing.

The T9 Peugeot 308 hatchback features a clean, understated five-door European silhouette with a low-slung stance and balanced proportions. It is styled with a rectangular, chrome-accented front grille housing the lion badge, flanked by sleek wrap-around headlights (with LED signatures on higher grades). The rear showcases distinctive three-claw LED tail lights integrated into a sculpted tailgate, complemented by clean alloy wheel designs and a smooth roofline.

The third-generation Peugeot 308 hatchback features a low-slung, athletic five-door body with a sharp silhouette and a lengthened wheelbase. The front end is dominated by a wide, patterned grille housing the modern flat-design shield logo, flanked by slim LED headlights and distinctive vertical "fang" daytime running lights. The rear showcases a sloping roofline ending in a subtle spoiler, angular three-dimensional "lion claw" tail lights connected by a black gloss accent strip, and sculpted muscular rear haunches.

The Peugeot 308 Touring (T9) is a five-door station wagon featuring a clean, elongated profile with an extended rear overhang and a roofline that flows into a subtle rear spoiler. The front end showcases a prominent chrome-surrounded grille with horizontal slats and a central lion badge, flanked by sleek, angular headlights (featuring LED signatures on higher grades) and a sculpted bumper. At the rear, it is fitted with wraparound LED tail lights incorporating a distinctive three-claw light motif. The exterior is accented by chrome window surrounds, roof rails, and alloy wheel options ranging up to 18 inches in diameter.

The first-generation Peugeot 4008 is a 5-door compact SUV featuring a distinctively sculpted front fascia with a floating grille, sharp wraparound headlamps, and vertical LED daytime running lights integrated into the bumper sides. While sharing its roofline and doors with its platform twin, it displays unique sheet metal, a rising beltline, and a boomerang-like rear tail-light graphic. It rides on either 16-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and features a sloping rear hatch profile with an integrated roof spoiler.

The Peugeot 408 features a sharp, fastback crossover body style combining a low-slung, coupe-like roofline with a raised SUV stance and five doors. The front end is dominated by a body-coloured matrix grille flanked by slim LED headlights and distinctive vertical "fang" LED daytime running lights. The rear profile incorporates unique "cat ear" aerodynamic roof spoilers, an angular bumper cutout, and 3D claw-effect LED tail lights. It rides on large alloy wheels up to 20 inches in diameter and features sharp geometric body surfacing throughout.

The Peugeot 5008 (P87 generation) features a large 5-door SUV body style with an extended, boxier profile and an upright tailgate to accommodate its seven-seat layout. Up front, it sports an aggressive frameless-style radiator grille flanked by sharp LED headlights, often incorporating distinctive fang-like daytime running lights. The rear is characterised by distinctive three-claw LED tail lights connected by a gloss-black trim strip. Exterior details include a contrasting 'Black Diamond' floating roof, chunky wheel arch cladding, silver roof rails, and large diamond-cut alloy wheels.

The Peugeot 5008 (P74) is a large, seven-seater SUV featuring an elongated, athletic silhouette with a sharply raked, fastback-style sloping rear window. Its bold front end showcases a frameless grille that seamlessly merges into the body color, flanked by ultra-slim Pixel LED headlights and vertical triple-claw daytime running light 'fangs'. The rear incorporates a distinct gloss-black applique housing a slim, horizontal LED tail light signature with three slanted claw elements. It rides on large aerodynamic alloy wheels and can be optioned with a contrasting 'Black Diamond' floating roof.

The first-generation Peugeot 508 sedan features a traditional four-door three-box profile with clean, flowing proportions and a balanced stance. Early models feature a curved chrome grille and swept-back headlights, which were updated during the 2015 facelift to a more upright, floating grille housing the Peugeot lion badge flanked by sharper, structured headlamps. The rear showcases wraparound tail lights with distinct triple-claw red lighting graphics, complemented by a clean bootlid line. It rides on alloy wheels ranging in design by trim level and features a smooth roofline flowing gracefully into the integrated rear deck.

The Peugeot 508 R8 fastback sedan features a low-slung, coupe-like stance with a heavily raked roofline and frameless doors. Its aggressive front fascia showcases a checkered digital grille flanked by slim LED headlights and distinctive vertical "lion's fang" daytime running lights. The rear is dominated by a gloss-black horizontal trim panel housing 3D "lion claw" LED tail lights. It rides on large multi-spoke alloy wheels and features a fastback liftgate hatch profile.

The Peugeot 508 Sportswagon (R8) features a low-slung, athletic station wagon profile with frameless door glass and an elongated silhouette. The front end is dominated by a checkered chrome grille flanked by slim LED headlights and distinctive vertical "fang" LED daytime running lights. The rear showcases a glossy black horizontal applique housing 3D "lion claw" LED tail lights. It rides on large multi-spoke alloy wheels (typically 18-inch or 19-inch) and features a dynamic, sloping roofline accented by integrated roof rails.

The first-generation Peugeot 508 Touring (W23) features a traditional, elongated station wagon body style with a balanced silhouette and a gently sloping roofline ending in an integrated tailgate spoiler. The front end is dominated by a "floating" chrome-accented grille and feline-styled headlights with integrated LED daytime running lights. Along the sides, refined body lines are complemented by satin chrome window surrounds, while the rear features distinctive horizontal tail lights housing three vertical red LED light tubes.

The first-generation Polestar 2 features an elevated fastback sedan body style with rugged lower body cladding and high-riding proportions. Early models feature a textured, dark grid-patterned grille, while updated versions incorporate a smooth, body-colored "SmartZone" panel housing driver-assistance sensors. Flanking the front are sharp LED headlights with signature Thor's Hammer daytime running lights. The rear is dominated by a distinctive full-width LED light-blade connecting angular tail lamps, complemented by frameless side mirrors and clean roof lines.

The first-generation Polestar 3 is a large luxury electric SUV featuring an aerodynamic, low-slung stance with a long roofline and a raked rear window. The front end incorporates a blanked-off 'SmartZone' panel flanked by distinctive dual-blade LED headlights and a unique aero wing integrated into the bonnet. The rear showcases a full-width light bar signature connecting wrap-around tail lamps. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 22 inches and features flush-fitting retractable door handles alongside a prominent panoramic glass roof.

The Polestar 4 features a five-door coupe-SUV body style with a distinctively lowered nose and a sharply sloping roofline that entirely eliminates the traditional rear window. Its minimalist exterior is characterized by split-blade LED daytime running lights, a closed front fascia featuring an illuminated central emblem, and flush-fitting retractable door handles alongside frameless windows and mirrors. The rear is defined by a full-width LED light bar sitting beneath a clean, windowless tailgate panel, while the stance is completed by aero-optimized alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 22 inches under a standard full-length glass roof.

The Porsche 718 Boxster (982) is a two-door mid-engine roadster featuring a low-slung stance, pronounced rear wheel arches, and an electrically retractable fabric soft-top. The front fascia incorporates sharp, horizontal Bi-Xenon headlights with integrated four-point LED daytime running lights above wide cooling air intakes. The rear is characterised by darkened three-dimensional LED tail lights connected across the boot lid by a high-gloss black accent strip bearing the Porsche lettering. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches, with side air intakes accentuating its dynamic mid-engine proportions.

The 982-generation Porsche 718 Cayman is a two-door sports coupe featuring a low-slung, balanced mid-engine silhouette with sharp side air intakes and a sloping fastback roofline. The front fascia incorporates wide air intakes and distinct projector-style headlights with integrated four-point daytime running lights. At the rear, it is characterized by slim, dark-tinted LED tail lights connected by a high-gloss black trim strip bearing the Porsche lettering, complemented by an active deploying rear spoiler and central exhaust outlets.

The seventh-generation Porsche 911 features a low-slung, wider stance with an elongated wheelbase, featuring swept-back oval headlights and a swept windshield. The coupe has a sharply raked fastback roofline, the convertible uses a fully automated fabric soft top maintaining the classic silhouette, and the Targa showcases a prominent metallic roll-over bar with a wraparound glass rear window. At the rear, it is characterized by slim, horizontal LED tail lights, active deployable rear spoilers, and wide muscular rear guards.

The eighth-generation Porsche 911 (992) features a muscular wide-body stance with pronounced front wheel housings and a heavily sculpted bonnet incorporating a characteristic recess. It is defined by round LED headlights, flush door handles, and a continuous, straight light bar spanning across the tail. The Coupe, Cabriolet, and Targa variants share these proportions, with the Targa uniquely distinguished by its wide metallic roll hoop and sweeping wraparound rear glass window.

The second-generation Porsche Cayenne features a more curvaceous, aerodynamic five-door SUV body style with sloping rooflines and heavily contoured flanks compared to its predecessor. The front fascia is dominated by a trapezoidal grille flanked by swept-back, teardrop-shaped headlights and LED daytime running lights embedded in the lower bumper air intakes. At the rear, it is equipped with wraparound, horizontal LED tail lights, a subtle roof spoiler, and dual or quad exhaust outlets depending on the powertrain. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 21 inches, filling out pronounced flared wheel arches.

The third-generation Porsche Cayenne (9YA) is offered as a traditional 5-door SUV and a sleeker, sloped-roof Coupe. It features athletic proportions with prominent wheel arches, a wide front grille punctuated by large air intakes, and distinctive multi-point LED headlights. The rear is characterised by a slim, full-width three-dimensional LED light bar running across the tailgate. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 22 inches, with the Coupe variant incorporating a standard panoramic glass roof or optional carbon roof.

The first-generation Porsche Macan (95B) is a compact five-door luxury SUV featuring a sloping, coupe-like roofline, athletic proportions, and frameless doors. Its side profile is defined by characteristic indented lower door blades. The front fascia incorporates a low, wide grille with distinct intake slats flanked by multi-point LED daytime running light clusters, while later revisions introduced a full-width continuous LED tail-light strip across the tailgate. It rides on staggered alloy wheels (ranging from 19 to 21 inches) and features a subtle roof spoiler above a raked rear glass.

The Porsche Macan Electric features a dynamic, coupé-like SUV body with a low-slung front bonnet, strongly contoured front fenders, and frameless doors incorporating characteristic lower sideblades. The front fascia is defined by split lighting, with flat upper four-point LED daytime running lights integrated into the wings and the main headlamp clusters positioned slightly lower in the bumper. At the rear, it sports a steeply raked glass window, a continuous 3D LED light strip with glass-effect Porsche lettering, and an adaptive rear spoiler above a clean bumper diffuser. It rides on short overhangs with large alloy wheels up to 22 inches in diameter filling the pronounced wheel arches.

The second-generation Porsche Panamera (971) features a sleek, low-slung five-door liftback sedan or shooting-brake Sport Turismo body style with a balanced, elongated silhouette. It is characterized by a sharply raked roofline, distinctively tapered side glass, and a wide stance accented by sharp quad-LED headlights and an aggressive front fascia. The rear is dominated by a continuous, three-dimensional LED light strip spanning across the tailgate, complemented by an active deployable rear spoiler and large alloy wheels ranging up to 21 inches.

The third-generation Porsche Panamera liftback sedan features a low-slung, athletic profile with a lower-contoured bonnet and more pronounced front wings. Its front fascia is defined by sharper, steeply raked matrix LED headlights flanking a wider lower intake, supplemented by an additional cooling air slot directly above the front license plate recess. The sleek, coupe-like window line flows seamlessly into a seamless full-width three-dimensional rear light strip containing delicate dual-arc light guides and a frameless rear window. It rides on a range of 19- to 21-inch wheel designs, with select variants featuring centre-lock options.

The Porsche Taycan (Type 9J1) is offered as a low-slung four-door sedan, a raised-ride-height Cross Turismo wagon with rugged cladding, and a sleek Sport Turismo wagon. It features a sculpted hood dropping between muscular front fenders, distinct four-point LED headlights, and a smooth front fascia lacking a traditional grille. The side profile displays a flowing roofline and flush door handles, while the rear showcases a full-width LED light bar spanning beneath an active spoiler. Lower variants ride on aero-optimized alloy wheels, with higher trims sporting large performance wheels and contrasting brake calipers.

The first-generation Proton Exora is a five-door, seven-seat people-mover featuring a tall, wedge-like MPV profile with a raked windshield and an ascending bonnet line. It features swept-back, angular headlights flanking a slim grille, a lower intake-heavy front bumper, and vertical-oriented high-mounted tail lights framing the large tailgate. The exterior is accented by subtle side body styling, standard alloy wheels, and an integrated rear roof spoiler on higher specifications.

The first-generation Proton Prevé is a four-door compact sedan featuring a traditional three-box silhouette with an ascending waistline and a high boot lid. The front fascia incorporates projector headlights and integrated lower LED daytime running lights that flank a broad 'winged' grille accented by a horizontal chrome slat and central badge. The side profile displays creased character lines along the body-colored door handles and rides on 10-spoke 16-inch alloy wheels. At the rear, it is fitted with high-mounted, angular tail lights and a wrapped-around bumper housing lower fog lamps.

The Proton Suprima S is a 5-door hatchback featuring a sleek, wedge-like profile with pronounced bodyside creases and a distinctive rear spoiler. The front fascia is highlighted by a honeycomb-patterned 'Wings' grille flanked by wraparound headlamps and LED daytime running lights on higher grades. At the rear, it is distinguished by wrap-around tail lights incorporating LED guide elements and a central rear fog lamp integrated into the lower bumper diffuser. It rides on either 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels housed beneath curved wheelarches.

The Ram 1500 DS features a bulky, muscular body style with an imposing front fascia dominated by a large chrome or black crosshair grille flanked by wraparound rectangular headlamps. It rides on large 20-inch alloy wheels beneath squared-off wheel arches, featuring a high ground clearance and long dual-cab proportions paired with either a short or long cargo tub. The rear end is fitted with simple vertical tail lights framing a flat tailgate bearing prominent embossed lettering, while details like chunky side mirrors and available black body cladding accentuate its rugged full-size stance.

The Ram 1500 DT features a muscular dual-cab ute body with sculpted, aerodynamic body lines and a commanding stance. It is dominated by a large, prominent front grille bearing bold RAM lettering, flanked by sleek LED headlights. The rear showcases vertical tail light clusters framing a wide tailgate, complemented by large alloy wheels (up to 22 inches) and available features like a dual-pane panoramic sunroof and RamBox cargo bins.

The Ram 2500 dual-cab ute features a commanding, heavyweight stance with a massive, prominent front grille flanked by sleek bi-LED projector headlights. Its muscular body includes a sculpted 'power bulge' performance hood and high-profile side proportions fitted with large alloy wheels and extended tow mirrors. The rear is defined by vertical LED tail lights framing a damped, central-locking tailgate that opens to a utility tub.

The fifth-generation Ram 3500 dual-cab ute features a commanding, muscular stance with a prominent, towering front grille flanked by sleek LED headlights and a vented sports bonnet. Its massive proportions include a large crew-cab configuration paired with a 6-foot-4-inch cargo tub, accented by bold black exterior badging, side steps, and 18-inch alloy wheels. The rear showcases vertical LED tail lights, a power-releasing tailgate, and a high-mounted stop lamp with an integrated cargo-view camera.

The first-generation Renault Arkana features a distinctive five-door coupe-SUV body style characterised by a steeply sloping roofline that tapers smoothly into an integrated boot lid spoiler. At the front, it showcases a wide grille accented by Renault's signature diamond badge, flanked by C-shaped LED headlights. The rear is defined by a full-width light bar connecting sleek LED tail lights. It rides on large alloy wheels (ranging up to 18 or 19 inches depending on the variant), balancing a raised SUV ride height with sweeping fastback proportions.

The first-generation Renault Captur is a compact light SUV featuring a rounded, high-riding stance with short overhangs and five doors. It features a prominent corporate front grille bearing a large central Renault diamond emblem, flanked by swept-back headlights and lower bumper-mounted LED daytime running lights. The exterior is characterized by a flowing, curvaceous profile that commonly highlights a signature two-tone contrasting color scheme for the roof, pillars, and door mirrors. At the rear, it has wraparound tail lights, a subtle tailgate spoiler, and is typically fitted with 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels.

The second-generation Renault Captur is a compact light SUV featuring a muscular stance with sculpted body sides, prominent wheel arches, and protective front and rear skid plates. The front fascia showcases an imposing grille flanked by LED headlights and distinctive C-shaped daytime running lights, while the rear features slim, C-shaped 3D-effect tail lights. It rides on 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels and commonly features a popular two-tone contrasting floating roof treatment. Lower body cladding and a high waistline complete its athletic urban crossover proportions.

The Renault Clio IV is a five-door hatchback featuring a coupe-like silhouette with hidden rear door handles integrated near the rear quarter windows. It has a bold front fascia dominated by a large, upright Renault diamond emblem set against a gloss-black grille, flanked by sleek headlights accented with chrome and standard LED daytime running lights. The body displays fluid, curvaceous shoulder lines and a lower stance, complemented by customisable wheel options ranging from steel wheels with trims to multi-spoke alloy wheels. The rear features wraparound tail lights and a subtle roof spoiler.

The first-generation facelift Renault Kadjar is a five-door medium SUV featuring smooth, flowing crossover proportions with wraparound body-colored bumpers and generous chrome accents. Up front, it sports a wider chrome-finish grille flanked by C-shaped LED daytime running lights and revised headlights, alongside rectangular LED fog lights integrated into the lower bumper. The rear features sleek LED tail lights, a sculpted tailgate, and a shark-fin antenna on higher grades. It rides on alloy wheel designs ranging up to 19 inches and includes robust front and rear skid plates.

The Renault Kangoo II panel van features a boxy, high-roof utility body style with sliding side doors and asymmetrical double-hinged rear barn doors. The front end showcases a prominent corporate grille housing the central Renault diamond emblem, flanked by wraparound, teardrop-shaped headlights. It rides on small steel wheels and features an upright, slab-sided profile designed to maximize cargo space.

The third-generation Renault Kangoo panel van features a modern, blocky commercial silhouette with distinctively sculpted body sides and a heavily upright front fascia. It incorporates a prominent chrome-accented grille housing the large central Renault diamond badge, flanked by contemporary swept-back headlights with C-shaped LED daytime running light signatures. The rear end showcases flat, high-mounted vertical tail lights alongside practical asymmetric side-hinged barn doors and dual sliding side access doors. It rides on 16-inch wheels and features a clean roofline that integrates smoothly with its utilitarian proportions.

The Renault Koleos II is a medium five-door SUV characterized by muscular proportions, a high beltline, and sculpted body sides featuring prominent chrome accent strips. Its front end is dominated by a bold grille featuring heavy chrome detailing and distinctive C-shaped LED daytime running lights that flank sleek LED headlamps. The rear features long, sweeping horizontal tail lights with a 3D light signature that stretch toward the central Renault badge. It rides on large multi-spoke or two-tone alloy wheels (ranging from 17 to 19 inches) and can be equipped with a full-length panoramic glass roof.

The third-generation Renault Master panel van features a high-roof, boxy large-van body style with a prominent, blunt nose and wraparound front bumper. It incorporates a large multibar front grille featuring the diamond corporate badge, flanked by tall, swept-back headlamps and lower C-shaped daytime running lights added during subsequent updates. The rear utilizes vertical, rectangular tail light clusters alongside asymmetrical 50/50 split barn doors and a wide passenger-side sliding entry.

The fourth-generation Renault Master large panel van features an aerodynamic "aerovan" body style with a shortened bonnet and a prominent, aggressive front grille featuring large C-shaped LED headlights. It rides on 16-inch steel wheels and is configured with a side sliding door and 270-degree opening rear barn doors. The streamlined silhouette includes sculpted door mirrors and is available in medium- and long-wheelbase lengths, with standard and high-roof options.

The fourth-generation Renault Megane hatchback features a low-slung, dynamic stance with a prominent central diamond badge set into a bold grille and distinctive C-shape LED daytime running lights. Its clean profile is defined by accentuated shoulder lines and subtly flared wheel arches. At the rear, ultra-long, horizontal LED tail lights stretch inward across the tailgate, nearly meeting to emphasize the car's width. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches in diameter, with sporting variants showcasing aggressive lower body kits and dual exhaust outlets.

The first-generation Renault Megane E-Tech features a compact, high-riding crossover body style with a sporty coupe-like silhouette, short overhangs, and a rising beltline. It is characterized by a sleek, blanked-off upper fascia merging into slim full-LED adaptive headlights, flush pop-out door handles, and large 20-inch alloy wheels. The rear sports a sloping roofline capped by an available contrasting roof, muscular shoulder lines, and full-width connected tail lights featuring a distinctive 3D moiré effect.

The Renault Scenic E-Tech is a compact electric crossover SUV featuring a streamlined, cab-forward silhouette with short overhangs and flush door handles. It sports a sharply angled front fascia with slim LED headlights and distinctively shaped vertical daytime running light signatures flanking a textured blanked-off grille. The rear showcases sleek, horizontally stretched LED tail lights connected across a sculpted tailgate, complemented by large 19-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels.

The first-generation Renault Symbioz is a compact crossover featuring a sharp European stance with a sculpted bonnet and angular LED headlights flanking a slim, textured grille. Its profile showcases clean character lines, black body-cladding, and 18- or 19-inch alloy wheels, topped by an available panoramic glass roof. The rear incorporates geometric LED tail lights stretching inward across a sharply raked tailgate.

The Renault Trafic III medium panel van features a boxy, functional body shape with a short, steeply raked bonnet blending into the windscreen angle. It has a prominent, wide rectangular grille dominated by a large central Renault diamond emblem, flanked by wraparound rectangular headlights. The side profile displays a distinct horizontal character line and a sliding passenger-side door, while the rear consists of vertical split barn doors with stacked vertical tail lights.

The facelifted Renault Trafic medium panel van features a boxy, functional utility body style with a prominent, squared-off front fascia incorporating a redesigned grille and bonnet. It is flanked by slim LED headlights featuring distinct C-shaped daytime running light signatures. The side profile highlights large electric-folding mirrors and sliding side doors, sitting on 16-inch steel wheels or 17-inch alloys depending on the grade. At the rear, it is fitted with vertical tail light clusters and a practical tailgate or barn-door configuration.

The Rolls-Royce Cullinan is a large, boxy luxury SUV featuring a commanding vertical Pantheon grille and rectangular headlights, with rear-hinged coach doors providing access to the cabin. Its tall, flat-roofed profile rests on large multi-spoke wheels, complemented by rectangular tail lights and a split-tailgate configuration. Updates include sharper front bumper intakes, optional illuminated grille elements, and distinctive vertical daytime running light signatures.

The Rolls-Royce Dawn is a two-door luxury convertible featuring rear-hinged suicide doors and an imposing silhouette defined by a long hood, short front overhang, and high shoulder line. Its front fascia is anchored by a prominent, upright stainless steel Parthenon grille flanked by narrow, rectangular-styled LED headlights. At the rear, it sports a tapered decklid covered by an open-pore wood-trimmed panel when the multi-layer fabric soft top is retracted, complemented by wrapped triangular tail lights and large multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Rolls-Royce Ghost Series II is a luxury four-door sedan featuring rear-hinged coach doors and a commanding upright stance. It is distinguished by re-sculpted LED headlights encircled by crisp, continuous daytime running light halos flanking a prominent Pantheon grille. The long-hood proportions incorporate a tapered 'wake channel' on the bonnet originating from the Spirit of Ecstasy, complemented by a forward-leaning side 'waft line' and large alloy wheels.

The second-generation Rolls-Royce Ghost is a large luxury sedan featuring a monolithic body profile with four traditional doors, including rear-hinged coach doors. It is characterized by a prominent, illuminated Pantheon grille flanked by slender LED headlights and daytime running lights, topped by the iconic Spirit of Ecstasy. The rear features upright, vertical LED tail-light signatures, while large 22-inch wheel options and clean, minimalist sheet metal emphasize its commanding proportions.

The Rolls-Royce Phantom VII sedan features a commanding four-door design with rear-hinged coach doors and monumental vertical proportions defined by a long hood and a high-set roofline. The front end is dominated by a prominent Pantheon grille topped by the Spirit of Ecstasy, flanked by rectangular headlights. Its side profile showcases large-diameter alloy wheels, a rising lower sill accent line, and thick C-pillars, while the rear features a flat decklid with understated vertical tail lights.

The Rolls-Royce Phantom VIII is a grand luxury sedan featuring a majestic upright Pantheon grille integrated smoothly into the front bodywork, flanked by rectangular laser headlights with frosted internal details. It utilizes a stately four-door layout with rear-hinged coach doors, a long bonnet, a set-back passenger compartment, and a flowing fastback-style roofline. The rear profile is accented by sleek, tapered tail lights and large polished alloy wheels, maintaining an imposing, monumental presence.

The Rolls-Royce Phantom Coupé features a grand two-door pillarless hardtop body style with rear-hinged coach doors and a heavily raked windshield. It has a commanding vertical stainless steel grille topped by the Spirit of Ecstasy, flanked by rectangular headlights. The rear profile showcases a sloping fastback roofline flowing into a distinct boot deck with a practical split-tailgate. Large alloy wheels and classic proportions emphasize its massive, authoritative stance.

The Rolls-Royce Phantom Drophead Coupé is a two-door, four-seat luxury convertible featuring rear-hinged coach doors and imposing, low-slung grand tourer proportions. Its front fascia is dominated by a prominent Pantheon grille and a retractable Spirit of Ecstasy, flanked by rectangular headlights. The rear features a distinctive, yacht-inspired handcrafted teakwood decking tonneau cover that is exposed when the multi-layer fabric soft-top is retracted.

The Rolls-Royce Spectre is a two-door ultra-luxury electric fastback coupe featuring wide rear-hinged coach doors and the widest illuminated Pantheon grille ever fitted to the brand. Its front fascia is defined by a modern split-headlight arrangement with slim upper daytime running lamps. In profile, it has a sweeping roofline that flows cleanly into the rear tail lights, riding on large 23-inch alloy wheels. Distinctive exterior elements include a flush-surface aerodynamic body style and the iconic Spirit of Ecstasy hood ornament.

The first-generation Rolls-Royce Wraith is a grand tourer coupe featuring a distinctive fastback roofline and rear-hinged coach doors. It has a prominent rectangular grille flanked by rectangular LED headlights and a sweeping shoulder line that runs toward the rear. The tail features integrated dual exhaust finishers and wrap-around LED tail lights, riding on large 20-inch or 21-inch alloy wheels.

The Skoda Elroq features a modern five-door medium SUV body style characterized by short overhangs and a closed-off 'Tech-Deck Face' gloss-black grille panel. It showcases split-level LED headlamps with ultra-slim upper daytime running lights, a sharply sculpted clamshell bonnet sporting prominent 'Skoda' lettering, and crisp character lines along its flanks. The rear incorporates tapered LED tail lights with crystalline graphics, a heavily raked rear window under a subtle roof spoiler, and athletic lower bumper sculpting. Alloy wheel designs range up to large aerodynamic options, while contrasting roof rails complete its rugged stance.

The Skoda Enyaq Mk1 is a five-door medium SUV featuring a modern stance with clean character lines and balanced proportions. It is characterized by an upright, signature Skoda grille flanked by sharply styled LED or Matrix LED headlights. The rear features distinctive crystalline LED tail lights, while the side profile is defined by alloy wheels ranging up to 21 inches and a gently sloping roofline that flows into a tailgate spoiler.

The Skoda Enyaq Coupé is a medium five-door electric SUV featuring a heavily raked, fastback-style sloping roofline that flows into a sharply defined rear spoiler lip. Up front, it showcases a flush "Tech-Deck Face" blanked grille flanked by angular LED Matrix headlights and a full-width lower intake. The rear is characterised by C-shaped LED tail lights connected by a subtle light element and dark lettering across the tailgate. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 20 to 21 inches, complemented by high-gloss black window surrounds and body-accents.

The Mk3 Skoda Fabia hatchback features a compact, squared-off five-door body with wide rear doors and sharp character lines along its flanks. It has a wide front grille with vertical slats flanked by angular, clean-cut headlights. The rear showcases crystal-shaped tailgate detailing and distinctive C-shaped lighting clusters. Alloy wheels and contrasting roof color options (such as black or white pillars and mirrors via 'Colour Concept' packs) were widely available.

The fourth-generation Skoda Fabia hatchback features a modern five-door body with larger, more dynamic proportions than its predecessor. The front end is defined by a wide hexagonal grille flanked by sharp, angular LED headlights with crystalline detailing. At the rear, wide horizontal tail lights extend onto the tailgate, complemented by an extended roof spoiler with aerodynamic side finlets. The profile exhibits crisp character lines, aerodynamically optimized mirrors, and contemporary alloy wheel designs.

The Škoda Kamiq Mk1 is a compact five-door crossover SUV featuring a high-riding stance and crisp character lines along its profile. The front fascia is defined by a broad hexagonal grille flanked by distinctive split-level LED headlamps, where narrow upper Daytime Running Lights flow seamlessly from the main clusters. At the rear, it features sharp C-shaped LED tail lights, a tailgate spoiler with aerodynamic finlets, and a rugged lower bumper diffuser. Alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches, silver or black roof rails, and lower body protective cladding complete its urban-focused proportions.

The first-generation Skoda Karoq is a compact five-door medium SUV featuring a structured, angular body profile with squared-off wheel arches. It is defined by a wide hexagonal radiator grille flanked by sharp, tapered LED headlights and lower bumper air intakes. The rear showcases crystalline C-shaped LED tail lights, an integrated tailgate spoiler, and a sculpted bumper. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 19 inches, with Sportline variants adding gloss black roof rails, trim accents, and body-colored body kits.

The Skoda Kodiaq Mk1 is a large, square-shouldered SUV featuring a wide, three-dimensional butterfly grille flanked by sharp, multi-element LED headlights. Its side profile is defined by a prominent character line known as the 'tornado line,' structured wheel arches, and roof rails. The rear showcases crystalline C-shaped LED tail lights and a sculpted tailgate. Alloy wheel sizes range up to 20 inches depending on the variant.

The second-generation Skoda Kodiaq is a large, five-door family SUV characterized by a longer, more aerodynamically sculpted body and softer surfacing than its predecessor. The front features a solid octagonal grille and slim split LED matrix headlights linked by a horizontal light strip, paired with a wide honeycomb air intake. In profile, it displays an elongated roofline with flat silver anodized roof rails, distinct square wheel arches, and a prominent D-pillar accent panel finished in dark or metallic styling. The rear incorporates crystalline LED tail lights spanning a clean tailgate, complemented by alloy wheel designs ranging up to 20 inches.

The third-generation Skoda Octavia liftback features a five-door, three-box sedan silhouette with a sharply angled rear tailgate that conceals a practical liftback boot. It is characterized by crisp, geometric body lines, including a prominent "tornado line" running along the flanks. Pre-2017 models feature clean, horizontal rectangular headlights flanking a butterfly grille, while the 2017 facelift introduces a controversial split-quad headlight arrangement. The rear showcases angular LED tail lights with signature C-shaped illumination patterns.

The fourth-generation Skoda Octavia liftback features a sleek, fastback-like five-door profile with a coupe-inspired roofline masking a practical tailgate. It is styled with a wide, distinctively-ribbed hexagonal front grille flanked by sharply angled, wedge-shaped LED headlights. The rear showcases crystalline LED tail lights with dynamic indicators, complemented by bold 'SKODA' lettering spelled out across the boot lid. Alloy wheel designs range up to 19 inches, maintaining a low-slung, balanced stance with clean character lines running along the flanks.

The Škoda Rapid Spaceback is a five-door hatchback featuring a wagon-like extended roofline and a coupe-like side profile defined by a sharp character line along the flanks. The front end is dominated by a distinctive vertical-slat grille with a chrome surround, flanked by angular headlamps and lower fog lights. At the rear, it features a raked tailgate with an integrated roof spoiler, C-shaped tail lights, and a horizontal bumper design. Higher specifications include a distinctive extended glass tailgate and a panoramic glass roof.

The Skoda Scala is a five-door hatchback featuring a low-slung, angular body with sharp character lines along its flanks. It has a wide, upright hexagonal grille flanked by slender, wedge-shaped LED headlights that taper toward the outer edges. The rear tailgate is distinguished by large individual letters spelling out the brand name instead of a traditional badge, stretching above wrapping LED tail lights. Alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches and an optional extended glass tailgate complete its sleek, wagon-like proportions.

The third-generation Skoda Superb liftback features a sleek, coupe-like fastback silhouette with a heavily raked roofline and a disguised dual-opening tailgate. Up front, it showcases a wide, angular chrome-surrounded grille flanked by sharp, geometric headlights with distinct crystal-line LED elements. The side profile is defined by a crisp, high "tornado line" running from the front guard through to the tail lights. At the rear, wide crystalline LED tail lights emphasize its planted stance, complemented by multi-spoke alloy wheels and clean horizontal surfacing.

The fourth-generation Skoda Superb wagon features a long, flowing estate body style with crisp character lines and an octagonal front grille flanked by slim, angular matrix LED headlights. The rear is defined by sharp, narrow wrap-around LED tail lights and a clean tailgate profile equipped with a hands-free power function. It rides on large alloy wheels up to 19 inches in diameter, complemented by gloss black exterior highlights and a sweeping roofline.

The Skoda Yeti Mk1 is a square-shouldered, 5-door compact SUV characterized by a boxy, upright greenhouse and high roofline. Early versions feature distinctive round inner fog lamps integrated directly beneath the front headlights, while post-2014 models adopt a sharper, rectangular headlight cluster alongside a wider grille. It features a flat tailgate profile flanked by C-shaped tail lights, with rugged Outdoor variants adding heavy black plastic cladding, underbody skid plates, and silver mirror caps.

The Smart #1 is a compact 5-door electric SUV characterized by smooth, flowing curves, a floating halo-style contrasting roof, and frameless windows. It features flush, retractable door handles and distinct full-width light bars connecting its slim LED headlamps and tail lamps. The stance is rounded and modern, sitting on 19-inch alloy wheels with distinct aerodynamic spoke designs.

The Smart #3 is a five-door compact coupe-SUV featuring an aerodynamic, sweeping roofline and a broad stance. It incorporates sleek CyberSparks LED headlights connected by a full-width light bar, flush-mounted concealed door handles, and frameless doors. The rear profile is dominated by a distinctive full-width LED tail light cluster with segmented elements, while the exterior roof details include a large fixed panoramic halo glass roof.

The KGM Actyon is a mid-size SUV coupé featuring a dynamic, fastback roofline paired with a broad, rugged stance and distinctive bonnet grab-handle details. Its front fascia incorporates slim LED headlights and a wide grille flanked by lighting motifs inspired by the Korean flag. The side profile rides on large 20-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels, complemented by a raked rear glass area and full-width LED tail lights, while higher grades add a panoramic glass sunroof.

The SsangYong Korando (C300) is a five-door medium SUV featuring a modern, angular stance with sharp character lines along its flanks. The front fascia is defined by a slim upper grille stretching into swept-back headlights—available with halogen or LED configurations—paired with a heavily contoured bumper housing prominent LED daytime running lights and fog lamps. At the rear, it sports angular wraparound tail lights, a roof-mounted spoiler, and a rugged lower bumper garnish. Depending on the specification, the exterior rides on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels and is accented by silver roof rails and an available power tailgate.

The SsangYong Musso Q200 is a dual-cab utility vehicle featuring a robust body-on-frame stance with a prominent, large front grille and wraparound headlights. It is offered in standard and extended (XLV) tray lengths, displaying contoured side character lines and rolling on 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels. The rear features stacked rectangular tail lights and a clean tailgate design, complemented by dark exterior accents on select variants.

The SsangYong Rexton Y400 is a large, boxy four-door SUV featuring an upright stance, strong shoulder lines, and prominent wheel arches. The front fascia is dominated by a large chrome-surrounded mesh or patterned grille flanked by sharp headlights with integrated C-type LED daytime running lights. At the rear, it features a broad tailgate with angular, horizontal tail lights and a robust lower bumper. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 18 to 20 inches and is equipped with functional roof rails and a flat roofline to maximize interior cabin space.

The SsangYong Tivoli compact SUV features a chunky, high-riding four-door body style with short overhangs and muscular rear haunches. The front end is dominated by a flat, slim upper grille flanked by angular headlights and a wider lower air intake bumper. At the rear, it has a vertical tailgate accented by angular tail lights and a subtle roof spoiler above the rear window. Exterior details include alloy wheel options up to 18 inches and a contrast or body-colored floating-roof aesthetic.

The SsangYong Tivoli XLV features a compact SUV body style with a distinctively elongated, wagon-like rear overhang designed to accommodate a significantly larger boot. Up to the C-pillar, it shares its sharp-edged styling, angular wraparound headlights, and blocky grille with the standard Tivoli, but adds an extra side window and bulkier proportions over the rear axle. Higher trim levels feature multi-spoke alloy wheels, a prominent roof spoiler, and available two-tone contrasting roof paint options.

The SsangYong Torres J100 medium SUV features a rugged, boxy five-door body style with an elevated ride height and high-gloss black A-pillars. The front end showcases a distinctive three-dimensional grille paired with slim LED headlights and integrated daytime running lights. The rear displays LED combination tail lights, a high-mounted stop light on the spoiler, and a metallic-finish skid plate, complemented by angular wheel arch mouldings and 18-inch to 20-inch alloy wheels.

The SsangYong Torres EVX is a boxy, rugged medium electric SUV featuring a smooth, blanked-off front fascia dominated by a continuous horizontal LED light bar spanning the width of the bonnet. Its main LED headlights are positioned low on the outer edges of the front bumper. In profile, it has upright proportions with a distinctive forward-sloping black C-pillar accent, squared-off wheel arches housing aerodynamic alloy wheels, and flag-style side mirrors. The rear features vertical-accented LED tail lights and a hexagonal trim element on the tailgate mimicking a spare tire casing.

The first-generation Subaru BRZ is a low-slung, two-door sports coupe featuring classic rear-wheel-drive proportions with a long hood and short rear deck. Up front, it features a wide lower trapezoidal grille flanked by teardrop-style headlights and a pair of small fender vents bearing 'BRZ' badging. The rear profile is defined by wraparound tail lights, a subtle integrated bootlid spoiler, and dual exhaust outlets. It sits on 17-inch alloy wheels, with later updates introducing revised LED lighting elements and a more aggressive front bumper aesthetic.

The ZN8 Subaru BRZ is a low-slung, two-door sports coupe featuring an aggressive front fascia with a wide lower grille and sharp, sweeping LED headlights with C-shaped daytime running light signatures. Its clean profile highlights muscular rear guards, flared fenders, and a fastback roofline flowing into an integrated ducktail rear spoiler. The rear is accented by slim, wraparound LED tail lights and dual exhaust outlets, with the stance grounded on multi-spoke 18-inch alloy wheels.

The Subaru Crosstrek compact SUV features a high-riding stance with heavy black plastic wheel arch cladding and rugged lower body molding. The front end is characterised by a hexagonal grille flanked by sharp, angled LED headlights and a muscular bumper layout. At the rear, it sports C-shaped LED tail lights framing a sculptured tailgate, complemented by factory roof rails and alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches depending on the variant.

The fourth-generation Subaru Forester (SJ) features a tall, boxy compact SUV body style with high ground clearance and expansive glasshouse visibility. Up front, it displays a hexagonal grille with a horizontal chrome bar flanked by swept-back angular headlights, while the rear showcases wraparound horizontal tail lights and an integrated roof spoiler. Profile details include prominent roof rails, flared wheel arches housing alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches, and distinct step-up body proportions.

The Subaru Forester SK features a boxy, upright compact SUV body style with four doors and a relatively flat roofline framed by roof rails. It is characterized by a prominent hexagonal grille flanked by angular, upswept LED headlights and distinct C-shaped tail lights wrapping into the tailgate. The glasshouse is expansive with large side windows and an additional fixed quarter glass panel behind the rear doors. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches, complemented by substantial black plastic wheel arch cladding and lower body molding.

The sixth-generation Subaru Forester features an athletic compact SUV body style with a muscular stance, prominent wheel arches, and an expansive glasshouse. At the front, it showcases a bold, dominant grille blending into slim, striking C-shaped LED headlights. The rear incorporates connected-style tail lights and a tailgate featuring bold 'Forester' lettering. It rides on 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels, utilizes ladder-style or low-profile roof rails depending on the variant, and maintains a high ground clearance.

The fifth-generation Subaru Impreza is available as a five-door hatchback and four-door sedan, defined by a low-slung, planted stance and athletic proportions. It features an aggressive hexagonal front grille flanked by angular, hawk-eye headlights, accompanied by C-shaped LED tail lights wrapping into the bootlid or tailgate. The exterior is characterized by sculpted body side creases, a roof-mounted shark-fin antenna, and a subtle rear spoiler on hatch variants. Depending on the specification, it rides on 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels.

The sixth-generation Subaru Impreza hatchback features a five-door layout with a lower, streamlined profile compared to its raised crossover sibling. The front end displays a prominent dark grille flanked by sleek LED headlights, while the rear showcases sharp C-shaped tail lights framing the tailgate. It rides on alloy wheels and features a clean roofline ending in an integrated rear spoiler, omitting the heavy plastic wheel-arch cladding found on SUVs.

The Subaru Levorg VM sports wagon features a low-slung, performance-oriented stance sharing structural similarities with the WRX. The front end is characterized by a prominent functional bonnet scoop, angular wraparound LED headlights, and a hexagonal mesh grille. Its profile is defined by a traditional five-door wagon silhouette with flowing rooflines, body-colored side skirts, and 18-inch alloy wheels. The rear incorporates C-shaped LED tail lights, a roof-mounted spoiler, and dual-exhaust cutouts.

The BN-generation Subaru Liberty sedan features a clean four-door body style with a structured, professional three-box profile and subtle roof curvature. The front end is defined by a hexagonal front grille flanked by sharply swept-back headlamps and C-shaped LED signature elements. The rear incorporates wraparound tail lights, a clean trunk lid design, and a balanced stance typically rolling on 18-inch alloy wheels.

The fifth-generation Subaru Outback features a rugged raised wagon body style with plastic wheel arch cladding and increased ground clearance. It has a prominent hexagonal front grille, wraparound halogen or LED headlights, and angular tail lights spanning the rear quarters. The exterior design incorporates a sloping roofline with integrated roof rails, prominent side window framing, and alloy wheels wrapped in high-profile tires.

The Subaru Outback generation BT features a rugged, raised station wagon body style with five doors and plastic body cladding around its wheel arches and lower bumpers. It has an upright front fascia with a hexagonal grille, C-shaped LED headlights, and hook-shaped C-clamp tail lights at the rear. Riding on elevated suspension with substantial ground clearance, it includes distinct roof rail configurations—such as integrated crossbars or heavy-duty ladder-style rails with accents—and 18-inch alloy wheels.

The Subaru Solterra medium electric SUV features a five-door hatchback body style with angular proportions, short overhangs, and prominent contrasting black plastic wheel arch cladding. Its front end showcases a closed-off hexagonal accent panel flanked by slim, sharp LED headlights, while the rear features a steeply raked window, distinct split-tail light elements, and a split roof spoiler design. Exterior details include aerodynamic alloy wheels (ranging from 18 to 20 inches) and an available panoramic glass roof.

The fourth-generation Subaru WRX sedan features a chiseled four-door body with an aggressive front fascia defined by hawk-eye headlights, a hexagonal grille, and a prominent functional bonnet scoop. Its profile is characterized by flared wheel arches, sharp character lines along the flanks, and multi-spoke alloy wheels. The rear end is fitted with C-shaped tail lights, a subtle boot-lid lip spoiler (or a massive raised wing on STI variants), and a lower bumper diffuser housing quad exhaust outlets.

The VB-generation Subaru WRX is offered as a four-door sedan and a five-door sportswagon, defined by angular body lines, pronounced muscular wheel arches, and controversial black plastic cladding over the guards and lower bumpers. The front end features a wide hexagonal mesh grille flanked by sharp, angular LED headlights and a prominent bonnet scoop. The sedan's rear incorporates C-shaped taillights linked by a dark trim strip and a sculpted boot lid, while the wagon features a sweeping roofline with a rear spoiler and wraparound tail lights. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches depending on the variant.

The first-generation Subaru XV features a compact five-door hatchback body style elevated by a high, rugged stance with 220mm of ground clearance. It is distinguished by heavy black plastic wheel-arch cladding, side sills, a hexagonal front grille with a chrome bar, and swept-back hawk-eye headlights. The rear is fitted with angular, wrap-around tail lights, a roof-mounted spoiler, and roof rails, riding on prominent 17-inch dark-accented alloy wheels.

The Subaru XV compact SUV features a rugged, raised stance with high ground clearance, heavy matte black wheel-arch cladding, and side sill highlights. The front fascia incorporates a low hexagonal grille flanked by sharp, hawk-eye headlights, complemented by chunky bumper styling. At the rear, it has horizontal C-shaped tail lights extending onto the tailgate, accompanied by a subtle roof spoiler. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches and features integrated roof rails across the profile.

The Suzuki APV van features a boxy, high-roof utility body style with a short, semi-forward control nose and a flat-faced profile. It is equipped with dual sliding side doors, a large rear-lifting tailgate, and high-mounted rectangular headlights flanking a simple two-slat front grille. Riding on 14-inch steel wheels with commercial tyres, the exterior is styled with utilitarian vertical body panels, wraparound bumpers, and corner-mounted vertical tail lights.

The Suzuki Baleno hatchback features a low, wide 'Liquid Flow' body style with soft, curving aerodynamic lines. It is equipped with wraparound windows, blacked-out pillars, and a chrome grille flanked by swept-back headlights that incorporate LED daytime running lights. The rear showcases a rounded tailgate with wraparound tail lights and sits on either 15-inch steel or 16-inch alloy wheels depending on the model.

The Suzuki Grand Vitara JT features an angular, compact SUV body available in 3-door short-wheelbase and 5-door long-wheelbase layouts with flared wheel arches and short overhangs. It has a distinctive front fascia with wraparound headlights and a horizontal-slat grille, complemented later by side-mirror-integrated indicators. The rear is characterized by a side-hinged tailgate carrying a full-size exposed spare wheel, and the roof features factory-fitted longitudinal rails.

The Suzuki Ignis features an ultra-compact, boxy light SUV body with five doors and a high-riding, upright stance boasting 180mm of ground clearance. Its front fascia incorporates a distinctive rectangular grille seamlessly framing circular or LED-projector headlights, complemented by a clamshell bonnet. The sides showcase flared wheel arches, black roof rails, and a C-pillar stamped with retro triple-slat styling grooves reminiscent of classic Suzuki coupes. At the rear, it has a flat tailgate flanked by wrap-around rectangular tail lights, riding on either 15-inch steel or 16-inch alloy wheels.

The third-generation Suzuki Jimny features a compact, boxy three-door body style with short overhangs and a distinctively narrow, tall stance on a ladder-frame chassis. The front fascia is characterised by round headlights flanking a vertical-slat grille and a rounded, clamshell-style bonnet. Later facelifted models introduced a prominent central bonnet scoop and updated bumper styling. At the rear, it features a side-hinged tailgate mounted with a full-size spare wheel and low-mounted vertical tail lights integrated into the bumper.

The Suzuki Jimny (JB74) features a boxy, utilitarian three-door or five-door off-road SUV body defined by flat panels, high-set proportions, and pronounced squared-off wheel arches. Its front end is characterized by a vertical slotted grille flanked by iconic round headlights and separate bumper-mounted turn signals. The rear profile is upright with a side-hinged tailgate carrying a full-sized spare wheel, complemented by rectangular tail lights embedded in the lower bumper. Exterior details include prominent rain gutters along the flat roof, exposed door hinges, and 15-inch alloy or steel wheels.

The Suzuki S-Cross (JY generation) is a five-door small SUV featuring a raised stance, black plastic wheel-arch claddings, and a flowing shoulder line. Early models featured a multi-slat chrome grille and swept-back headlights, while the 2017 facelift introduced a prominent vertical-slat chrome or piano-black grille, heavily contoured bonnet, and projector-style LED headlamps. The rear is defined by wraparound tail lights, a high-mounted bumper, and available silver roof rails alongside 17-inch alloy wheels. Higher grades included a distinctive double-sliding panoramic glass sunroof.

The third-generation Suzuki S-Cross (JYB) is a 5-door small SUV featuring a boxy, rugged stance with squared-off wheel arches clad in black plastic. It is characterized by a prominent, high-set piano-black grille flanked by slim, multi-element LED headlights, and a flat clamshell bonnet. The rear incorporates connected-style tail light assemblies and a sculpted tailgate, complemented by 17-inch alloy wheels and silver roof rails.

The FZ-generation Suzuki Swift is a compact five-door hatchback featuring an evolutionary, rounded silhouette with a distinctively high, flat roofline. It is characterized by wraparound headlamps, a low-slung trapezoidal front grille, and vertically oriented rear tail lights that stretch onto the rear shoulders. The stance is defined by short overhangs, a slightly longer wheelbase than its predecessor, and alloy or steel wheel options ranging from 15 to 17 inches depending on the variant. Sport models add an aggressive body kit, prominent rear spoiler, and unique bumper styling.

The ZC-generation Suzuki Swift is a compact five-door hatchback featuring athletic proportions with hidden rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars. It is styled with a prominent hexagonal front grille, angular wraparound headlights, and a distinctive floating roof design created by blackened pillars. The rear end is fitted with squared-off tail lights and a subtly sculpted tailgate, riding on compact alloy or steel wheel options.

The fourth-generation Suzuki Swift is a compact five-door hatchback featuring a rounded yet muscular stance with sharp shoulder creases and a clamshell bonnet. It incorporates a clamshell-style piano-black grille paired with angular LED headlights featuring distinctive L-shaped signature DRLs. Unlike older generations, it moves the rear door handles from the C-pillars down to conventional positions on the doors. The rear end is fitted with squared-off LED tail lights, and the exterior sits on either 15-inch steel wheels with covers or 16-inch alloy wheels depending on the variant.

The Suzuki Vitara (LY generation) features a compact, boxy, five-door SUV body with an upright stance and short overhangs. Its front fascia is defined by a clamshell bonnet, a pronounced horizontal-slat grille, and sharp projector-style headlights. The rear incorporates wraparound tail lights, a clean vertical tailgate, and alloy wheel options ranging up to 17 inches. Certain variants offer distinctive two-tone contrasting roof colour combinations.

The first-generation Tesla Model 3 is a four-door, fastback-style electric sedan characterized by a smooth, completely closed front fascia and teardrop-shaped LED headlights. Its low-slung, aerodynamic profile features a continuous fixed panoramic glass roof and flush door handles. The rear end is defined by curved, wrap-around horizontal tail lights integrated into the boot lid and a clean bumper lacking exhaust cutouts. It rides on alloy wheels often fitted with aerodynamic plastic covers, and features a minimalist cabin layout dominated by a large central touchscreen.

The second-generation Tesla Model 3 (facelift) is a sleek, four-door electric sedan characterized by sharper, low-profile aerodynamics. It features a simplified front fascia with smoother contours, ultra-slim wrap-around LED headlights, and a continuous panoramic glass roof. The rear showcases distinct, C-shaped wrap-around taillights integrated into a clean boot lid, complemented by flush door handles and aerodynamically optimized alloy wheels.

The Tesla Model S features a low-slung, aerodynamic 5-door liftback body style with flush door handles and a sloping roofline. Early models feature an oval faux-grille insert, which was replaced in a 2016 refresh by a cleaner, body-colored nosecone featuring a narrow upper trim bar and sleek LED headlamps. The rear showcases wraparound tail lights connected by a chrome trunk-lid strip, sitting above a smooth bumper profile.

The first-generation Tesla Model X is a large crossover SUV featuring a smooth, aerodynamically rounded profile and a full-length panoramic glass roof. Its most defining feature is the set of rear 'falcon-wing' doors that hinge upward. The front fascia is dominated by a smooth, blanked-off nose cone or minimalist body-colored grille area flanked by swept-back LED headlights. At the rear, it sports wraparound horizontal tail lights and a powered liftgate atop multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Tesla Model Y is a five-door medium crossover SUV featuring a high-riding, aerodynamic fastback silhouette with a heavily curved roofline. It features a smooth, minimalist front fascia lacking a traditional grille, flanked by swept-back LED headlights, and a continuous full-width rear light bar spanning the tailgate. The exterior sits on large alloy wheels and is defined by clean, flush body surfacing, frameless door glass, and an expansive tinted all-glass panoramic roof.

The Toyota 86 (ZN6) is a compact, low-slung two-door sports coupe featuring a sleek aerodynamic profile, a heavily raked windshield, and an aluminium bonnet. The front fascia is defined by a wide, trapezoidal lower grille and sharp headlamp clusters (incorporating HID projection originally and updated to LED units with integrated indicators in later years). At the rear, it features wraparound tail lights, a sculpted boot lid often paired with a subtle lip spoiler, and a lower bumper diffuser flanked by twin exhaust tips. Distinctive styling elements include a unique '86' piston-motif badge mounted on the front guards and multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The Toyota Aurion XV50 features a wide, aerodynamic four-door sedan body with a prominent cab-forward stance. The front end showcases angular wrap-around headlights flanking a low, aggressive chrome or mesh grille, depending on whether it is a luxury or sport-oriented trim. The rear is defined by wraparound tail lights, a clean boot lid often accented by a subtle lip spoiler on sport variants, and dual exhaust outlets. Alloy wheel designs range across trims from 16-inch multi-spoke units to larger 17- and 18-inch sport configurations.

The Toyota bZ4X (EA10) is a medium 5-door electric SUV featuring a sleek, aerodynamic profile with a bold 'hammerhead' front fascia. It incorporates distinctive contrasting wheel arch claddings, sharp body creases, and a heavily raked rear window leading into a full-width light bar tail lamp. Depending on the variant, it rides on 18-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels and features a low-slung stance with a long wheelbase.

The first-generation Toyota C-HR features a compact, coupe-like SUV body style with a heavily raked, tapering roofline and hidden rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars. Its angular, diamond-inspired geometry includes heavily sculptured body sides, flared wheel arches, and a prominent upper grille flanked by sweeping wraparound headlights. The rear is dominated by distinct, boomerang-shaped protruding LED tail lights and a high-mounted roof spoiler. Higher grades feature contrasting two-tone roof paint options and machine-finished alloy wheels.

The second-generation Toyota C-HR features a compact, high-riding stance with a sharply sculpted, coupe-like silhouette and a swooping roofline. Its front end adopts Toyota's 'hammerhead' design language, characterized by C-shaped LED headlights flanking a low, wide grille. The rear is defined by a prominent roof spoiler, angular full-width LED tail lights, and clean surfacing with flush door handles. Higher grades offer contrasting black two-tone roof treatments and 17-inch to 19-inch alloy wheels.

The Toyota Camry XV50 sedan features a distinctively angular, wedge-like body profile with pronounced shoulder lines and a flat trunk deck. The front fascia displays a wide trapezoidal lower grille and sharp, wraparound angular headlamps, with sportier Atara variants adding a mesh grille and aggressive bumper styling. At the rear, wide wraparound tail lights stretch into the boot lid, bridged by a chrome garnish bar across most trims. The exterior is completed by alloy wheel designs ranging from 16 to 18 inches and a clean, conventional roofline.

The Toyota Camry XV70 features a low-slung, four-door sedan body style with a coupe-like, tapered roofline and sharp character lines along its profile. The front end is dominated by a sweeping, aggressive grille configuration stretching low into the bumper, flanked by slim, angular LED headlamps. At the rear, the decklid features horizontal LED tail lights that wrap into the quarter panels, complemented by multi-spoke alloy wheel designs and subtle aerodynamic sculpting across the bodywork.

The Toyota Camry XV80 sedan features a dynamic four-door fastback silhouette characterised by Toyota's signature 'hammerhead' front design. It incorporates a sharp, low-slung nose with sleek C-shaped LED headlights flanking a wide lower grille, complemented by angular tail lights spanning the rear deck. The profile displays clean character lines converging towards a tapered rear roofline, sitting on alloy wheel designs ranging from 17 to 18 inches depending on the model grade.

The Toyota Coaster B40-generation bus features a conventional single-deck, boxy transit layout with large side passenger windows and an aerodynamic, rounded front fascia. It is configured with a front passenger entry door on the left side, a driver-side door, and dual rear emergency exit doors. The front end displays wraparound rectangular headlights flanking a simple horizontal grille, while tall vertical tail lights sit on the rear corners. The body rides on steel wheels, often partially covered by chrome wheel trims, and features a high-roof profile with a smooth, integrated contour over the windshield.

The Toyota Coaster B50 generation is a single-deck light bus featuring a boxy, high-roof body style with upright sides and large panoramic side windows equipped with privacy glass. The front end incorporates integrated wraparound rectangular headlights flanking a prominent grille, with the Deluxe grade uniquely styled with a sleek black panel beneath the windscreen. It utilizes a two-door configuration comprising a front driver's door and a passenger side entry door (folding on Standard, automated sliding/gliding on Deluxe), riding on 17.5-inch steel wheels. At the rear, it features stacked vertical combination tail lights framing a flat tailgate panel.

The E180 Toyota Corolla hatchback features a low, wide stance with a five-door body style and angular, wedge-like proportions. The front end showcases wraparound headlamps flanking a slim upper grille and a pronounced lower bumper aperture (with sportier variants receiving aggressive lower air dams and side skirts). At the rear, it is styled with wraparound tail light clusters, an integrated roof spoiler, and a hatch tailgate. Depending on the grade, it rides on 16-inch steel or alloy wheels up to 17-inch alloys, and features a roof-mounted shark-fin antenna.

The eleventh-generation Toyota Corolla sedan features a crisp, angular four-door body style with an extended wheelbase and a planted stance. The front fascia is defined by a sharp, chrome-accented horizontal upper grille that flows seamlessly into narrow, wrap-around headlamps. At the rear, wide, wraparound tail lights are connected by a prominent chrome trunk garnish. It rides on either 15-inch steel wheels or alloy wheel options ranging from 15 to 17 inches depending on the grade, complemented by clean character lines along the profile.

The E210 Toyota Corolla hatchback features a dynamic, athletic five-door body with a low-slung stance and a steeply raked rear window. Its aggressive front fascia showcases a large lower honeycomb grille flanked by sharp, wrap-around LED headlights. The sculpted profile highlights muscular rear haunches, a distinct roof spoiler, and wraparound LED tail lights connected across the tailgate. Alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches complement its planted, modern proportions.

The Toyota Corolla Cross (XG10) features a traditional five-door medium SUV body style with a raised stance, black lower-body cladding, and flared wheel arches. It incorporates a trapezoidal front grille paired with swept-back LED headlights, complemented by wrap-around tail lights at the rear. Depending on the specification, exterior appointments include 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels, roof rails, and an available panoramic glass roof.

The Toyota Fortuner AN160 is a rugged, high-riding five-door large SUV featuring a robust ladder-frame stance with flared wheel arches. It is characterized by a prominent front grille, swept-back LED headlamps, and a chunky bumper assembly with a skid-plate design. The side profile reveals a floating roof effect created by darkened D-pillars, topped with a shark-fin antenna, while the rear features wraparound horizontal tail lights.

The Toyota GR Corolla (E210) is a muscular five-door performance hatchback featuring dramatically flared front and rear guards that create an aggressive, wide-body stance. The front end showcases a large matrix-mesh grille flanked by sharp LED headlamps and deep functional air ducts, complemented by a vented aluminum bonnet. At the rear, it features a pronounced roof spoiler, slim LED tail lamps connected by a subtle light strip, and a distinctive triple-exit exhaust system. Riding on 18-inch alloy wheels housing red-painted brake calipers, variants like the Morizo Edition also feature a lightweight carbon-fibre reinforced polymer roof.

The Toyota GR Yaris is a stubby three-door performance hatchback featuring a wide, aggressive stance with flared wheel arches and a heavily raked, lower carbon-composite roofline.
