It features a massive lower front grille air intake flanked by angular LED headlights and side vents, a muscular rear hatch topped with a prominent roof spoiler, and dual exhaust tips. Depending on the variant, it rides on lightweight 18-inch alloy or forged BBS wheels housing distinct multi-piston brake callipers.

The Toyota GR86 sports coupe features a low-slung, fastback profile with a two-door configuration, defined by athletic proportions and a wide stance. The front fascia is highlighted by an aggressive 'G-mesh' grille, functional side air vents behind the front wheels, and sharply angled LED projector headlights. The rear incorporates a pronounced ducktail spoiler integrated into the boot lid, C-shaped LED tail lights joined by a dark accent strip, and dual exhaust tips. It rides on alloy wheels ranging up to 18 inches and features aerodynamic venting elements across its side sills and wheel arches.

The Toyota Granvia H300 features a semi-bonneted, boxy people-mover body style with an imposing length of 5.3 metres, dual sliding side doors, and a tall roofline. Its front fascia is highlighted by a prominent, chrome-heavy grille and sharp wraparound LED headlights with integrated daytime running lights. The rear showcases large, distinctive 'L-shaped' tail lights flanking a flat tailgate. It rides on 17-inch alloy wheels and features expansive side glass windows for the passenger cabin.

The fifth-generation Toyota HiAce van features a distinctive cab-over, flat-nose body design with a near-vertical front fascia and a short overhang. It is characterised by large, wraparound angular headlights flanking a prominent front grille, sliding side doors, and a high, flat roofline available in standard or long-wheelbase high-roof configurations. The rear is fitted with vertical stack tail lights flanking a wide-opening tailgate or dual barn doors.

The H300 generation Toyota HiAce van features a distinct semi-bonneted 'snub-nose' front layout rather than a traditional flat-face design. It comes in long-wheelbase (LWB) and super-long-wheelbase (SLWB) body styles equipped with sliding side doors and a choice of a lift-up tailgate or dual barn-style rear doors. The front end is characterized by a prominent chrome or dark accent grille flanked by swept-back angular headlights, paired with wraparound tail lights at the rear. It rides on 16-inch steel or alloy wheels and features an extended, boxy cargo profile.

The eighth-generation Toyota HiLux features a utility body style available in single cab, extra cab, and double cab configurations, as well as cab-chassis layouts. It exhibits a prominent stance with swept-back projector or LED headlights framing a trapezoidal grille that evolved through several facelifts to include more muscular, interlocking bumper designs. The profile is defined by high beltlines, flared wheel arches, and rolling stock ranging from 16-inch steel wheels on base work variants to 17- or 18-inch alloy wheels on higher grades. The rear features vertical tail light clusters flanking a drop-down tailgate, complemented on higher specification variants by sports bars and robust tub liners.

The third-generation Toyota Kluger is a large, five-door seven-seat SUV featuring an aggressive, trapezoidal front grille flanked by wraparound headlights. Its side profile is defined by flared wheel arches, subtle body sculpting, and a tapering glasshouse, riding on either 18-inch or 19-inch alloy wheels. The rear showcases a broad tailgate design with wraparound tail lights and a dark lower bumper diffuser.

The fourth-generation Toyota Kluger is a large, five-door seven-seat SUV featuring a curvy, aerodynamic silhouette with pronounced rear haunches wrapping into the tailgate. The front fascia displays slim, angular blade-style headlamps flanking a trapezoidal, mesh-pattern grille with a distinctive horizontal upper bar bearing the Toyota emblem. Depending on the grade, it rides on either 18-inch alloy wheels or larger 20-inch chrome-effect rims. The rear incorporates wraparound LED tail lights, a roof spoiler, and a clean, sculpted tailgate design.

The Toyota LandCruiser J70 features a boxy, utilitarian body-on-frame silhouette available as a single-cab/double-cab utility, long-wheelbase Troop Carrier, or four-door wagon. It is defined by flat body panels, a high-set stance with prominent live-axle proportions, and upright glass. Up front, it showcases a blunt, flat face featuring a mesh or horizontal-slat grille flanked by circular or rectangular headlights, which transition into retro-styled cowled housings on later updates. The rear exhibits vertical tail lights integrated into the lower corners or bumper structure, complemented by external details like a snorkel, steel or split-rim wheels, and a guttered roofline designed for heavy-duty off-road use.

The Toyota LandCruiser J200 is a large, square-shouldered five-door SUV featuring a commanding stance with prominent wheel arches and high ground clearance. Its broad front fascia is dominated by a substantial horizontal chrome grille flanked by wraparound headlight clusters. The rear profile incorporates a practical two-piece split tailgate and horizontal tail lights. It rides on robust alloy wheels (ranging from 17 to 20 inches depending on the grade) and features a flat roofline often equipped with integrated rails.

The Toyota LandCruiser J300 is a large, 5-door body-on-frame station wagon featuring a high-riding, muscular stance with squared-off wheel arches and a flat bonnet. Its front end is dominated by a massive, commanding grille—either horizontal slats or a bold mesh design depending on the variant—flanked by sleek, wrap-around LED headlamps. The rear showcases wraparound tail lights, a practical split-opening or powered tailgate, and clean sheet-metal surfacing along the flanks. Depending on the specification, it rides on wheel sizes ranging from 17-inch steel or alloy wheels up to 20-inch luxury alloys, with some grades offering unique black exterior detailing and distinctive off-road bumpers.

The Toyota LandCruiser Prado J150 is a tall, rugged five-door large SUV featuring a muscular, high-riding stance with flared wheel arches and distinct body-on-frame proportions. Up front, it features a prominent vertical or horizontal slat grille flanked by swept-back headlights, which shifted from a stepped lower edge to sleeker, integrated LED clusters through subsequent updates. At the rear, it is defined by a side-hinged tailgate—often housing a rear-mounted spare wheel on lower specifications or a clean panel with a separate opening glass window on higher grades—complemented by stacked vertical tail lights. Depending on the model tier, it rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches, and features a flat roofline typically fitted with roof rails.

The Toyota LandCruiser Prado J250 features a boxy, squared-off large SUV body style with upright pillars and muscular proportions. It showcases a flat, prominent front fascia with a rectangular grille housing heritage 'TOYOTA' lettering, flanked by horizontal or round LED headlights depending on the grade. The rear features high-mounted vertical tail light clusters and a tailgate equipped with a convenient opening glass window. Depending on the variant, it rides on 18-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels, and higher trims include roof rails and a panoramic moonroof.

The fourth-generation Toyota Prius is a five-door liftback featuring a low-slung, wedge-like silhouette and an angular, aerodynamic body. The front end is characterized by sharp, swept-back LED headlamps and complex lower bumper creases integrating vertical daytime running lights. At the rear, it sports distinctive, sharply-hooked vertical tail lights that extend down the corners of the tailgate alongside an integrated rear spoiler. It rides on alloy wheels (15-inch with aero covers or 17-inch) beneath a heavily raked windshield and sloping roofline.

The Toyota Prius c light hatchback features a compact, wedge-like five-door body profile with an ascending character line along the sides and a roof spoiler over the tailgate. It is characterized by an aggressive lower front bumper design integrating a prominent hexagonal grille flanked by angular headlamps. The rear is defined by vertical LED tail lights framing the tailgate, while rolling on 15-inch steel wheels with covers or multi-spoke alloy wheels depending on the model grade.

The Toyota Prius v features a five-door wagon body style with a prolonged, aerodynamic wedge silhouette and an elongated roofline designed to maximize interior space. It has a low-set front bumper with integrated LED daytime running lights, sweeping angular headlights, and a narrow upper grille opening. The rear profile is upright and squared-off with a wide tailgate and vertical tail light clusters. It rides on 16-inch alloy wheels and incorporates a large, raked windshield paired with a flat, extended roof for increased cabin headroom.

The fourth-generation Toyota RAV4 features a medium five-door SUV body with angular proportions and a rising beltline. Its front fascia incorporates a slim upper grille connecting swept-back wraparound headlights above a prominent lower bumper opening. At the rear, the tailgate opens upward rather than sideways, as the spare tire was relocated underneath the boot floor. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches and features an integrated roof spoiler.

The Toyota RAV4 XA50 features an angular, rugged medium SUV body style with pronounced, square wheel arches and heavy black plastic cladding. The front end is dominated by a trapezoidal grille and sharp, multi-faceted LED headlights, complemented by a chiseled side profile and geometric character lines. The rear features wrap-around tail lights joined by a horizontal accent strip, a roof-mounted spoiler, and alloy wheel sizes ranging from 17 to 19 inches depending on the variant.

The A90 Toyota Supra is a low-slung, two-door sports coupe featuring a distinct 'double-bubble' roof and an aggressive, long-bonnet short-deck proportion. Its front fascia is defined by a prominent, blunt nose cone with wide lower air intakes and swept-back LED headlights, complemented by a raised integrated ducktail spoiler at the rear. It rides on 19-inch forged alloy wheels and exhibits heavily sculpted, muscular rear haunches alongside sleek, tapered tail lights.

The XR50-generation Toyota Tarago features a sleek, aerodynamic people-mover body with a distinctive wedge-like silhouette and an expansive glasshouse. It is equipped with dual sliding side doors and an upright tailgate. The front end showcases swept-back headlamps flanking a low-set horizontal grille, while the rear features wraparound tail lights extending into the quarter panels. Depending on the model grade, it rides on 16-inch or 17-inch alloy wheels, and higher variants include roof-mounted details such as a dual moonroof configuration.

The third-generation XP130 Toyota Yaris hatchback features a compact, wedge-like body profile initially offered in both 3-door and 5-door variants (transitioning to 5-door only). Its front end is defined by a prominent, large lower grille opening and angular, swept-back headlamps, which were significantly sharpened during mid-cycle facelifts with wider bumper accents. The rear features a practical flat tailgate topped by a subtle roof spoiler and horizontal or wraparound tail lights. Exterior details include short overhangs, clean side character lines, and standard steel or alloy wheels depending on the trim grade.

The fourth-generation Toyota Yaris hatchback features a compact, aggressive stance with a short rear overhang, a long bonnet, and pronounced, muscular haunches over the rear wheels. The front fascia is dominated by a large, low-slung cascading grille flanked by sharp, angled headlamps and integrated daytime running lights. At the rear, the tailgate features a distinct full-width light bar aesthetic connecting angular tail lamp clusters, complemented by a roof spoiler. Higher grades ride on alloy wheels (15-inch or 16-inch) and offer distinctive two-tone paint configurations with a contrasting black roof.

The Toyota Yaris Cross features a high-riding, 5-door compact SUV body style with heavily flared, squared-off wheel arches and a stubby stance. The front end displays a wide lower intake paired with a slim upper grille flanked by angular headlights, while the rear showcases a prominent roof spoiler and a continuous LED light bar running across the tailgate. Higher grades sit on larger 18-inch alloy wheels and offer contrasting black or white floating roof treatments.

The first-generation Volkswagen Amarok dual-cab ute features a rugged yet car-like stance with clean, horizontal body lines and squared-off wheel arches. Its front end is defined by a rectangular grille integrating horizontal louvres that flow directly into rectangular, angular headlights. The rear exhibits vertical, stacked tail lights framing a drop-down tailgate stamped with the prominent Volkswagen logo. Depending on the spec, exterior details include alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 19 inches, optional side steps, and a stainless steel sports bar over the tub.

The second-generation Volkswagen Amarok is a four-door dual-cab ute featuring a muscular stance with prominent, squared-off wheel arches. The front fascia is dominated by a distinctive upper grille layout that transitions into C-clamp or X-design framing depending on the variant, flanked by slim, angular LED matrix headlights. At the rear, it features C-shaped LED tail lights and bold 'AMAROK' lettering stamped across the tailgate. Exterior details include varying alloy wheel designs up to 21 inches, integrated roof rails, and utility-focused options like sports bars or sailplanes.

The Volkswagen Arteon fastback features a sleek, low-slung four-door silhouette with a sweeping coupe-like roofline and a liftback tailgate. Its wide front fascia showcases a prominent multi-bar chrome grille that merges smoothly into sharp LED headlights, complemented by a continuous light strip on updated models. The profile is defined by frameless door windows and clean character lines running along the flanks down to large alloy wheels. At the rear, it is equipped with slim, angular 3D-effect LED tail lights and a sculpted decklid.

The A5 Volkswagen Beetle features a distinctive, low-profile silhouette with a flattened, elongated roofline and pronounced rounded wheel arches. Available as a 3-door hatchback and a 2-door convertible with a power-operated soft top, it showcases circular headlights flanking a pinched, upright grille and a horizontal lower intake. The rear incorporates rounded tail lights and a clean tailgate design, sitting on alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches depending on the specification.

The Mk3 Volkswagen Caddy panel van features a boxy, high-roof utility body style with short-wheelbase and extended Maxi configurations. It is characterized by a sloping front bonnet that flows into a raked windscreen, rectangular multi-reflector headlights flanking a simple horizontal-slat grille, and vertical, rectangular tail lights positioned flush against the high-opening rear barn doors. Side profiles are defined by a practical sliding side cargo door and flat panel sides, riding on steel wheels with utilitarian black or silver detailing.

The fifth-generation Volkswagen Caddy panel van features an aerodynamic, passenger-car-inspired body style built on the MQB platform, available in short-wheelbase and extended Maxi lengths with side sliding doors. It showcases a sharp front fascia with a sleek lower grille incorporating a honeycomb structure, flanked by swept-back angular headlights and integrated daytime running lights. The rear is defined by distinctive, tall vertical LED tail lights framing an asymmetric split tailgate or liftback. Exterior styling details include clean shoulder lines, steel or alloy wheels ranging from 16 to 18 inches, and optional roof rails.

The Volkswagen Caravelle T6/T6.1 features a boxy, utilitarian van body style with dual sliding side doors and a top-hinged tailgate. It features a flat roofline, a commanding upright driving stance, and an extended wheelbase proportion. The front end is characterized by a horizontal slatted grille integrated with rectangular headlights (incorporating LED signatures on the T6.1 facelift), while the rear showcases wraparound tail lights and alloy wheels.

The Volkswagen CC features a low-slung, four-door fastback sedan body style with a sweeping, coupe-like roofline, frameless door glass, and a pronounced shoulder line. It has a wide stance with a multi-slat chrome grille flanked by sleek bi-xenon headlights (incorporating LED daytime running lights). The rear end is defined by elongated horizontal LED tail lights and a cleanly integrated boot spoiler. The exterior is finished with chrome window surrounds, sculpted lower sills, and multi-spoke alloy wheels.

The first-generation Volkswagen Crafter features a large, utilitarian commercial van body sharing its foundational architecture with the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter. It is characterized by an upright front fascia sporting a prominent V-shaped chrome-slatted grille and large, swept-back trapezoidal headlights. The rear profile is dominated by high-mounted vertical tail lights flanking wide-opening split barn doors. Side details include a prominent side-sliding loading door, boxy high-roof height options, and steel wheels.

The second-generation Volkswagen Crafter is a large commercial van featuring a boxy, aerodynamic silhouette with a slab-sided profile and a prominent front grille sporting horizontal slats and the central VW badge. It is flanked by angular, horizontally swept headlights and available with high or super-high roof configurations. The rear is fitted with vertically stacked, rectangular tail lights and wide-opening asymmetrical barn doors, while the side provides a massive sliding access door.

The Volkswagen Golf Mk7 hatchback features a sharp, angular five-door body with a long bonnet, a heavily raked C-pillar, and a low-slung, planted stance. It is defined by a wide horizontal grille that flows directly into angular, multi-faceted headlights, complemented by a low front bumper intake. The rear showcases geometric LED tail lights with distinct L-shaped signatures and a sculpted tailgate. Riding on various alloy wheel designs depending on the variant, the silhouette emphasizes clean character lines running along the flanks and wheel arches.

The Volkswagen Golf Mk8 hatchback features a five-door layout with a low, aerodynamic stance, clean shoulder lines, and signature thick C-pillars. It is styled with a slim upper grille framing a flat VW badge, flanked by sharply tapered, narrow LED headlights. The front fascia is dominated by a deep, expansive lower bumper air intake. At the rear, it has angular LED tail lights, a clean tailgate centred with the model name, and an integrated roof spoiler.

The Volkswagen ID. Buzz features a retro-inspired electric van body style with short overhangs, a stubby snout, and optional two-tone paint configurations. It is equipped with sleek LED matrix headlights connected by an illuminated light bar flanking a prominent front-center VW badge, sliding side doors, and a flat-faced tailgate with a full-width rear light strip. The profile is characterized by large alloy wheels (ranging from 18 to 21 inches) and a distinctive D-pillar featuring louvered detailing that nods to the classic T1 Kombi.

The Volkswagen ID.4 is a five-door medium electric SUV featuring a smooth, aerodynamic silhouette with short overhangs and a raked rear windscreen. The front end is characterized by a closed-off grille area and swept-back IQ.LIGHT Matrix LED headlights connected by an optional illuminated light bar. At the rear, horizontal LED tail lights span the width of the tailgate. It rides on large alloy wheels ranging from 19 to 21 inches and comes equipped with standard roof rails and flush, aerodynamic door handles.

The Volkswagen ID.5 features a five-door electric coupe-SUV body style characterized by a sweeping, fastback roofline and a pronounced rear spoiler. It showcases a smooth front fascia with IQ.LIGHT matrix LED headlights linked by a light bar, a closed-off lower grille, and a contemporary stance riding on large alloy wheels. The rear is defined by a full-width LED tail-light strip and clean, minimalist surfacing across the tailgate. Gloss black exterior accents and a fixed panoramic glass roof further accentuate its aerodynamic silhouette.

The Volkswagen Jetta Mk6 is a four-door sedan featuring a clean, three-box silhouette with a stretched wheelbase and sharp character lines along the flanks. The front end showcases a horizontal multi-slat chrome grille flanked by angular, trapezoidal headlights, while the rear features wraparound rectangular tail lights and a subtly integrated boot-lid spoiler. Its profile is defined by defined wheel arches, a flat roofline, and alloy wheel options ranging from 16 to 17 inches depending on the specification.

The Volkswagen Multivan T6 and T6.1 feature a boxy, utilitarian people mover silhouette with a flat roofline and short or long wheelbase options. The front fascia is defined by a wide horizontal grille accented with chrome strips, flanked by angular rectangular headlights utilizing halogen or LED technology. Along the sides, it incorporates dual sliding doors, large flush glass areas, and alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 18 inches. The rear is distinguished by a high-opening vertical tailgate with an integrated window wiper and rectangular LED tail lights.

The Volkswagen Passat B8 is offered in four-door sedan and five-door wagon (Variant) body styles with a low, wide stance, short overhangs, and a long wheelbase. Its front fascia features a slim, multi-bar chrome grille that flows seamlessly into angular, sharp-edged LED headlights. A crisp, prominent shoulder line cuts horizontally across the side profile, passing directly through the door handles to link the front and rear light clusters. The rear is defined by horizontally oriented LED tail lights featuring distinctive dual-strip lighting signatures, complemented by various multi-spoke alloy wheel designs.

The Mk5 Volkswagen Polo hatchback features a compact, squared-off body with clean horizontal character lines and a low-slung, planted stance. The front fascia is defined by a narrow, horizontal upper grille flanked by angular, upswept headlights, sitting above a wider lower air intake. In profile, it has short overhangs, a sharply raked windshield, and a distinct shoulder line running into squared tail lights positioned high on the rear corners. The rear features a subtle roof spoiler, a flat tailgate, and simple alloy wheel options.

The sixth-generation Volkswagen Polo is a five-door light hatchback featuring crisp, horizontal body lines and shorter overhangs. It features a sharp, low-profile grille flowing into angular headlights—upgraded to LED units across the range and available with matrix technology on higher grades. The rear showcases wide, angular tail lights that wrap into the tailgate, alongside clean bumper sculpting and alloy wheel designs ranging up to sporty 17-inch rims on the GTI variant.

The Volkswagen T-Cross is a five-door light SUV featuring a boxy, upright stance with short overhangs and a high waistline. The front end showcases a wide radiator grille flanked by LED headlights, complemented on higher grades by an illuminated light bar and matrix clusters. The rear features angular tail lights connected by a reflective trim panel across the tailgate, while wheel sizes range from 16-inch to 18-inch alloy designs depending on the variant.

The first-generation Volkswagen T-Roc features a compact, muscular five-door SUV stance with angular body lines and prominent wheel arches. The front end is characterized by a wide hexagonal grille merging into sharp LED headlights, complemented by distinctive hexagonal LED daytime running lights set low in the bumper. At the rear, it sports wraparound LED tail lights, a raked rear window, and a chunky bumper layout. Depending on the variant, it often includes contrasting roof paint and rides on 17-inch to 19-inch alloy wheels.

The second-generation Volkswagen Tiguan features a squared-off, angular five-door medium SUV body with sharp horizontal character lines along its profile. The front end showcases a wide horizontal grille seamlessly integrated with sharp LED headlights, while the rear incorporates angular LED tail lights and a sculpted tailgate with centrally placed model lettering. It rides on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 20 inches, sporting clean roof rails and a distinctively planted, low-slung stance for an SUV.

The third-generation Volkswagen Tiguan features a smoother, more aerodynamic medium SUV body style with soft, flowing character lines and a pronounced stance. The front fascia is dominated by a sweeping upper grille structure flanked by sleek, narrow LED headlights that can be joined by an optional horizontal light bar. The rear showcases a contemporary look defined by wraparound connected LED tail-lights spanning the tailgate width. It rides on prominent alloy wheels (ranging up to large diameter options depending on the spec) and incorporates a sculpted rear roof spoiler.

The second-generation Volkswagen Touareg features a streamlined, large 5-door SUV body with softer, flowing lines compared to its predecessor. At the front, it showcases a multi-slat horizontal chrome grille flanked by angular headlamps with integrated LED daytime running lights. The rear incorporates wrap-around tail lights, a subtle tailgate crease line, and a lower diffuser. Higher grades like the R-Line add sporty body-kit styling, side sill extensions, and large alloy wheels ranging up to 21 inches.

The third-generation Volkswagen Touareg is a large, wide SUV defined by bold, muscular proportions and sharp character lines. Its wide front grille merges seamlessly with sophisticated LED or HD matrix headlamps, complemented by a prominent bumper with large lower air intakes. The profile features a sweeping roofline, optional panoramic sunroof, and distinct alloy wheel designs ranging up to 21 inches. At the rear, it sports wraparound LED tail lights connected by a continuous light bar incorporating an illuminated Volkswagen badge.

The Volkswagen Transporter T6 and T6.1 feature a boxy, utilitarian commercial van body available in short- and long-wheelbase configurations with a side sliding door and rear tailgate or barn doors. The front fascia is defined by a rectangular multi-slat chrome-accented grille flanked by angular halogen or LED headlights, which transition into a sharper, full-width lower intake design on the later T6.1 facelift. It rides on steel wheels and features utilitarian unpainted or grey bumpers on standard trims, flat body sides, and a high roofline.

The Volkswagen Transporter T7 features an aerodynamic commercial van body with a more rounded, forward-stretching nose and a wider stance than its predecessor. It is styled with a distinctive low-profile horizontal front grille flanked by sleek, modern LED headlights. The side profile highlights clean character lines, sliding side doors, and robust alloy or steel wheel options paired with short- or long-wheelbase configurations. At the rear, it features crisp tailgate or barn-door surfacing complemented by vertical tail light clusters.

The Volvo EX30 is a compact, five-door electric SUV featuring a short, athletic stance with minimal overhangs and flush door handles. The front showcases a modern, closed-off shield grille paired with a contemporary iteration of the brand's 'Thor's Hammer' digital LED headlight signature. At the rear, it has distinctive split tail lights with upper sections flanking the rear windscreen and lower C-shaped clusters built into the bumper. It rides on large aerodynamic alloy wheels (typically 19-inch or 20-inch diamond-cut styles) and is styled with a contrasting high-gloss black roof and pillar treatment on higher trim levels.

The P3 Volvo S60 sedan features a four-door coupe-inspired profile with a sweeping, fastback-style roofline and a pronounced double-wave shoulder line running from the front headlamps to the rear tail lamps. The front end is characterized by a low, wide stance, an angled grille featuring the diagonal Volvo iron mark, and swept-back headlamps that flank a sharply sculpted bonnet. At the rear, it sports wraparound tail lights that curve into the C-pillars, a short boot lid, and dual exhaust finishers. Depending on the variant, it rides on multi-spoke alloy wheels (ranging up to 18-inch or larger performance options) and includes athletic body kits on R-Design trims.

The third-generation Volvo S60 sedan features a low-slung, athletic four-door profile with clean, taut body lines and a planted stance. The front fascia is defined by a concave grille flanked by distinctive LED headlights featuring 'Thor's Hammer' signature daytime running lights. At the rear, it sports C-shaped LED tail lights that wrap onto the boot lid alongside dual exhaust outlets. It rides on large alloy wheels up to 19 inches, complemented by short front and rear overhangs characteristic of its rear-biased platform proportions.

The Volvo V40 P1 generation is a compact five-door hatchback featuring a low-slung, dynamic stance with a coupe-like sloping roofline. It features a prominent rectangular grille flanked by swept-back headlamps, which transitioned to signature 'Thor's Hammer' LED units during its 2016 facelift. The rear is characterised by wraparound tail lights that climb vertically alongside the rear glass hatch and a sculpted bumper finish.

The P3-generation Volvo V60 is a five-door station wagon featuring a low-slung, coupe-like sloping roofline and a heavily sculpted, wedge-shaped body profile. It is fronted by an angular rectangular grille flanked by swept-back, wraparound headlamps, and a sportily contoured front bumper. The rear showcases trademark vertical LED tail lights that trace the outer edges of the tailgate and taper upwards around the D-pillars. It sits on alloy wheels ranging from 17 to 19 inches, featuring integrated roof rails and a distinctively curvaceous rear haunch.

The Volvo V60 station wagon features a sleek, elongated two-box silhouette with a low-slung stance and prominent shoulder lines. It is fronted by a concave grille flanked by distinctive 'Thor's Hammer' LED headlights. The rear showcases sweeping, C-shaped vertical tail lights that extend onto the tailgate. It rides on large alloy wheels beneath clean, sculpted body panels and an integrated roof spoiler.

The Volvo XC40 is a compact, five-door luxury SUV characterized by a boxy, upright stance, short overhangs, and a nearly horizontal roofline often paired with a contrasting black roof. It features a prominent vertical grille crossed by Volvo's diagonal slash, flanked by signature 'Thor's Hammer' LED headlights. The rear is defined by vertical, pillar-mounted LED taillights and a clean tailgate design. Rugged aesthetic touches include black wheel arch cladding and sculpted lower doors, riding on various alloy wheel designs ranging up to 20 inches.

The first-generation Volvo XC60 features a muscular, coupe-inspired crossover SUV body style with a sloping roofline and pronounced, curvaceous rear shoulders. It has a prominent upright front grille centered with the Volvo iron mark, flanked by swept-back headlights that were streamlined into a single-piece unit during the 2013 facelift. The rear is defined by signature, elongated vertical tail lamps that trace the contour of the broad shoulders. Profile details include prominent wheel arches housing large alloy wheels, flush-fitting side windows, and integrated roof rails.

The Volvo XC60 SPA generation features a sleek, medium-sized five-door SUV body with balanced proportions and a confident stance. The front end is defined by a concave vertical-slat grille carrying Volvo's iconic iron mark, flanked by distinctive 'Thor’s Hammer' LED headlights. At the rear, it sports signature vertical, L-shaped LED tail lights that wrap onto the shoulders of the tailgate. The profile is clean with a subtly sloped roofline, clean surfacing, and large alloy wheel options ranging up to 21 or 22 inches.

The Volvo XC90 SPA generation is a large 5-door luxury SUV characterized by a stately, upright stance, a long wheelbase, and balanced proportions. The front end features a prominent rectangular grille flanked by signature 'Thor's Hammer' LED headlights and a sculpted bonnet. The rear showcases distinctive vertical tail lights extending up the D-pillars, complemented by a clean, flat tailgate. Exterior detailing ranges from bright chrome accents to high-gloss black packages, riding on large 20-inch to 22-inch alloy wheels alongside a panoramic glass sunroof on select variants.

The Zeekr 009 is a large, boxy luxury people mover featuring a commanding, flat-faced front profile dominated by a massive, illuminated intelligent grille and sleek vertical daytime running lights. It has a blocky silhouette with hidden dual A-pillars, large curved side glass, sliding rear doors, and a dual glass roof with power shades. The rear is defined by a vertical tailgate layout stretching a wide 1.47-meter integrated LED light bar, complemented by aero-style alloy wheels.

The first-generation Zeekr 7X is a medium-to-large 5-door electric SUV featuring a sleek, aerodynamic profile with a distinctive clamshell bonnet and frameless doors. Its front fascia is highlighted by a continuous light bar integrating slim LED headlamps, while the rear showcases a clean, minimalist full-width tail-light signature. The body exhibits an athletic stance with flush door handles and clean surfacing, riding on either 19-inch alloy wheels or large 21-inch forged wheels depending on the variant. A panoramic glass roof spans overhead, complementing its modern proportions.

The Zeekr X is a 5-door compact electric SUV featuring a low-slung stance, sharp body creases, and a high shoulder line. It is characterized by distinct double-edged LED daytime running lights, a smooth enclosed front fascia, and a full-width organic glass rear light bar. Details include frameless side mirrors, flush door handles, a contrasting black roof option, and large 19-inch or 20-inch alloy wheels.
